title: Adept Thaumaturgy > A Magical Box
text:
Quest: A Magical Box
Quest line: Adept Thaumaturgy

I can use dyes on the top of the box to assign its location, and any box with the same colors will share the same space. Using a diamond on the box locks it to me, and me alone.

Shift-right-clicking will remove the diamond and the chest will rejoin the public network.

title: Adept Thaumaturgy > A Magical Tank
text:
Quest: A Magical Tank
Quest line: Adept Thaumaturgy

This tank always seems to connect to the same dimensional space. I can push fluids into the tank in one dimension, and retrieve them in a totally different dimension!

I have discovered a way to assign a location to each tank using dyes applied to the top. Using a diamond makes the tank private, attuned to the user's mind, and will not share fluids with any other player's tanks.

Shift-right-clicking recovers the diamond and makes the tank part of the public tank network again.

The dial on the front controls the input/output of the tank. When blue is up, the tank accepts fluids. When orange is up, the tank will eject fluids.

If you get FPS problems from large numbers of them, try the setting in the config to turn off the fancy render at the bottom.

title: Adept Thaumaturgy > A Travel Companion
text:
Quest: A Travel Companion
Quest line: Adept Thaumaturgy

Lonely? The Traveling Trunk is a simple companion, giving you some extra space. With upgrades (one per trunk) it can offer you some nice advantages. Like other golems, you can pick it up with the Golemancer's Bell. Its brain is pretty small though, so it can easily get stuck. You can order it to stay in one spot via the GUI. It will attempt to teleport to you, as long as the chunk is still loaded. It can also follow you into different dimensions.

They will heal slowly on their own, or faster if you right-click on them with any food, including rotten meat. Keep away from lava.

Golem upgrade effects:
Aer: Moves faster
Earth: 1 more row of item slots
Fire: Attacks hostile mobs, setting them on fire
Water: Nearly invulnerable. In SMP, can only be opened or picked up by player who placed it.
Entropy: Sucks in loose items nearby if it has room
Order: Can be picked up with its contents, and nested in other inventories. Don't be stupid about this.

Tasks:
- Retrieve: Traveling Trunk
Rewards: Uncommon Treasure; enhancedlootbags:lootbag:10; choose one of: Golem Upgrade: Air; Golem Upgrade: Earth; Golem Upgrade: Fire; Golem Upgrade: Water; Golem Upgrade: Order; Golem Upgrade: Entropy

title: Adept Thaumaturgy > Dynamism Tablets
text:
Quest: Dynamism Tablets
Quest line: Adept Thaumaturgy

The Dynamism tablet is a block that simulates the functionality of a left and right-click autoclicker. It can be obtained fairly early in the game (early-mid MV), and is a useful tool for simple automation.

Upon placing, the tablet will target the block that it's facing (the direction is indicated by a small dot on the overlay) and will start once you give it an item in its slot. If it holds a block/seed/sapling, it can also place it on the block below it.

It can be configured to either left/right click and also has an option to only be active when it receives a redstone signal. Hoppers or item pipes of any sort also allow the tablet to receive items.

Note that some special mob drops or special interactions (like BM sacrificial knife) are disabled for the Dynamism tablet. However, they do work with Tinkers Tools.

This item has received a rework in 2.8 and has had most of its bugs fixed. If you still encounter any bugs, feel free to report it on our GitHub page or discord server.

title: Adept Thaumaturgy > Infused Seeds
text:
Quest: Infused Seeds
Quest line: Adept Thaumaturgy

Infused Seeds are very slow growing magical crops. Each seed is associated with a Thaumcraft aspect, and a fully grown plant can produce resources related to that aspect. Some of these drops are surprisingly useful. For example, a fully grown Venenum Infused Seed will drop 16 Quicksilver, an Iter Infused Seed will drop Arcane Bricks, and a Herba Infused Seed will give you random saplings.

You can see the products of different seeds using NEI.

There is a catch: the Infusion Altar can only directly create seeds for the six primal aspects. To create seeds for compound aspects, you'll need to combine their component aspects through the farmland itself.

Let's make a Venenum Infused Seed as an example. Venenum is composed of Aqua + Perditio, so begin by crafting both an Aqua Infused Seed and a Perditio Infused Seed.

Plant the Aqua Infused Seed on ordinary vanilla farmland and allow it to grow. As the seed grows, it leaves some of its aspect behind in the farmland. Once the farmland has been infused with Aqua, remove the Aqua seed and plant your Perditio Infused Seed on the same block.

The Perditio from the seed will combine with the Aqua already stored in the farmland, producing Venenum. The farmland and seed will become infused with the new aspect, and once the Venenum seed reaches maturity, it can be harvested.

Naturally, waiting for these things to grow isn't particularly exciting. The Hoe of Growth works on Infused Seeds and can greatly speed up the process, although each use consumes 25 durability. With a sufficiently durable or repairable Hoe of Growth, you may even find some interesting ways to automate the process.

One warning before you dive too deeply into magical agriculture: reaching and researching Infused Seeds involves a lot of Warp. Consider yourself warned before deciding that unlimited magical wheat sounds harmless.

Maintaining multiblocks can be a pain, especially if you prefer performing other tasks around your base.  
To solve this, a certain engineer developed the Magical Maintenance Hatch — a simple maintenance hatch that fixes all your maintenance problems using centi-vis.

Simply attach the hatch to any multiblock and keep it within reach of a centi‑vis network. The device will consume 2500 centi‑vis of each primal aspect to resolve any maintenance problems the multiblock may develop.

The hatch stores 5000 centi-vis of each primal aspect. This means it takes on average 1000 ticks (50 seconds) to reach the internal buffer.

If you're having trouble making it work, make sure you place the hatch near a Vis Relay or an energized node with each primal aspect.

title: Adept Thaumaturgy > Primordial Armor
text:
Quest: Primordial Armor
Quest line: Adept Thaumaturgy

The Primordial Armor is the final evolution of the Fortress armor line, built by upgrading a full set of Shadow Fortress armor with primal power. This is a very powerful set, allowing for great defense and a plethora of useful mobility options for getting around.

By shift right-clicking any piece in your hand you can switch its primal alignment which grants unique abilities, some of which are powerful enough to require multiple pieces of armor to be aligned to one aspect: 

Aer
1 Alignment: Projectiles shot at you are reflected back at the shooter. In practice, this has an inconsistent minimum range of several blocks.
2 Alignments: Gain creative flight.

Terra
Boots: Gain knockback resistance.
1 Alignment: Gain Regeneration (2 + number of Terra-aligned pieces) whenever you take damage, except damage from the Sacrificial Knife.

Ignis
Helmet: Gain Night Vision when it is night or when the brightness level is less than 4, which also works underwater.
1 Alignment: Fire is automatically extinguished, and gain 25% resistance to explosion and fire damage. Further, whenever you take damage from a non-undead source, light it on fire for (5 * number of Ignis-aligned pieces) seconds.
2 Alignments: When fully submerged in lava you gain Fire Resistance, becoming immune to its damage, and can see without the normal red filter, but you also gain Blindness which limits your range of visibility.

Aqua
Helmet: Gain Water Breathing and, when underwater, Night Vision.
1 Alignment: Cure Blindness, Poison, Wither, Confusion, Taint Poison, Mining Fatigue, Hunger, and Weakness.

Ordo
Any piece: Reduces the Warping level from 10 to 5, and increase the vis discount from 6% to 10%.
1 Alignment: Gain Regeneration I, and any negative effects from warp (Vis Exhaustion, Thaumarrhea, Unnatural Hunger, Blurred Vision, Sun Scorned, or Death Gaze) have their potency reduced by the number of Ordo-aligned pieces and their duration reduced by 1/(1 + number of Ordo-aligned pieces).

Perditio
1 Alignment: Whenever you take damage from a non-undead source, afflict it with Slowness IV and Blindness for (10 * number of Perditio-aligned pieces) seconds.

title: Adept Thaumaturgy > Stable Division Sigil
text:
Quest: Stable Division Sigil
Quest line: Adept Thaumaturgy

The second ritual will not be as easy as the first one. After this ritual your sigil will be stable enough to make stable unstable ingots which will not explode, and will no longer take durability damage.

This ritual needs to be performed in The End dimension. The ritual is performed by placing a Beacon in the center of a flat area of at least 11x11, not necessarily End Stone. Then place a chest in each of the cardinal directions leaving 4 spaces empty between the chest and the Beacon. In each chest insert these specific contents:

North: iron ingot, gold ingot and the other things listed in the task.
South: The different Ore Blocks and the other things listed in the task.
East: The potions.
West: The Music disks.

A spiral pattern of Redstone and String is then laid out around the beacon. At any time, shift-right-clicking the Beacon with an Activated Division Sigil in hand will show the building progress of the ritual.

Finally, kill an Iron Golem while it stands within the ritual area to activate the process. If it works, there will be an explosion that destroys the beacon and chests, while every Enderman in the End vanishes. During the ritual, throngs of aggressive mobs imbued with Haste will begin spawning and attacking the Player who needs to kill 100 of them to complete the ritual. If the Player dies or leaves the dimension, the ritual will fail and will have to be started over. Once enough mobs have been killed, the first activated Sigil in the inventory will stabilize. The Pseudo-Inversion Sigil can be used an unlimited number of times, and dividing an Iron Ingot by Diamond will produce Mobius "Unstable-Stable" Ingot which does not explode, can be produced in any crafting interface and will stack up to 64.

title: And So, It Begins > Even more challenges needed?
text:
Quest: Even more challenges needed?
Quest line: And So, It Begins

You have played through most of the pack a few times already? Maybe you even made a Stargate? Or are you just looking for something a bit different? Don't worry, we have a few options for you:

- Play in Hardcore. Either Minecraft Hardcore, or BetterQuesting Hardcore. The latter is a bit more forgiving. Maybe this seems impossible, but people have indeed reached UEV+ in Minecraft Hardcore. Better be prepared to restart a few times. This is obviously not for everybody.

- Never make a rocket. The so called no-rocket run is somewhat supported by now, you will be able to do almost everything in the pack. Use bees, crops, and blood magic meteors as your main resource production. Be warned though that such a challenge is grindy and slow. For instance, you might need to collect large amounts of Andradite ore or via the aluminium bauxite slag route to get your first titanium. Or have to start breeding bees early without much technology to help.

- Skyblock. Yes, really. It is also known as Garden of Grind and it is absolutely brutal. There is no actually supported skyblock version of the pack but some players have figured out the minimal amount of changes needed to make it work. Ask around or search on the official discord channel for all the details. But don't expect any fun down this road.

- Speedrunning. A few players have designed some basic rules and have started to record speedruns to early game goals like the Coke Oven. Ask around or search on the official discord channel for all the details. Maybe you just want to watch how they do it.

title: And So, It Begins > Loading the Chunks
text:
Quest: Loading the Chunks
Quest line: And So, It Begins

Minecraft works in chunks - the 16x16 columns of blocks from bedrock to sky. The chunks in a radius around you are simulated or, in other words, chunkloaded. If a chunk is not loaded, nothing happens in it - crops don't grow, machines don't work. Thus, you want to have your base chunkloaded when you're off exploring. Later on, you want your base chunkloaded so things don't spontaneously blow up, especially multi-block machines.

You can chunkload in a few ways:

1) The ServerUtilities mod. With default settings, you will not be able to chunkload. Feel free to change that in the config if you are in singleplayer (SP) or running your own server.

2) Use four types of Anchors from Railcraft, although they are not craftable until the Low Voltage (LV) tier. In SP, or a server you run, cheat in Admin Anchors to chunkload forever, for free. They're limited on servers to prevent TPS dropping from people chunkloading a base forever when they aren't even there. On the officials, you need to use Ender Fragments, Ender Pearls, or Coins to fuel them. Look at the tooltip on each for how long it will work, and in what chunkloader.

3) Use one of the blocks that chunkloads itself. If you do this on a server, expect the admins to possibly get very mad at you if it's not something you're allowed to do. Same for vanilla methods.

Don't use chicken chunks to get anchor-like blocks. It's buggy.

title: And So, It Begins > Your First Night
text:
Quest: Your First Night
Quest line: And So, It Begins

Hello, friend, and welcome to GTNH!

Don't get used to things being nice and comfy, because in about ten minutes the sun will set, and unlike Vanilla Minecraft, there's no light whatsoever at night but plenty of Infernal mobs coming to get you. So your first task is to find food and shelter for the night.

But by the end of this quest tab you will have a bed to make things easier.

You don't need to keep this book. Even if you don't have the item, you can press Tilde (~) to view it at any time...unless you decided to change the keybind.

If you need any extra help or just want to hang out, feel free to visit our Discord server at https://discord.gg/gtnh. And yes, the links are clickable! On the Discord, select your tech tier in #role-select - it will help people to tailor their advice to your situation.

Many GTNH topics are explained in our Wiki at https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/Main_Page. It does not have the same extent and structure as the Questbook, but some things are much better with pictures and tables! The wiki also has tips on extra topics like what additional mods might work with the pack, how GTNH can be installed for modern Java versions or how to set up a server.

Additionally, there is a spreadsheet at https://www.gtnewhorizons.com/spreadsheet for the info you would want a spreadsheet for.

If you play through a launcher that relies on CurseForge, be aware that it doesn't always work properly. It doesn't play well with all the custom versions of mods that this pack has. So if you have any problems, first switch to another launcher like MultiMC, Prism, or Technic. The wiki has instructions there as well. The latest version of the pack is available on the Discord channel from #announcements or with the !download command.

Hopefully you didn't get munched by a monster while reading this, good luck!

title: Applied Energistics > 1k Crafting Storage
text:
Quest: 1k Crafting Storage
Quest line: Applied Energistics

Component of the crafting CPU which provides 1024 bytes of storage for crafting. The Crafting Storage blocks are the only necessary part. Each crafting CPU multiblock allows for a separate crafting job (this is different from sub-tasks of the same job). The more items in the recipe and sub-recipes, the more crafting storage you'll need. Having one big and a couple small might be a good idea, but remember it will try to use the best one available first when you order a craft. They are also used when a crafting card requests a craft, so you'll need several separate ones if you intend to use those a lot. A crafting CPU multiblock uses only one channel, regardless of its size. It must be square to form.

title: Applied Energistics > A Digital Singularity
text:
Quest: A Digital Singularity
Quest line: Applied Energistics

What? You filled up the Quantum storage cell? I hope it was with something better than Cobblestone. Anyway, you'd better make something EVEN bigger then.

Hmm, adding even more storage capacity to a single cell would result in something so dense with information that it would just collapse into a singularity. So why not be smart about it? Just use an already existing singularity! Build a sturdy casing around it and add some connecting components, and you should be good. Better use an eternal singularity, though, to make sure things remain stable.

The Digital Singularity can store more than 4 quintillion items. If you manage to fill one up, please contact the dev team so that they can ban you for cheating... eh, I mean, congratulate you on your achievement, of course!

title: Applied Energistics > Applied Greg?
text:
Quest: Applied Greg?
Quest line: Applied Energistics

ME Buses are a combination of technology and...other technology. Don't give me that look, it is, OK? With these, you can now directly I/O items between GregTech multiblock and ME network. They have significantly less lag, so please start using them as soon as possible on servers.

You just pop off your GT bus + ME bus or ME interface combination, and replace both with the new bus and connect a ME cable directly to it. It uses 1 channel, same as the other options.

The output bus and hatch have limited output space. If you need more, you can upgrade them either by crafting them with storage components or putting a cell inside. A digital singularity cell will make the cache near infinite.

Note that the output bus must eject each item from its cache in order. If it cannot eject the topmost item, it will be stuck and cannot eject any other items.

If voiding is turned off, the multiblock will not void when the ME Outputs are full.

Inside of the ME Output bus you have the option to enable Cache Mode which will fill the storage cell rather than sending the items to the ME network. Checking Mode will verify the inserted storage cell can accept the output before the machine starts.

For usage in some machines, i.e. the advanced assembly line, the configured item must be in the first slot in order for the multi to work.

The Knowledge Core holds up to 21 patterns for use in the Arcane Assembler, but you need a new assembler for every Knowledge Core if you want to autocraft more than that.

To encode the patterns, you need a Knowledge Inscriber. It works exactly as you would expect. It doesn't connect to the network, so it doesn't need a channel. If you want to erase a pattern, select it and the save icon should become erase instead.

title: Applied Energistics > Beam Me Up, Scotty
text:
Quest: Beam Me Up, Scotty
Quest line: Applied Energistics

If you want to teleport stuff around using these, you'll need a drive in the SIOP, and at least 6 pylons hooked up. The pylons need to indicate the X, Y and Z dimensions, with you needing 1 more than you would think. If the efficiency goes below 100%, the AE cost will balloon enormously, so add more pylons to counteract that. After using a redstone signal to activate the SIOP, the blocks will be moved to the spatial IO dim, and the drive will move to the output, so you can send it somewhere else. This is very important to do properly if you want to use it as a teleporter. Otherwise, you can get stuck there. Your network will need to be able to hold all the power needed to teleport at once, so you'll need at least one energy cell. You can only have one Pylon setup per controller, so consider putting them on a subnetwork.

Using 2 in the X and Z dimensions and 3 in the Y will give you a 1x2x1 teleporter to teleport yourself. You'll want a SIOP port on each side for sending and for receiving. But you'll still need to design a redstone contraption to activate them properly!

Read this if you want to know more about spatial IO in general, and larger setups: https://www.reddit.com/r/feedthebeast/comments/3c2b2r/a_treatise_on_nocheat_smp_ae2_spatial_io/
Also see this if you want to see a fancy teleporter: https://www.reddit.com/r/feedthebeast/comments/2mhrf8/ae2_spatial_transporters/

Spatial cells, once used, will only work in the XYZ dimensions first used, with no way to format or recraft. Test in creative first!

Expect your world to lag for a second after using, blame AE.

title: Applied Energistics > Bundled AE Channels
text:
Quest: Bundled AE Channels
Quest line: Applied Energistics

P2P tunnels. You'll probably want a bunch of them! They act as teleport points from one place to another for the contained information.

They can pack up to 32 channels into 1 channel and transport those to the destination P2P bus. Each P2P tunnel requires 1 free channel. P2P connections cannot be nested, but one transport cable can carry multiple P2P connections. For a normal fluix cable, that's 4 P2P connections, and 16 for dense.

You can use separate cables to connect input P2Ps to the controller and to transport from the controller to around your base, allowing for 32 output P2Ps on one dense cable. Alternatively you can use an entirely separate controller as a transport network.

Generally, you'll want to have the first point be one side of an ME Controller block (remember you can add more!), and the other where some of your machines are.

A nice online guide can be found at https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/Applied_Energistics_2 under P2P tunnels.

If you want to use one of the P2P tunnels for something other than ME channels, use an applicable item on the center of the face of the tunnel, (for example, a GT cable for GT EU, redstone for RS signal, an RF conduit for RF, a torch for light, a bucket for fluid, a chest for items, or an OC cable for OC) and it will convert to that type, even if you pick it up. Use a fluix cable to change it back.

title: Applied Energistics > Cables
text:
Quest: Cables
Quest line: Applied Energistics

To have access to your applied energistics network from your entire base, you'll need cables. A lot of them. For now, the basic ones will do, but eventually, you'll end up using dense cables and p2p channels. Glass and Covered cables are functionally identical, just different in looks. Each can carry 8 channels. Quartz fibers don't carry channels but can carry energy. This is useful for providing power from your main network to independent subnetworks.

You can also color your cables - cables with different colors will not connect, so those can be used to expand network capacity by running parallel cables. Only fluix colored cables connect to all other colors. Later it will probably be more efficient to use P2P channels to jam a bunch of channels into 1.

Anchors are like covers, keeping things from connecting when you don't want them to.

The card can only be inserted into:

ME Dual Interface
ME Interface

The Locking Card allows an interface to optionally block new crafts from being started for one of the following conditions:

While Redstone is low
While Redstone is high
After a craft has been pushed, until a redstone pulse is received
After a craft has been pushed, until the results have returned to the same network

Advanced Blocking Card:

The Advanced Blocking Card is able to ignore non-consumables in a subnet for more complicated automations. 

In a standard subnet, where two interfaces are facing each other, the Advanced Blocking Card is to be placed on the subnet interface.

title: Applied Energistics > Co-Processing
text:
Quest: Co-Processing
Quest line: Applied Energistics

Component of the crafting CPU which provides additional item delivery from the CPU to the ME Interface for crafting.

This can be used to make more machines active in parallel for the job, and thus increase overall crafting speed. 

Every Co-Processor adds one AE2 operation per tick. AE2 uses operations to push items to interfaces, this speeds up the rate at which it can push into your machines. As a side benefit, AE2 will split a task between multiple interfaces with the same pattern (or simulated pattern like with P2P Interface). This means if you have two interfaces with the same pattern for the same item AE2 with no co-processors will only push to one of those interfaces until it is full (so, if the craft is small it may not split it at all) whereas with a co-processor it will round robin between the two by splitting its operations per tick.

title: Applied Energistics > Deck of Cards
text:
Quest: Deck of Cards
Quest line: Applied Energistics

These cards add additional functionality to certain devices or fixtures. They specify what devices they work on in the tooltip.

Redstone Card: 

The Redstone Card adds redstone interactivity to the devices it can be used on, with the following options: 

Always active
Active with redstone signal
Active without redstone signal
Activate once per pulse

Capacity Card: 

The Capacity Card adds more slots for items that use them. 

If you add this to an Export Bus, an icon is added to select item priority.

Crafting Card: 

The Crafting Card allows you to automatically request autocrafting of items.

In an ME Interface: 

If you put in items to be stocked, if there aren't enough, it'll craft them until it reaches the selected amount. 

These crafts are being stocked for recipes that the ME Interface has.

If you want them to be seen by the network, you'll need to put a storage bus on the ME Interface.

In an ME Level Emitter: 

First Mode: It'll emit a redstone signal while the specific item is being crafted.

Second Mode: It will emit a redstone signal once a crafting job for the item has been requested, but it won't send the items to be crafted. 

This is useful if you're using a dummy pattern, and are using the level emitter to tell something else to happen. 

You still need to get the item(s) requested back into the system so it doesn't tie up a crafting CPU though.

In an ME Export Bus: 

It'll attempt to send whatever item(s) are selected in the export bus' GUI.

First Mode: It'll send available items first, then create crafting jobs for the rest. 

Second Mode: It will only send crafted items.

Acceleration Card: 

The Acceleration Card makes the device/fixture work faster. 

You'll probably want a lot of these.

Inverter Card: 

The Inverter Card allows you to invert the item filter of certain fixtures.

Fuzzy Card: 

The Fuzzy Card allows you to apply fuzzy logic to filtering to allow items with different NBT or damage data to be counted as the same. This is different from metadata. 

If you just want it to be fuzzy for NBT, set to Match Any. 

If it is set to 99%, it will work on anything that is damaged. You can use the Inverter Card to reverse this.

When used in an ME Interface, each fuzzy card (up to 3) will control 3 slots of the interface, from right to left.

The ME Storage Bus, when attached to another inventory block in the world lets you access that inventory via networked functions. This allows you to use chests, barrels, or other types of item storage in your networks.

The storage via the ME Storage Bus is bidirectional, it can both insert, or extract items from the inventory block it is attached to as long as the ME storage bus has its required channel.

The UI allows you to control which items are selected as storable items, this selection has no effect on what items can be extracted once they are in the storage.

The storage bus will function with nearly any inventory block, including ME Interfaces, EFR barrels, JABBA Barrels, Storage Drawers, etc. They can also be used to route items passively into Buildcraft pipes.

If you place a storage bus on an ME Interface the storage bus will be able to interact with the full contents of the target network, unless that interface is configured to store items inside itself, in which case it will see those stored items.

title: Applied Energistics > ME in Your Cleanroom
text:
Quest: ME in Your Cleanroom
Quest line: Applied Energistics

Wireless Connectors are a close range Quantum Network Bridge alternative.

Connections are point-to-point - you can't connect more than 2 blocks together. Each block will use 10 + distance * ln(distance^2 + 3) AE/t. Does not work across dimensions. Power needs to be provided on only one side. Up to 32 channels can be transferred through the connection. Can connect directly to dense cables. The Wireless Connector itself does not use any channels.

The Wireless Kit can be used to link the connectors together. There are three modes: Simple, Advanced, and Super. In Simple Mode, you simply right-click your source and target, and they will link. In Advanced Mode, you can do this in queue/binding groups instead of individually. In Super Mode, you can manage the connections through a menu that opens after you right-click.

Also, these are more TPS friendly than large chains of dense cables!

The security system does not prevent destructive tampering, removing cables / machines or breaking of drives. If you need to protect your system from physical vandalism you will need another form of physical security. This block provides network level security.

The player who places the ME security terminal has full control over the network and cannot exclude themselves any rights. By adding a blank biometric card you define a default behavior for every player who has no biometric card registered.

In addition to security on the software layer, you can link up your wireless terminal with the network and access it wirelessly if you have that setup already.

If you have one on your main network, your subnets may also need one to have access to your main network, but this is not always the case depending on how you set it up.

T2: Normal access point range

title: Applied Energistics > Moar Patterns!
text:
Quest: Moar Patterns!
Quest line: Applied Energistics

You may have noticed that the ME Interface's GUI is different than before. That is because with this card you can have more patterns, adding 9 more per card up to a total of 36. HOWEVER, it also uses 4 times the energy for every item when crafting, and this is multiplicative for each new card. If doing large crafts, make sure you have some dense energy cells ready.

So basically: (sum of amounts of items in the pattern) * config multiplier (which is 10 for GTNH). With cards, it's also multiplied by 4^(number of upgrades)

E.g: (wood log -> planks) in the interface w/o upgrades would draw: 1*10 AE units, which is 5 EU (remember 1 EU = 2 AE)
(9 charcoal -> charcoal block) compressor recipe in the interface with 3 upgrades will draw 9*10*4^3*0.5 = 2070 EU, but only 45EU without any cards

They're kind of expensive, so consider holding off if you can't afford the material or EU costs. If you remove it, all the extra patterns will pop out, so be careful of that when moving your stuff.

title: Applied Energistics > Optimizing Patterns in Late Game!
text:
Quest: Optimizing Patterns in Late Game!
Quest line: Applied Energistics

You have probably already seen the button called Optimize Patterns when making an order in your AE system, now it's time to put it to good use!

To unlock this feature, just add a Pattern Optimization Matrix block to your AE system (you only need one).

# What does it do?

This feature allows you to multiply patterns that are needed in large amounts.

1. After calculating a big order, just click Optimize Patterns and you will be welcomed by a new window.
2. There you specify how much you wish for a singular pattern to be ordered (maximum amount of steps), we recommend putting it at 1000 or 100, remember that over-optimizing patterns could lead to longer waiting times. At this point, you can also disable singular patterns from optimization by clicking on them, but there shouldn't be any unwanted patterns anyway if you already excluded them by toggling a button in unwanted interfaces.
§

3. Click Optimize and you are done! Try ordering again to see the changes in pattern steps

All changes are permanent and can't be reverted automatically so make sure that you have excluded all unwanted interfaces (the Allow Pattern Optimization button is GRAY) like:
- Single Assembly Line interfaces
- Extreme Crafting interfaces
- And any interface that doesn't have (almost) infinite buffer at the other side (inf. chest/storage cells)
Patterns are only multiplied by powers of 2, so your AAL patterns should be safe.

If you are still confused about maximum order steps here's an example:
Ordering an EOH calculates that it will need 1,000,008 UHV superconductors crafted (41667 steps, 24 UHV SC patterned), now you proceed to optimize patterns and specify that you wish it to do 1000 steps maximum, it will multiply your pattern 64 times to achieve that goal (41667 / 64 ~= 652 which is lower or equal to 1000). After clicking optimize, UHV SC pattern will now output 1536 UHV SC (24 before).

title: Applied Energistics > Pattern Repeater
text:
Quest: Pattern Repeater
Quest line: Applied Energistics

The Pattern Repeater is a niche but useful tool. It allows recipes to be visible across networks.

When two networks are linked via a repeater, you could have a pattern that lives on network A and be able to see it in network B. In practice, you could request the item from network B (using items from network B), then those items would be transferred to the pattern destination on network A, and the resulting item would end up on network B when completed.

In order to set this up, simply make a pair of Pattern Repeaters (attached to separate networks) face into one another. You can then use a wrench to toggle each to the desired mode: either Provider or Accessor. You will need one of each.

The "Accessor" side is where the original pattern should sit. It will "send" the pattern to the other network. (Network A in the example above)

The "Provider" side is where the pattern is provided to. It "receives" the incoming pattern from the other network. (Network B in the example above)

title: Applied Energistics > Pattern Terminal
text:
Quest: Pattern Terminal
Quest line: Applied Energistics

A specialized version of the ME crafting terminal designed to encode blank patterns into encoded patterns.

Lets you browse the contents of your network like other terminals, but also contains an area for designing patterns. There are two modes for pattern encoding. Crafting patterns, and processing patterns. Processing patterns are designed for use with machines that do not use standard crafting recipes - such as furnaces, or other machines. To select between modes, click the button to the right of the interface: when it shows a standard crafting table, it will create crafting patterns, and when it shows a furnace, it will create processing patterns.

For crafting patterns ("Crafts..."), you specify the input crafting materials on a standard 3x3 crafting grid, and the output materials are determined automatically.

For processing patterns ("Creates..."), you specify the input materials and output materials, including quantity, by placing stacks of items in the interface. If a processing operation is not guaranteed to succeed (such as secondary products from some machines), it will not work correctly as a processing pattern.

When designing crafting patterns you can click the output to extract a crafted item as long as you have the materials required to craft the item.

Be cautious about accidentally enabling oredict substitution, it's rarely used and you will keep it disabled 99% of the time.

Works exactly the same with items, fluids, and essentia.

title: Applied Energistics > Short Guide - A Basic AE2 System
text:
Quest: Short Guide - A Basic AE2 System
Quest line: Applied Energistics

So you've unlocked AE2, but don't know how to use it? Not to worry, that's what this questline is for. For a basic (and not completely useless) ME system, make the items on the right first. After you go through the quests to get them normally of course.

You could technically make one with an ME Chest, but there's no advantage over using a regular chest.

Connect power to the Energy Acceptor, place the ME Drive next to it, place a Fluix Cable on top of the ME Drive connect the ME Terminal to the cable. Just put in the Storage cells, and you're done! Remember you need a Network Tool to see how much power it actually uses. Also, it lets you pick up stuff easier.

To save power, let's do a little extra work. Place the Pressure Plate two spaces in front of the ME Terminal, place redstone next to it and beside the Energy Acceptor. Remove the EA and place a Fluix Cable there, and then place the ME Toggle Bus between the Drive and where the Energy Acceptor will be. Then plunk that back down and re-power it. This will cause it to only connect (and thus use power) when you stand on the plate. This tiny network uses about 38 EU by itself, so you should understand that an ME system is not cheap either in materials or power.

You should make either 1k or 4k storage cells to put into your ME Drive.

title: Applied Energistics > Short Guide - Autocrafting
text:

Quest line: Applied Energistics

This is the main purpose of AE2, so let's get to it. Plunk down the Crafting Storage and Molecular Assembler, connect the Pattern Terminal to a cable, and attach the ME Interface to the MA (make sure it has power from another side). You could run it without a ME Interface, but you can only do one recipe then. Place a Blank Pattern in the Pattern Terminal, and add the recipe for a Crafting Table, then click the arrow to save it to the pattern. Put this in the ME Interface and you can now request a craft of it. (if the items are in the network, otherwise it'll fail obviously)

For processing patterns (machines, anything not regular 3x3 crafting) click the button on the right. You'll need to specify all I/O for it yourself. You can use this on an ME Interface on a furnace (for example), combined with an ME Import Bus to collect the results. If it's a machine that auto-ejects (like multis) you can use a ME Interface to collect the results much faster (and with less lag).

Quest line: Applied Energistics

Drawers are great, right? Well, let's connect your ME system to a bank of them. Set up some drawers nearby with a controller attached. Then place an ME Storage Bus against the controller and set the priority to +1. This will prioritize I/O to the drawer controller. Lock your drawers before they fill with random stuff. Now you have access to the whole thing! Great for the results of mining, and anything else you have thousands of, while keeping your ME system relatively empty.

You can also connect to chests and other things if you want. You can use an Ender Chest to send stuff into your network, which will then send it to the drawers, but you'll have stuff entering and exiting constantly, so it'll mess up your view in the Terminal. You can use filtered view cells, or process them before they go into your ME network (or in a different one) and/or send them to the DC directly via another EC. It depends on what you want to do and what it is.

Using the drawer controller with large amounts of I/O will tank TPS! If you're on a server, do not use drawer cubes, or expect the possibility of it being deleted or you getting banned.

title: Applied Energistics > Starting Your AE2 Journey
text:
Quest: Starting Your AE2 Journey
Quest line: Applied Energistics

Applied Energistics 2 is an integral part of GTNH gameplay. 

AE2 is the primary networking and logistics management mod in GTNH for Items, Fluids, and Crafting. You will use it starting from EV and onward for most automations you perform. Given the sheer density of this modpack there are a variety of unique tools and features added specifically to aid in your adventure. Most of these tools are covered in this quest tab.

There is a lot to learn, but don't feel overburdened! Your abilities will continue to grow the more time you spend with it. There are a wide variety of helpful resources to take advantage of in addition to this book when it comes to learning:

1. The Wiki: https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/Applied_Energistics_2

- The Wiki has a lot of great starter information on what various systems do. They also have a lot of machine specific automation tutorials so be sure to check the Wiki if you're struggling or want a point of reference.

2. The Discord: https://discord.gg/gtnh

- The Discord is full of experienced AE2ers', check out #ae2-help to find plenty of people who will take time to help you figure something out.

3. Video Tutorials: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LUYVmIAEC-I

- There are a lot of great GTNH content creators who make high quality video tutorials for this. Here is a link to AE2 Fundamentals by IX. There's an advanced version as well.

title: Applied Energistics > Storing Your ME Data
text:
Quest: Storing Your ME Data
Quest line: Applied Energistics

The ME Drive is designed to do one thing, store storage cells. This block holds 10 storage cells so you can tightly pack your storage into a very small space. ME drives show their contents and the storage cell status on the front of the drive face.

The ME Chest which you used to craft the Drive is very similar, except it can only store 1 cell (though it comes with an in-built terminal!).

Red - Indicates the storage cell is full.
Orange - Indicates the storage cell cannot hold any more types, but it can store more items.
Green - Indicates the cell can hold more types, or more items.
Black - Indicates there is no channel, or power is offline.

It's important to note, that without an ME Network this block does nothing. It's only useful when combined with a way to input, and output items, and requires 2 AE/t power to function, and additional power for each storage cell stored inside it.

About Priority: Many devices in AE2 have a priority setting, this determines what gets items first. This is useful in some situations, but not so much in others. Higher number = higher priority.

title: Applied Energistics > Super Stock Replenisher
text:
Quest: Super Stock Replenisher
Quest line: Applied Energistics

The Super Stock Replenisher (SSR) is an incredibly useful item, especially for those pesky loop automations!

To use, put a storage cell in the empty slot (item vs fluid & type amount do not matter) and you can set up to 63 items & 9 fluids to be stocked by the machine. The total quantity of both items and fluids are determined by the byte size of the storage cell.

When an item / fluid is stocked, it will pull it from the ME network it is attached to and those items / fluids will become invisible to your network. You can then use a storage bus to make these items visible to a subnet. Items will not be able to re-enter the SSR once pulled out. The SSR will automatically replenish its inventory from your AE network whenever the internal stock reaches less than 50% of the configured value.

When an item or fluid is erased from the stocker or when the stocker is broken, everything will return to the network the stocker was attached too, so no need to panic about losing items.

Prerequisites: Stocking Fluids; Applied Greg?

title: Applied Energistics > To Link P2P Buses
text:
Quest: To Link P2P Buses
Quest line: Applied Energistics

A small item that can be used to store, copy, and paste settings. Shift-right-click on a configurable object to save the settings onto the memory card, then right-click on any other block of the same type to paste the settings. Shift-right-click on a non-configurable object (or the air) to clear. They are also used to link the input P2P tunnel to the corresponding output P2P tunnels. They can also link Vis Relays to compatible devices.

If you're doing more advanced operations in a large network of P2Ps, it's recommended you use the advanced memory card. It has a helpful UI that allows you to visualize and set names, inputs, and outputs of P2P tunnels. 

Remember P2Ps can only have 1 input! The only exception being fluid P2Ps whose input can function as an output and whose outputs can function as an input.

Make sure there aren't any cards in your network tool when you craft the Advanced Memory Card, they will be deleted!

title: Applied Energistics > Tools of the Trade
text:
Quest: Tools of the Trade
Quest line: Applied Energistics

The Network Tool is AE2's main utility tool.

Right-click on a network to see the power usage, and what makes up the network.
Right-click on air to interact with its inventory to store cards or turn facades transparent.
Shift-right-click to remove fixtures (import bus, interface, etc.) that don't take up a full block without removing the cable, or remove any AE block immediately the same way.

The Network Visualizer does exactly what it says, it allows you to visualize the channels of your network. First, right-click a network to select it. At first you'll see everything, but you can change the modes by holding sneak and right-clicking to see different things. Remember that if you have a subnetwork, like one that P2P tunnels go through for example, those nodes won't show up since it's a different network, but the P2P tunnels entrances and exits will. This goes through solid objects, so you can look at your whole base.

title: Applied Energistics > Visualizing How Much Your Stuff
text:
Quest: Visualizing How Much Your Stuff
Quest line: Applied Energistics

The ME Storage Monitor allows you to visualize how much of an item or fluid you have. For example you can tell if you're running low on circuits and should make more, or how a long crafting process is proceeding. There are a couple of ways to use them.

Right-click with item or control-right-click with fluid container: Will display the current level of that item or fluid if not locked.
Right-click with empty hand: Will reset the display if not locked.
Right-click with AE2 wrench or network tool: Will toggle the lock.

The ME Conversion Monitor is the upgraded version of the ME Storage Monitor. It adds the ability to directly withdraw from or store items and fluids in the ME Network. It has the normal interactions, plus more.

Shift-right-clicking with item or fluid container: Attempts to insert the item stack into the network. This works even if it's not the displayed item!
Shift-double-right-clicking: Attempts to insert all item and fluid stacks of the type displayed into the network.
Right-clicking (while locked): Attempts to pull out a stack of the item displayed or fill held cell.

title: Basic Automation > Electrolyzing Water
text:
Quest: Electrolyzing Water
Quest line: Basic Automation

Now let's automate electrolyzing water into oxygen and hydrogen. You'll need hydrogen for tons of stuff including desulfurization, obtaining tungsten, and nitric acid production. Oxygen is also useful as I'm sure you noticed when making steel.

How to set it up:

Place the electrolyzer down and connect it to water and electricity. Place the 2 super tanks nearby. Set the electrolyzer to produce hydrogen gas and oxygen cells. Use normal GT fluid pipes to output the hydrogen gas into one super tank. That is now your hydrogen storage. Now connect interface pipes to all 3 machines.

For the electrolyzer put in item stock keeper set to keep 2 empty cells stored. Also put in extractor set to extract oxygen cells.

Now for the oxygen storage put in item responder chip set to accept oxygen cells and extractor set to extract empty cells.

Now put some empty cells inside your default storage chest and don't forget to have a broadcaster there.

title: Be(e) Breeding > Attuned
text:
Quest: Attuned
Quest line: Be(e) Breeding

You're now getting into Magic Bees, and one of its mundane bee species is the Attuned species. These are scooped out of Deep Hives that you can find in the Overworld. These hives are a pain to find, so you should consider just buying hives with coins until you get a princess and a drone. However, if you are a real masochist or completionist try-hard, then here's some information about where they spawn:

* From Y=1 to Y=25
* In stone, surrounded on 5 sides. Not just vanilla stone.
* In biomes tagged with one or more of:
   * MOUNTAINS: Actual mountains may not count. It's the biome type that counts.
      * Example: Canyon.
   * HILLS: Again, actual hills don't count.
      * Example: Snowy Coniferous Forest.
   * MAGICAL: Unlike the others, they do have some ethereal aspect.
      * Examples: Magical Forest is obvious, but also Cherry Blossom Grove counts.
* Surrounded by a small redstone vein. This often fills any open space around them.

They also like to just kind of show up whatever-what-the-heck in other biomes. Our beekeeping intern found a Deep Hive in a Lush Desert:

Lush Desert [HOT, DRY, SAVANNA, LUSH, SANDY]

You can dump the biome data in NEI by clicking on the NEI options button (the wrench), then the Tools button, then the Data Dumps button, and finally the Dump button in the biomes category. This creates a "dumps" directory in the root folder of the modpack with a biome.csv inside of it. Any listed biome that has the tags of HILLS, MOUNTAINS, and/or MAGICAL can generate Deep Hives. You can feed these biomes into a Nature's Compass and see if there are any nearby.

Prospector's Scanners will pick up the little ore pockets for these (traces, small samples). If you had one of those end-game ones with a display, it would come up as a few red pixels. Larger ones are probably just regular ore veins. The ore finding wand doesn't do a good job from the surface. Chasing lava veins and tunnels helps. Ore veins filled with redstone will saturate either tool.

Of course, just buying hives is the low-effort way.

Beekeeper's Notes:

If you get real bad luck and wind up with an ignoble princess, then just get a bunch of drones out of it and convert some other pristine princess afterwards. However, using base princesses will compel the bees to turn into the Common species. There are two choices:

1. Use an Alveary with an Alveary Stabilizer to block mutations.
2. Create a princess that doesn't line up with the Attuned species' breeding possibilities before starting.

title: Be(e) Breeding > Breed some common bees
text:
Quest: Breed some common bees
Quest line: Be(e) Breeding

To cross breed bees you need two different species of bees. One drone and one princess from different naturally-generating hives (Meadows and Forest as an example).

Bee Houses do not allow crossbreeding. You need an Apiary to cross-breed them to a new species. Certain frames will help this process. Shortening their lifespan means faster crosses. Increasing the mutation rate means getting mutations and thus rare bees quicker.

Common Bees produce Honey Combs every 2.2 minutes. Note that production times are an approximation based on the bee's base production speed and the product's rarity. They do not reflect actual production time.

Make sure your bees are pure by checking their genetics with a Beealyzer or GT scanner.

Breeder's Notes:

Riiiight from the start, they have a trick for you. The Common bee is bred from most mundane species smashed into each other. The problem is the Cultivated species, which is next in line, is bred with most mundane species along with Common. Noble and Diligent then are crossed from Common and Cultivated. You could start with two mundane bees, have the results loop back unattended, and run that whole progression. Here's an example active:inactive mix you could get on a princess over time:

Meadows:Forest
Meadows:Common (Yay!)
Common:Meadows (Double yay! Active trait!)
Cultivated:Common (Boo!)
. . . some time passes . . .
Diligent:Noble (Wait, what?!)

Meanwhile, this quest would still be sitting there, waiting for you to submit Common bees. Whoops!

If Cultivated starts to show up, just stuff any princesses and drones involved into a chest and act like that didn't happen for now. You can use them when you complete this quest to jumpstart the Cultivated species.

Now, if you don't have any way to speed up breeding and don't want to stand around to micromanage, you can try filtering, or just checking on the result from time to time. Either way, maybe don't leave it going overnight if you're on a server.

Quest: Clay
Quest line: Be(e) Breeding

To breed a Clay bee, you must put a Clay block beneath the housing. Clay bees are the bedrock of many important bee lines. Breed them from Industrious and Diligent.

Breeder's Notes:

This bee is an ancestor for a diverse group of species. A lot of them have incompatible biome requirements--especially the humidity. While breeding, you'll find that you have to alter the biome from cycle to cycle. You probably want to just earmark a spot that is NORMAL/DAMP right now if your only option for handling this is to run around with your breeding setup.

You're probably on your way to more interesting production bees, but don't forget that clay dust can be electrolyzed into some useful stuff!

Prerequisites: Industrious; Diligent

title: Be(e) Breeding > Coal
text:
Quest: Coal
Quest line: Be(e) Breeding

Ah yes, Coal is King indeed, but Coal Bees are matriarchal. A great bee, giving you Coal to use to power your industry. This will require a Coal Block under your bee housing. This bee will also have the first really dangerous effect - it will apply a creeper explosion to you if you are not wearing your Apiarist suit. Breed them from Peat and Industrious.

Breeder's Notes:

This is a major prerequisite ancestor species to a lot of other bee species in this chapter, and they're advanced ones too. The problem is the Coal species is long-lived, so it takes a long time for the queen to drop down to a princess and two drones (assuming the Coal species default of 2x fertility). Consider using some lifetime-reducing frames to accelerate that so you can get a Coal drone stock more quickly and start on those other species.

Tasks:

Rewards: enhancedlootbags:lootbag:26
Prerequisites: Industrious; Peat
Unlocks: Apatite; Ash; Diamond; Explosive; Lead; Oil; Steel; Thorium

The Copper Combs have a strong chance of centrifuging into copper dust, but you'll also see a Chemical Reactor recipe to use hydrochloric acid to get a 1:1 exchange. You have some bee options for getting chlorine so you should think about a sustained hydrochloric acid production line soon. You'll eventually have to use hydrochloric acid and won't have the Centrifuge option for later combs.

Breeder's Notes: Infernal bees are used to make both this species and Spiteful, which is next in line from Hateful. That means you'll probably start winding up with Spitefuls while trying to make this species. Since this is a progression to more interesting species, you could say it doesn't matter, but:

1. Skipping straight to Spiteful means not getting this quest done and then losing your progression.
2. Maybe you want to do a Smoldering bee, which needs this one.

What we recommend is tucking away any Spitefuls you get and just act like that didn't happen until you finish this bee. If the princess starts turning Spiteful and you don't want to just start a new one, you'd want to pump it with Infernal or Eldritch (pick one!) until you've cleaned out the Spiteful trait.

Heroic is the only thing you can use them for, but you'll have a better time of it if you have more than a handful of drones. Infernal bees are mundane: you get them from hives, and they have no ancestors.

Infernal hives are in The Nether, surrounded by nether quartz. Avoid large nether quartz blobs in ore chunks. Instead, look for little pockets of nether quartz. Any ghast-infested, open area will show a few dabs of them. Alternately, if you're tunneling around, you'll inevitably bump into some of these small pockets.

Zombie pigmen will get mad if they spot you nibbling on their quartz, so consider just breaking away the netherrack around the quartz to see that it's a solid cluster that could surround a hive. If so, you are just one or two mining hammer swings away from a likely infernal hive.

There's another way to get these hives: buy them with coins! Ka-ching!

Their molten combs are nice for a mundane bee. They centrifuge down to refractory wax, which can be used for fireproof wood and refractory capsules.

Infernal bees have an aggressive trait, so they'll damage entities--namely, you--when you are within their territory. You want an apiarist's suit before you start working with them. Alternately, if you set them up in an isolated spot, you can just run real fast. This isn't sustainable for all types of aggressive bees, by the way.

Breeder's Notes: You can run these bees in the Overworld if you can find a hot/arid climate. When in doubt, place an apiary and look at what it claims the climate is in the upper right of its GUI. Even if the bee isn't jubilant, but you can get drones out of them for breeding. Then you don't have to run back and forth to The Nether to run a cycle with a fussy queen while cross-breeding.

Use nether wart to keep them happy, and don't forget some soul sand!

They don't cross breed with other mundane bees into stuff like Common and Cultivated bees, so you can convert another mundane princess to an Infernal princess if you have the drones. Just take some care with this. For example, if you try this with an Arctic princess, you could wind up with an Infernal princess that needs a scorching/arid climate, but also needs snow to pollinate.

title: Be(e) Breeding > Monastic
text:
Quest: Monastic
Quest line: Be(e) Breeding

Monastic bees aren't found in hives or bred. Instead, you will need to find a Beekeeper villager and trade with them for it. There are various ways to make more villagers, so do some research.

Trader's Notes:

Beekeeper villagers spawn in houses that have a fenced back yard with apiaries. If the apiaries are missing, the villager didn't spawn. Or, well, a player already came along and looted the apiaries. They might have abducted the beekeeper too. The beekeeper should be wearing an apiarist outfit. Their initial trades probably don't have this bee. You will have to work up to this by trading what is available. If they require a princess for a trade, an ignoble one is fine. Honorable mention goes to the trade of some logs for an apiary. That's so much easier than having to make them yourself! If trades lock up, one trade of the "rightmost" trade should unlock preceding ones so you can keep trying to get this trade to pop up.

You can make a golden lasso at LV tier and run off with the villager. If you do, prepare a heavily-fortified spot. Even single-block-wide walls won't keep all zombies away. Consider just keeping the beekeeper in the lasso when you're not using them.

Beekeeper's Notes:

The base fertility for a Monastic bee is 1x. That's really annoying. When each cycle ends, you get a princess and a drone. That's it. You don't get surplus stock for carrying on breeding. If you can't just straight up alter the genome, then you can try to convert an arctic princess (or something else with a high fertility) with monastic drones in a way that gives you a higher fertility.

On the flip side, their long life is useful to try to get into production bees so you don't quickly clog up your bee product inventories with drones.

The "monastic line" of bees have other quirks. They'll take stuff like wheat and bookshelves as pollination sources. They can have some nasty aggression habits. They are long-lived, so you want something that cuts their life cycle for breeding--like an oblivion frame. You will start out here with a bee that likes average temperatures and humidity, but that'll drift to outright hellish and arid (but not The Nether!) for descendant species.

title: Be(e) Breeding > Ocean
text:
Quest: Ocean
Quest line: Be(e) Breeding

The Ocean bee is bred from Diligent and Water in an ocean-type biome. Note that this doesn't mean literally an ocean. It is any biome that has the OCEAN tag. The stock terrain generator does not generate oceans in The Overworld, but there are a few biomes that carry the tag.

Skipping The Overworld, you might have luck trying in a Twilight Forest lake - you'll know you are in the right biome if you see Water Creepers!

You can dump the biome data in NEI by clicking on the NEI options button (the wrench), then the Tools button, then the Data Dumps button, and finally the Dump button in the biomes category. This creates a "dumps" directory in the root folder of the modpack with a biome.csv file inside of it. Try anything that has OCEAN tagged to it. You can feed these biomes into a Nature's Compass and see if there are any nearby.

Some examples: Shield, Tropics, Twilight Lake, and Lush Swamp.

If you have trouble locating an appropriate spot, you can also purchase Ocean bees from the Vending Machine. Breed them from Diligent and Water.

You get more than one princess per purchase, so it's a useful way to get a few extra pristine princesses.

title: Be(e) Breeding > Salt
text:
Quest: Salt
Quest line: Be(e) Breeding

At this point, you may have noticed that these higher-tier metal combs can't be extracted with a centrifuge. Instead, you need to pass them through a chemical reactor with some hydrochloric acid. This will leave you in a pickle. Here you are, trying to reach post-scarcity, and now you're limited by chlorine.

Speaking of pickles, hydrochloric acid is kind of like a pickle, right? After all, you make both with salt! The salt bee is perfect for this. Well, the apatite bee line can get you some salt and also some phosphorus for phosphoric acid, but you have to start on ash bees first. Meanwhile, you'll likely take care of the salt bee's prerequisites on your way through getting all the major ores.

Breed them from clay and aluminium bees on top of a block of salt.

They will produce salt combs, borax dust, slag combs, and trace lithium combs. The salt combs will require at least an MV-tier centrifuge, but at least it doesn't require processing with acid in a chemical reactor!

Breeder's Notes:

There are two challenges with this bee:

1. The 5% chance of mutation. You may consider trying the escritoire minigame to get a boost to this chance. If so, favor aluminium drones because you're probably on your way to the other bees derived from aluminium ancestry, and they all only have a 5% chance anyways. They could all use a little boost.

2. The humidity swing between clay and aluminium species. Clay bees want it wet, and both aluminium and salt bees want it completely arid. If you can't manipulate the climate or the tolerances of any of the bees, consider starting by plugging clay drones into a modest princess. This has a good chance to get you a clay princess that prefers a dryer climate. You can then do all your breeding exclusively in an arid biome.

Also, once the Vis species trait shows up in some drones and/or a princess, it's just regular cross-breeding to get a pure princess and pure drone. That can be done any day too.

Despite the focus on moon phases, you do not need to breed at night to trigger the mutation.

The Ethereal and Infernal bees are a rough combination. Since you'll need a new princess for this bee, consider using a pristine princess that isn't aggressive and is closer to your Ethereal bees' climate. If you get lucky, you may breed out the aggression and produce hybrid Infernals that don't need to live in an oven to function. You will probably need your apiarist suit if the bred queen gets a dominant Infernal trait for a few cycles.
