title: Forestry and Multifarms > The Multifarm
text:
Quest: The Multifarm
Quest line: Forestry and Multifarms

The smallest farm you can build requires 36 farm blocks (3x4x3 - the largest is 5x4x5 or 100 farm blocks). Place the underlying blocks corresponding to the farm type you built. In this case, Stone Bricks. You can place these blocks beside or under the multi structure, but not the layer above. It will search 6 blocks above these for dirt/farmland/sand/soul sand/humus depending on farm type, with the appropriate crops, saplings, etc. on top of that.

You can use different modes to collect different crops. Arboretum for trees, infernal for nether wart and so on. You can even mix and match modes on the same farm - cutting trees down for wood in part, and collecting fruit from trees without destroying it in another, for example. So long as they're on different sides, at least.

You may need to experiment a bit to see what works, but https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/Multifarm has a decent list, though it doesn't specify cotton for managed crop farms for example. It might be a GTNH change, I dunno. A number of crops have an added CropsNH crop version as well, so you may prefer those for the higher yield if you level them up. Orchard mode works with Pam's, and Witchery, just to save you some time. Pam's nether crops however don't seem to work at all though.

title: Getting Around... > Better Boots with a little pizzazz

Quest: Better Boots with a little pizzazz
Quest line: Getting Around...

Electric Boots of the Traveller grant you a 2% Vis Discount along with all the benefits of the regular Boots of the Traveller.

In addition, they come with a wide variety of new features thanks to our amazing magic devs:

- Configurable Jump Boost: You can choose between 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, or a 100% jump boost.

- Configurable Speed Boost: Similar to the jump boost, you can adjust the speed boost percentage to your preference.

- Flight Inertia: When toggled on, this feature cancels inertia while flying, allowing for precise movement even when traveling at high speeds.

- Omnidirectional Movement: This toggle lets you decide whether your speed boost applies in all directions or only while running straight ahead.

None of these keybinds are set by default. The easiest way to configure them is to go into Options -> Controls, turn on the "Category" button, and type "Thaumic Boots." Then, assign keys for the features as needed.

If you want to advance in the dark arts you can also make them voidwalker boots.

title: Getting Around... > Fluid Loader and Unloader
text:
Quest: Fluid Loader and Unloader
Quest line: Getting Around...

If you plan to automate the oil transport from your oil field far away, you need a fluid loader and unloader. A locking track will stop the train as long as oil is loaded or unloaded.

PS: You should probably use the Long Distance Fluid Pipeline once you can make it in LV unless you really love trains.

Full details on how to use these may require online research (GTNH changes the recipes, not normal Railcraft functionality), but here is a simple list of things to do:

1. Make a loop of track from your base to the oil well.
2. Place a locking track near the well, and put a fluid loader two blocks above it. The track should be in Locking Mode - use a crowbar to change it.
3. Use the tank car on the filter in the loader and set it to Immediate mode.
4. Connect the well to the loader as normal.
5. Put a fluid unloader under a locking track at your base, and set it the same as the loader.
6. Automate the locomotive similarly - a fluid loader above a steam locomotive set to manual and filtered to the locomotive.

Either you got it working, you need to do more research, you realized it moves 32 buckets a trip and decided to just walk, or you can go to Discord and ask why anyone would build a train.

Item loaders also exist, but the main use for them may be to refuel your locomotive.

 * If looking at a block within 4 range: teleport to the other side of a wall, 16 range

Shift-right-click:
 * Same as right-click, but ignoring travel anchors

Note: The right-click and shift-right-click actions are fully configurable. Check the EnderIO Staff Settings configs!

 0: Do nothing

title: Handle Logistics with Pipes > Get Those Machines to Work
text:
Quest: Get Those Machines to Work
Quest line: Handle Logistics with Pipes

Most of the recipes are made in all kinds of machines. While a crafting logistics pipe works, it can only hold 1 recipe per pipe.

It is not an issue for logistics crafting tables as it can only hold one crafting table recipes, but it is wasteful to assign only one recipe for one machine.

For machines, use chassis. Preferably a higher tier. A Mk1 chassis with a crafting module is basically just a crafting logistics pipe.

You can't shift-click recipes from NEI so you have to drag the recipe from it. Don't worry, you can drag ghost items from NEI into the slots in the module to configure it.

You notice there are 3 gray slots at the right. They are for satellite logistics pipes. We will talk about it later.

Note: do NOT use the output face of the machine. The output side blocks all interactions unless you hit it with a screwdriver.

Also do NOT use auto-output, or else the machine will output the item into the pipe and the network will treat the product as an item inserted into the system rather than an item requested by the system and will send it to its storage. Every other face except the cover works.

The check mark means you have read the whole thing and should know how machine automation works using LP. The reward of this quest is the knowledge of how to automate GT machine recipes

Quest line: Handle Logistics with Pipes

There are 2 pipes that can do the job: transfer fluid into a tank connected to a fluid basic pipe allocated to said fluid.

1. Logistics Fluid Extractor Pipe. It extracts fluid from connected buffer to the correct big storage tank. It doesn't require a pump but it is slower.

2. Logistics Fluid Insertion Pipe. It does not pull fluids from tanks actively, requiring a GT pump if you are using GT tanks, but it can send fluids faster.

Take a pick :)

title: Handle Logistics with Pipes > Let this Sink in
text:

Quest line: Handle Logistics with Pipes

A well organized storage system is crucial for a logistics system.

With the ability to use modules through a chassis, we can now prepare for storage modules.

Logistics Pipes uses ItemSink modules to assign storage spaces.

This ItemSink modules can be used in 2 ways:

1. Assign the storage of a connected inventory with at most 9 different kinds of items by setting 9 items as filter on the module.

2. Assign a connected inventory as a default route. The default route is a destination for items that have no other valid storage spaces.

Note: remember to always check if the default route has additional spaces because items that are stuck in the pipes without a destination will eventually YEET themselves out of the pipes.

Every system takes power. A Logistics Pipes network is no exception.

The Logistics Pipes system runs on an energy called LP, but there are no generators that generate LP.

Instead, Logistics Pipes has a power adapter called the Logistics Power Junction that converts EU into LP. Use a Basic Logistics Pipe to connect the Power Junction to the whole network.

The Power Junction can receive power from all 6 sides while a Basic Logistics Pipe can only connect to the sides in the 4 cardinal directions.

title: Handle Logistics with Pipes > Satellites! Wait,... They don't Orbit...
text:
Quest: Satellites! Wait,... They don't Orbit...
Quest line: Handle Logistics with Pipes

A buffer of 64 per slot is never big enough. Just look at red alloy ingot for example. It can only hold 16 recipes worth of redstone at once. You don't really want the items to just zoom around the pipes while waiting for the machine to make room... You want to have a big chest buffering items to be processed.

Introducing the Satellite Logistics Pipes. It provides additional input into the recipe incorporating it.

The pipe runs on a numerical frequency system, with the whole server sharing the number pool. This ensures that 2 separate systems can be connected to each other without conflict.

You can "connect" a crafting module with one satellite pipe by selecting the correct frequency of the satellite part. Multiple modules can connect to a single satellite pipe.

Satellite pipe inputs are the 3 gray slots on the right of the 9 slots of the module. Only items in the 3 gray slots will be sent to satellite pipes.

Note: Ensure your satellite pipe has any frequency other than 0. A satellite pipe with frequency 0 will not work.

Tasks:

Rewards: enhancedlootbags:lootbag:5; 5 × Coin "The Technician 10"
Prerequisites: Get Those Machines to Work

title: Handle Logistics with Pipes > Sorting Incoming
text:
Quest: Sorting Incoming
Quest line: Handle Logistics with Pipes

Now that storage spaces are organized and assigned, time to let the network sort the items for us.

There are 2 ways to insert items into the system

1. Use an extraction module to extract items into the system. It is slow, but everything that has a valid destination will be sent into the network.

2. Use a QuickSort module. It extracts a whole stack of items that has a valid destination. This module will ignore items that have no destinations other than the default route though...

It is your choice. Pick what you like.

They only connect to other pipes and don't have any item routing capabilities, but you will need a ton of them.

You can apply upgrades to pipes and modules, but you can't just access the upgrade menu by right-clicking the chassis with a wrench.

text:
Quest: Curses
Quest line: Hardcore End(er) Expansion

A Curse is a magical powder that attaches itself to an area of blocks, a mob, or a player, crafted using living matter, End Powder and specific ingredients.

It can be either placed right on a block or an entity, or thrown. If it gets thrown into a group of entities, it will have a chance to hit more than one at the same time.

Curses eventually disappear, but they can be made eternal by crafting them with stardust and an arcane shard. Eternal Curses will stay forever on blocks and mobs, and longer than normal Curses on players.

Curses placed on blocks are only visible to the player who cast it, and for a short duration to players affected by it.

Getting very close to a Curse makes it visible without having it affect you, but it requires extreme carefulness.

It is possible to remove Curses by using a Potion of Purity.

title: Hardcore End(er) Expansion > Enderpearl Enchantments
text:
Quest: Enderpearl Enchantments
Quest line: Hardcore End(er) Expansion

Enhanced Ender Pearls are a special version of vanilla Ender Pearls with one or more special effects (enhancements).

The way to make enhanced pearls is to right-click with End Powder in your hand to modify your ender pearl. You can continue adding as many effects to one pearl as you want.

These effects are useful when throwing the pearl, for pearl teleportation effects.

Natural occurrence:
It is possible to find pearls with random effects in a Dungeon Tower's loot chests.

Enhancements:
No fall damage (Wool)
Upon the pearl's landing, the player will not receive any fall damage.

No gravity (Feather)
The pearl will not follow the rules of gravity, which makes it possible to throw it straight up. After 10 seconds of flight, the pearl is automatically destroyed without any teleportation or fall damage.

Increased range (String)
Unlike the no gravity effect, the pearl will fall down due to gravity, but will do so 25% slower. If the pearl has the no gravity effect too, it will override this effect.

Double speed (Gold Nugget)
Increases the pearl's speed by a factor of 2, but won't change the flight trajectory. This can be helpful if you are in a bad situation (fell in lava, swarm of mobs around...) and need to be saved very quickly. In combination with the riding effect, you may notice slight stuttering on a server.

Explosive (Gunpowder)
Upon landing, the pearl will explode with radius of 2.7 (TNT has radius of 4). This will not harm the thrower as long as they are far enough from the landing spot.

Freeze (Snowball)
The pearl will freeze mobs and players within 5 blocks of the landing spot for at least 4 seconds. Just as with the explosive effect, this will not affect the thrower unless they throw the pearl close to them, or have the riding effect applied. This effect is also followed by ice cracking sound and snow particles.

Riding (Lead)
The thrower will "ride" the pearl to its destination. During the ride, if another pearl with this effect is thrown, the previous pearl will destroy itself and deal fall damage (unless No fall damage effect is applied).

Trivia:
The Enhanced Ender Pearls can still be used for crafting an Eye of Ender.

After the Altar creation is complete, a player has to place up to 8 matching solid blocks (of any kind) near the altar. These blocks require 1 block of air above them and no solid blocks touching them on the sides and diagonally. These blocks are the pedestals. The Dragon Essence Altar will project purple particles to all the pedestals connected to it.

Dropping an item onto the pedestal will place it there. After the item has been placed on top of the pedestal, the altar will start "infusing" the item using Dragon Essence stored in the altar itself. Adding more essence to the altar is done by right-clicking.

Infusing makes items repair themselves (this does not work for items that require Energy), increases the level of existing enchantments (up to 4 enchantments per item) and can even add new enchantments.

There are two items in this mod that can be obtained only by Dragon Essence infusion:

Enhanced Brewing Stand - by infusing a vanilla Brewing Stand, requires 20 pieces of Dragon Essence.

Temple Caller - by infusing a vanilla Eye of Ender, requires 50 pieces of Dragon Essence. It's disabled though, so don't bother.

title: Hardcore End(er) Expansion > Find all the Ores in the End
text:
Quest: Find all the Ores in the End
Quest line: Hardcore End(er) Expansion

End Powder Ore:
Generated in the End in between End Stone at every height level. When the ore is mined with any type of pickaxe, it will drop one or two pieces of End Powder.

Endium Ore:
Rare ore that starts to appear near Dungeon Towers, and gets more common the further you travel.

Igneous Rock Ore:
Generated in the End in the Burning Mountains and sometimes in the Endstone Blobs. This block emits lava particles but does no damage to the player. When the ore is mined with an Iron Pickaxe or better, it will drop one Igneous Rock.

Note: the Fortune enchantment does not affect Igneous Rock Ore. However, the Silk Touch enchantment does work with this block. You can get better output with a Macerator.

Instability Ore:
Generated in the End in the Biome Islands, especially common in the Fiery Mines. When the ore is mined with an Advanced Pickaxe, it has a 40% chance to drop one Instability Orb, otherwise it breaks without providing any items.

Note: the Fortune enchantment increases the chance of getting an Instability Orb by 4% per level, and the Silk Touch enchantment also works with this block. You can get better output with a Forge Hammer.

Stardust Ore:
Generated in the End in the Biome Islands. When the ore is mined with an Advanced Pickaxe, it has a chance to drop 0-4 pieces of Stardust. Even though this ore comes in clusters, two ore blocks from the same cluster can be generated away from each other, making Stardust Ore a rare resource which requires thorough exploration and mining.

Note: the Stardust Ore block has different textures on its sides.

Sphalerite: Often found floating in the open space around Endstone Blobs. You can macerate it for crushed normal Sphalerite.

The Spatial Dash Gem is used for enderpearl-like teleportation.

The Spatial Dash Gem uses Energy and can be charged in an Energy Extraction Table. Right-clicking with the gem in hand sends a purple beam straight to where the player is aiming. When the beam hits a block, the player will be teleported to it. Maximum travel distance is 75 blocks horizontally. The teleportation doesn't hurt the player, unlike Ender Pearls.

The Spatial Dash Gem always tries to place the player on top of the block, even if the beam hits the side or bottom of it.

The Spatial Dash Gem can teleport the player through 7 solid blocks in a row, making the gem a good way of teleporting through cave walls and ceilings. If the wall is thicker than 7 blocks, the gem then tries to find 2 air blocks inside the wall. If the air blocks are not found, the player will be teleported into a wall, leading to suffocation.

A Spatial Dash Gem is also dropped by the Ender Eye mini-boss upon death.

Once the charge of the Transference Gem becomes lower than 44%, negative effects will appear:

Deflection - the player will be teleported to a random location instead of the linked block.

Slowness II
Nausea I
Weakness II
Hunger I

Endermen - Angry Endermen will spawn and attack the player.

Item drop - a random amount of items in player's inventory will drop to the ground.

Storm - will cause a 2-3 minute storm. This is the rarest effect.

title: Hardcore End(er) Expansion > Visit the Infested Island
text:
Quest: Visit the Infested Island
Quest line: Hardcore End(er) Expansion

The Infested Islands are mostly a flat biome with occasional hills, long caves and a decent amount of ores. There are 2 variations of the biome - Deep and Ravaged. Both of these variations contain Silverfish, Infested Bats and occasionally Endermen.

The Deep variation is massively populated with Spooky Trees that can have faces on them, which are how you get Ectoplasm. The ground has all types of infested plants, including Thorny Bushes.

The Ravaged variation has patches of infested plants and occasional Spooky Trees, but the most important feature is the Ravaged Dungeon which is an open gate to getting your Charms.

About Infestation:
Simply by standing on the Infested End Stone, the infestation level will rise. After leaving the area for several minutes, if the infestation level is low, it will reset and won't do any harm to the player.

However, if the infestation level gets high enough, it will trigger one or more potion effects, which include weakness, slowness and mining fatigue, and if the player's level is severe, blindness, confusion and/or poison may take place as well. These effects cannot be cured using milk; however you can drink Infestation Remedy to shorten them.

title: How to Be(e) > A Stim a Day Keeps the Doctor Awake
text:
Quest: A Stim a Day Keeps the Doctor Awake
Quest line: How to Be(e)

Supporting circuit boards that can hold 4 electron tubes, the Electrical Stimulator provides a variety of functions. Use a Forestry Soldering Iron on an Intricate Circuit Board to set four slots worth of electron tubes. The tubes' capabilities are listed here as percentages:

Iron ET -> +0.5 Production
Diamantine ET -> +1.5 Production
Apatine ET -> 1.5x Pollination (Max 5x)
Obsidian ET -> 0.8x Lifespan
Lapis ET -> 1.5x Lifespan (Max 5x)
Blazing ET -> Simulates Hellish temperature
Golden ET -> 1.5x Mutation Rate (Max 5x)
Tin ET -> 0.4x Territory (Min 0.1) & -0.1 Production
Bronze ET -> 1.5x Territory (Max 5x)

Genetic Decay is also increased by 50% for all of them. This affects how long until ignoble bees die off, so don't worry about it if your bees are pristine.

Remember that lifespan is represented by ticks, not time. You need a world accelerator if you want a lifespan that is really less than 1 tick.

Breeder's Notes:
12x Golden ETs and 20x Obsidian ETs across eight of these will make a super breeding party alveary; it will spike your mutation chances while dramatically decreasing lifespan. If you have been using the oblivion frame in an apiary to shorten lifespan for breeding, then this *does not* replace that because you cannot use world accelerators in alvearies. title: How to Be(e) > Breeding Bees Into Oblivion
text:
Quest: Breeding Bees Into Oblivion
Quest line: How to Be(e)

If bee breeding is a dice game, then these are the biggest factors you'd control to win:

1. Fertility: How many dice you can roll each turn.
2. Mutation Rate: How good of a roll you need to make.
3. Lifespan: How often you can play the game.

The Oblivion Frame dramatically helps with #3 by reducing the bee's lifespan to the point that you can play the breeding dice game in one "tick" of 27.5 seconds. A bee with the "Shortest" lifespan trait cycles for 10 ticks (275 seconds), so you'd minimally cut the cycle by a whole order of magnitude!

You can find Oblivion Frames in Stronghold libraries. This is how you can get them in the early game for very aggressive bee breeding. Later, you can make them from Dragon Eggs. These frames are very precious and you don't want their durability to run out. A typical repair method is to use a Thaumic Restorer on them.

Wait, to find a Stronghold reliably, I need some Eyes of Ender, and that's an HV-tier Chemical Reactor recipe! If you happen to have a Large Chemical Reactor, remember that it overclocks perfectly, so you can crank er' up with a bunch of MV-tier Energy Input Hatches.

The Oblivion Bee Meta

The oblivion bee meta can be enough to breed most bees quickly. You could do the whole bee breeding quest line with it, but you can ultimately improve on it with Alvearies and genetic modification. What you need for this meta is:

1. An Apiary
2. An Oblivion Frame
3. Some way to repair the frame (typically: thaumic restorer)
4. A Beealyzer and a lot of honey

This is a hands-on process. You don't automatically send the princess and drones back through because you need to watch the oblivion frame's durability. You inspect all the offspring bees after each cycle and hand-pick which to try next after a pass through the Beealyzer.

You can accelerate the Apiary with a World Accelerator. Be sure to protect the World Accelerator and supporting equipment from rain! You can use glass or a breakable clear glass so the Apiary can still see the sky while the World Accelerator is protected. If you need to use batteries, you can use a State Cell to draw out a button pulse to the world accelerator so it runs juuust long enough for an accelerated cycle.

title: How to Be(e) > Droning On
text:
Quest: Droning On
Quest line: How to Be(e)

Both scale their requirements by the number of genes you intend to apply to a single Larvae.

The Inoculator

Run Time: 10 minutes per gene
RF Cost: 600,000 RF per gene
RF/t: 50
Bacteria Vector: 15 mB per gene.

This one has a lower power and recipe cost at the expense of needing Bacteria Vector, created by incubating Bacteria and Blaze Powder, to transfer the gene into organisms. The consumption for Bacteria Vector is quite low.

It is also slooooow.. 

The Splicer

Run Time: 1 minute per gene
RF Cost: 12,000,000 RF per gene
RF/t: 1,000

The Splicer is much like the Inoculator in function, however it has the benefit of not requiring any liquid. Its power consumption is terrifying compared to the Inoculator, but overall it only consumes twice the RF despite gobbling it much faster.

*or trees and flowers via their pollen, or butterflies via their caterpillars.

title: How to Be(e) > IAADDS
text:
Quest: IAADDS
Quest line: How to Be(e)

Aka the Mega Apiary.

It has three primary modes (change with screwdriver) and two operation modes (change with shift+screwdriver):

INPUT MODE: Does not take power. Put your queens in the input bus to put them in the internal buffer.

OUTPUT MODE: Does not take power. Will give your bees back to the output bus.

OPERATING MODE - NORMAL: The processing time is 5 seconds. Uses 1 Amp LuV per queen. All bees are affected by 64x acceleration and 8 Production Upgrades as well as a Genetic Stabilizer Upgrade. The IAADDS also simulates a perfect environment for all bees.

You can provide royal jelly to increase the outputs. 1 royal jelly grants 5% bonus per bee. They will be consumed on each start of operation and be applied to that operation only. The maximum bonus is 200%. The normal bee stats still apply of course, though the IAADDS is able to provide a perfect environment for any bee.

OPERATING MODE - SWARMER: In this mode you can only insert 1 queen. The IAADDS will then slowly produce ignoble princesses for 100 royal jelly per operation. The base processing time is 1 minute but you can overclock this process. The base usage is 1 Amp IV.

Yes you need thousands of queens, not princesses.

Prerequisites: Admit it, You Love This Pt 1 in UV; Bees By the Millions

title: How to Be(e) > Incubator
text:
Quest: Incubator
Quest line: How to Be(e)

The Incubator is a general production machine that serves two purposes:

1. Hatching (modified) Larvae into drones at the end of the whole process.
2. Heating items and liquids to produce different resources you will need in different parts of the entire research and modification process.

There are up to five different resources you can create from Incubators:

1. Liquid Growth Medium: Water + Growth Medium
2. Bacteria: Liquid Growth Medium + Wheat OR more Bacteria + Growth Medium
3. Enzyme: Bacteria + Sugar
4. Bacteria Vector: Bacteria + Blaze Powder OR more Bacteria Vector + Growth Medium
5. Polymerizing Bacteria: Bacteria + Bone Meal OR more Polymerizing Bacteria + Growth Medium

Three of the recipes can optionally be extended by injecting them with more Growth Medium instead of using a different ingredient. If you're able to produce a bunch of Growth Medium, consider "priming" incubators for these outputs and then switching them to use Growth Medium indefinitely in a feedback loop.

Enzyme is usually produced in a pipeline from Bacteria, which is in turn produced from Liquid Growth Medium.

Bacteria Vector is only used by the Inoculator to modify Larvae, and you don't need it if you use a Splicer instead.

PS: You'll also need a source for Ethanol for the Genepool and the Isolator. This technology line has a drinking problem.

PPS: Blaze Powder also comes up with at least Fluorescent Dye later.

Tasks:
- Retrieve: 2 × Genetics:labMachine:2
Rewards: Genetics:labMachine:2; enhancedlootbags:lootbag:26
Prerequisites: Welcome to Biology Class!
Unlocks: Growth Medium

title: How to Be(e) > Isolator
text:
Quest: Isolator
Quest line: How to Be(e)

The Isolator will take Ethanol and Enzyme to extract a single gene from a candidate bee. Sometimes it gets hungry and eats the bee too. Don't feed it any bees you won't mind getting destroyed!

You must provide a Blank Sequence to store the output gene. This will be stored with a "faint" level of strength that can be sequenced slowly, or made stronger to be sequenced faster by passing the sequence through a Polymerizer.

The exact gene you get from the bee is going to be a random choice from that bee's genome. You won't know what it is until you run it through the Sequencer. It will then be accessible forever in the Gene Database.

You can wind up isolating the same gene from the same bee multiple times. It's just bad luck. They won't be isolated in any particular order.

The Sequencer will drain the container back into a Blank Sequence, so you can feed them back into the Isolator. You only ever need to make a few Blank Sequences because you can just loop like this indefinitely. If, however, you have a sequenced gene and want to make it blank again immediately, then just run it through your smelting/furnace device of choice.

The bee you use in the Alveary should be whatever you intend to modify. It can be any kind if you intend to overwrite all the traits, but you probably should have it either be:

title: How to Be(e) > Making Bees More Comfortable
text:
Quest: Making Bees More Comfortable
Quest line: How to Be(e)

The Acclimatiser can widen the temperature tolerance of a bee. This is technically a little side quest with Binnie's Genetics machines, but these alterations are permanent and carry into their genome.

Note that the bee's species determines its favored temperature for jubilance. You can't use this to make a bee produce secondary products in a different climate.

Drones, princesses, queens, and even larvae can go in these machines. This means you can boost one queen and be set for life for that bee.

(You can also use it for pollen, butterflies, caterpillars, plants...)

When a specimen's tolerance has been pushed as far as it can go, that bee will go in the output slot. The typical thing to do here is pipe the bee automatically into another Acclimatiser like a little trauma conga line. At the end, the bee should be able to tolerate being anywhere.

Here's what you can use for what at what factors:
* Temperature down
  * ice: 0.75
  * snowball: 0.15
* Temperature up
  * lava (canned!): 0.75
  * blaze powder: 0.5
  * blaze rod: 0.75
* Humidity up:
  * water (canned!): 0.75
* Humidity down:
  * sand: 0.15

Fluid containers are consumed. If only you had a waxy substance in overabundance you could use for throwaway fluids!

The Ole' "Both Trick": If your specimen already has at least Up/Down 1 for temperature or humidity, acclimatizing it in the opposite direction will make it Both 1. The trick is that it'll now grow both ways for the price of expanding only in one.

So, if handling canned water and lava is annoying, and you can start with Up 1 for temperature and humidity, then you can just bombard it with temperature and humidity lowering steps. It'll switch to Both 1 and then eventually Both 5 without ever raising temperature or humidity again.

This lets you skip out on canning liquids, you sly dog.


Tasks:
- Retrieve: Genetics:labMachine:4
Rewards: 16 × Snowball; 16 × Sand; Forestry:waxCapsuleWater
Prerequisites: Welcome to Biology Class!

title: How to Be(e) > Polymeriser
text:
Quest: Polymeriser
Quest line: How to Be(e)

The Polymeriser is necessary to turn Serum into something you can actually inject into a Larvae. It has a bonus use of strengthening an isolated gene so it can be sequenced faster by a factor of 4x.

The Polymeriser requires Raw DNA and Polymerising Bacteria. Raw DNA is obtained from the Genepool, and Polymerising Bacteria is made from incubating bacteria with bone meal. Gold nuggets can be used as a catalyst to speed up the process. You can also make more Polymerising Bacteria by feeding it back into an Incubator with Growth Medium.

When using the Polymeriser to prepare some Serum for a Larvae, the result will have a number of "charges." In other words, you get multiple uses out of it. This is nice because you are going to need to make a bunch of drones if you are trying to get all those traits to stick. Remember that you cannot use this process to modify a princess or queen directly! If you are satisfied before you use up all the Serum, you can recycle it by passing it through a smelter/furnace of your choice.

It takes two minutes to polymerise stuff. If you already use a World Accelerator for sequencing, then the Polymeriser would also benefit from cuddling up with that accelerator on another side.

title: How to Be(e) > Production Frames

Quest: Production Frames
Quest line: How to Be(e)

You can make proven frames or purchase them from a villager. If you can't find a beekeeper, there are a couple of different options to get one. Rescue a zombie villager, add doors to a village to get them to make kids, or perhaps use a cupid's bow and arrow...

About magic frames:
They're the core of magically endowed frames. They also have a special ability - no maximum production chance. Normal frames are ineffective to get above 16x production (4 frames) but with magic frames you can keep going - just watch out, above 16x you'll be working your bees so hard they have a chance to degenerate into ignoble ones. This can happen any bee tick, not just when they die. Frames to lower genetic decay will lower the chances of this happening.

Of course, with very long lifespans, high production genes, swarmers, and tons of frames, you may think this is worth it.

Note that normal products have a cap of 200% produced, and specialties 100%.

title: How to Be(e) > Upgraded Home
text:
Quest: Upgraded Home
Quest line: How to Be(e)

The Bee House can be used to stabilize mutations, for example if you have successfully bred two different bees, but the passive traits are different from the active ones.

To actually breed those together to get a new species, you'll need something different - the Apiary. Building them will require a Carpenter and Impregnated frames, along with Seed Oil and Creosote - quite a bit of industrialization! Or, if you're lucky, you can find a beekeeper villager to trade with. Maybe you can help the villagers get lucky to make more beekeeper villagers? If only Cupid and his bow were around...

Production rates in an empty Apiary are low - lower than a Bee House by quite a bit, in fact. But the Apiary has two big advantages - Frames, and Automation. You can now use your Untreated or Impregnated frames in here to boost output - and the boost is multiplied. So 3 x2 frames gives you 2 * 2 * 2 = 8x extra output! You can also automate I/O for the bees and their products, though not frames unfortunately.

Bees also don't live as long as in a Bee House, but that's actually a good thing.

Also, you should check the Genetics mod for useful machines. The Acclimatiser can give very picky bees a much wider temperature or humidity tolerance without having to breed it into them.

Rewards: enhancedlootbags:lootbag:25; 3 × Forestry:frameUntreated; 5 × Coin "The Beekeeper 10"
Prerequisites: Impregnated Frames

title: How to Be(e) > Upgrading the Alveary
text:
Quest: Upgrading the Alveary
Quest line: How to Be(e)

These basic upgrades to the Alveary make it more powerful.

Frame Housing - Automation-enabled frame slot for the Alveary. Uses 5 durability every bee tick (27s). If it runs out on that tick, it has no effect.
Alveary Stabilizer - Prevents the bees from mutating into another species. Ideal for breeding traits into a line.
Alveary Transmission - Power input for upgrades that use power.
Alveary Sieve - Instead of the pollen from a bee fertilizing a nearby tree, it is stored here and can be manually applied. Requires manually placing woven silk in the inventory.
Swarmer - Creates additional Ignoble queens in hives around the Alveary. These are genetic copies of the original. This uses Royal Jelly or Aromatic Lumps. The latter are more effective.

Note that all upgrade blocks must be in the bottom 2 layers. The center block also cannot be an upgrade block, though the bottom center can.

When using power, the transmission block will suck down entire amps to fill a tiny amount. Use the EnderIO capacitors or something similar to prevent this.

Prerequisites: Alvearies

title: How to Be(e) > Welcome to Biology Class!
text:
Quest: Welcome to Biology Class!
Quest line: How to Be(e)

Binnie's Genetics mod will allow you to pick and chose traits for bees, trees and Botany flowers. But not for free! Doing this comes at a price.

Note: We'll be focusing just on the bees in this section.

You will need a few streams of resources you can automate into passive generation. These are used across the process in different machines for different purposes, but Growth Medium is a super-resource you can substitute for some of the steps if you're able to produce that in abundance.

The research process can be easily automated. Gene modification and drone generation can be automated, but are slow and infrequent enough that you will probably just attend to them when you need them.

The general idea is to sequence a pile of leftover drones until you get all the traits you want from it. You'll then have those traits forever and can inject your own combinations of everything you've found into drone Larvae to make new drones that carry those traits. Larvae hatch only into drones. You don't get to directly hatch princesses and queens, so you have to worry about these new traits sticking across generations.

These genetic edits don't let you create new traits out of thin air. They just let you pick and choose what you have already researched, and that has to come out of bees you already have. You may use this to set up all your production bees through the rest of the game, but traits like 4x fertility also help with breeding.

You'll want to prepare a lab workspace for this. The actual machines won't take too much space. In fact, you'll probably wind up smacking a bunch of them against world accelerators, which will require direct contact due to using Tile Entity mode. What will end up taking up more space is any passive resource generation you prepare to make the process more hands-free.

You will need an alveary with a hatchery to produce Larvae of the base bee you want to modify.

These machines require RF power. It's recommended to provide power to an Ender IO capacitor and power these machines with RF instead of powering directly with GT EU. You can connect GT EU power up to these, but you run into strange consumption from amperage conversion glitches, or machines not getting power despite looking like they have proper cabling.

Ultimately, you'll need at least 7 of these casings and could end up making 14+ casings for all the machines you may opt to produce. You will also need HV-tier circuit production. There is one EV circuit involved in the complete process too.

We give special credit to Three for a video explaining all these machines and their interplay:

An Early Game Guide to Genetically Modify your Bees in Gregtech: New Horizons
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EmhDlga2SCA

Note that he will rant about the quest book. That was--ahem--an older version of the quest book.

title: How to Generate Power > Force Plasma - The Mk1 Ending
text:
Quest: Force Plasma - The Mk1 Ending
Quest line: How to Generate Power

Once you have the two plasmas from before, fuse them together into a new one, Neon Plasma. If you were to use this directly, you could get Neon! There are other, more useful materials to get later in this process, so keep a lookout for those.

However, this is not the final plasma in mk1 recipes. To get it, you need to do the last activation step, which exists in all three chains, and involves adding a non-plasma related material, of the appropriate GT tier, to obtain the powergen plasma. The material you need here is Arcanite, one you probably have used before. This step requires you to preferably automate it with ABS, and have a steady supply of Thorium 232.

If you look at the last recipe, you'll see it's 144L Neon Plasma input to 1000L Force Plasma output. This multiplying makes it so that step, and all final steps, are the slowest ones. You will need 0.144 Neon Plasma reactors for every Force Plasma reactor, which means that 1 Neon reactor feeds nearly 7 Force reactors (6.9444... reactors, more precisely).

Once you get Force Plasma, this is the end of the mk1 fusion chain. Force Plasma is a 150M fuel value plasma, which means it has a 53.5% penalty with Infinity Catalyst in XL Plasma Generators. This is better than Helium Plasma with its 86.1% penalty but still not great for power generation. You probably don't need this in ZPM, but it'll be a stepping stone for your future progression.

title: How to Generate Power > Gas Turbine
text:
Quest: Gas Turbine
Quest line: How to Generate Power

A Large Gas Turbine is more fuel-efficient than singleblock turbines, and can have lower pollution output with upgraded mufflers.

You will also need a Muffler and Dynamo Hatch to complete the multiblock. Don't forget to use a Fluid Regulator, to control the flow rate into the multi! It can usually be an LV Fluid Regulator, since the optimal flow is much lower here than in Steam Turbines.

Each turbine material has a specific fuel efficiency (the higher, the more EU you get from the same amount of fuel), and the multi only reaches this efficiency if the fuel flow into it matches the optimal flow.

If you go beyond the optimal flow, you will get a higher EU/t value, but less fuel efficiency, and the maximum EU/t value depends on the turbine type and its Overflow Efficiency tier. For this type of turbine, tier 1 reaches the max at 150% of optimal flow to produce 112% of the EU/t, tier 2 reaches the max at 300% of optimal flow to produce 180% of the EU/t and tier 3 reaches the max at 450% of optimal flow to produce 252% of the EU/t. The closer you get to this maximum, the more fuel efficiency you're throwing away.

For the best turbine materials, see the spreadsheet and Large Turbine Calculator.

title: How to Generate Power > Harnessing Chaos
text:
Quest: Harnessing Chaos
Quest line: How to Generate Power

You've mastered antimatter production, but raw antimatter alone won't run your machines. To turn that potential into unparalleled power, it's time to harness the chaos itself!

Introducing the Shielded Lagrangian Annihilation Matrix!

The SLAM creates raw energy by reacting the Semi-Stable Antimatter with normal matter in a controlled environment.

Every cycle, the generator will react all antimatter and matter in hatches instantly, converting it all into energy directly. The EU output is based on the equal amounts of antimatter and matter annihilated. Therefore, imbalance between the amounts will waste your precious energy.

Depending on the matter used to annihilate, the antimatter amount gets an exponent applied to it, directly increasing the amount of energy produced from 1L of antimatter - this means the more you annihilate in one go, the more efficient it is!

The maximum EU for a cycle is limited by the capacity of all laser source hatches on the structure (limited to 64), even on wireless mode.

It can't output more than 9.22e18 EU in a cycle, or just below 43 16M UXV Laser Sources (If you're crazy enough for it)

The Formula and the exponents for each of the possible matters are:

Generated EU = (Antimatter^exponent) * 1,000,000,000,000

Molten Copper - 1.00
Molten Superconductor Base UIV - 1.02
Molten Superconductor Base UMV - 1.03

title: How to Generate Power > I'll teach you... how to Praise the Sun!
text:
Quest: I'll teach you... how to Praise the Sun!
Quest line: How to Generate Power

TL;DR: The casing amount in this quest is for the best Solar Tower, which generates around 2 LuV amps and is a major Stainless Steel, Titanium and HV circuit sink, amongst other things.

Have you ever laid eyes upon a solar panel? You might have built a few of them here. What do they all have in common, I ask you... they generate either Steam or EU directly from sunlight, and that is not efficient. There's something that everybody forgot!

Singleblock solar panels are best to insert anywhere that has sun, and provide constant power to a machine. However, EU storage and transport are easy here, so why not build something better? Instead of generating energy directly, send those warm beams of sunlight into a central structure with circles of Solar Reflectors, and bask in the eternal power of the biggest fusion reactor in the Solar System!

(If you end up making a bigger one, don't come arguing to me about this. Be quiet.)

The whole idea is that the energy of the Sun's rays is directed towards a fluid that can retain the energy, a Solar Salt that does it far better than water. The Solar Tower transfers heat to all the fluid inside it, but watch out! If there's too much cold Solar Salt inside, it will drain away all the heat and slow down the entire process.

In more detail, the Solar Tower has a heat value that ranges from 0 to 100000, and it only heats up Solar Salt at 30000 or above. The amount of heat gained per cycle depends on the number of Reflectors, but also the current heat value: this process is optimal at exactly half the maximum, so 50000 heat. To get a perfect tower setup, you have to slowly feed cold Solar Salt to maintain this heat value, taking away just enough heat to keep it there. I'll let you figure out what the flow rate is, given that it depends on how many Reflectors you have.

From there, generate Steam or SH Steam by heat-exchanging in the same way as Hot Coolant does it. If you want this setup to truly be optimal, do place it in your personal dimension for permanent daylight.

title: How to Generate Power > Incomplete Combustion
text:
Quest: Incomplete Combustion
Quest line: How to Generate Power

A chemical fuel engine for LuV? Well, if you are a crazy fan of diesel or benzene, you will love it.

This engine accepts all diesel, gas and also rocket fuel, although the Rocketdyne burns the latter more efficiently. It also needs Combustion Promoter to keep it running.

This engine consumes all fuel and combustion promoter in its input hatches per second and outputs power depending on the amount of fuel consumed, and its fuel value.

Its efficiency is determined by the Combustion Promoter/Fuel ratio. If the ratio is larger (there is more promoter), the efficiency will be higher. The max efficiency is 150%, but you cannot achieve this value without inputting an infinite amount of promoter. Expect efficiencies around 130% for high fuel value fuels like High-Octane Gasoline, unless you spend a LOT of promoter.

e.g. You input 100mB/s of HOG and 1000mB/s of combustion promoter. The efficiency is 149% and the sum of the HOG fuel value is 250000 EU. The output power will be 250,000 * 149% / 20 = 18625 EU/t.

title: How to Generate Power > Large Heat Exchanger - Fermat's Last
text:
Quest: Large Heat Exchanger - Fermat's Last
Quest line: How to Generate Power

The Large Heat Exchanger is a powergen multi that accepts a non-direct fuel, and doesn't output EU. What is it for, then? To heat up water with hot liquids, that's what!

Effectively, it's a Steam Boiler that uses fluids instead of solids, but it's more complicated. The three sources of energy are Lava, Hot Coolant, and Hot Solar Salt. The salt is the most powerful, but hardest to get. Lava can be automated from Everburn Urns or a myriad of other options, Hot Coolant usually comes from Fluid Nukes, and Hot Solar Salt is produced in the Solar Tower.

For Lava, the LHE outputs 160 L of Steam for every 1 L of Lava, up to 1000 L/s of Lava input (4000 EU/t at 100% turbine efficiency). For Hot Coolant, the LHE outputs 400 L of Steam for every 1 L of Hot Coolant, up to 800 L/s of input (8000 EU/t at 100% turbine efficiency). For Hot Solar Salt, the LHE outputs 2000 L of Steam for every 1 L of Hot Solar Salt, up to 160 L/s of input (8000 EU/t at 100% turbine efficiency).

If you go above these input rates, the output becomes Superheated Steam, which needs to pass through a Large HP Steam Turbine before the regular Large Steam Turbine. The maximum input rate here is twice of what was before and the conversion rates are now 1:80 for Lava, 1:200 for Hot Coolant, and 1:1000 for Hot Solar Salt. The energy output at 100% turbine efficiency is 12000 EU/t for Lava, 24000 EU/t for Hot Coolant, and 24000 EU/t for Hot Solar Salt.

Very powerful, but complicated, and needs turbines!

For more information, visit https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/Large_Heat_Exchanger or https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/Fluid_Reactor.

title: How to Generate Power > Large Naquadah Reactor
text:
Quest: Large Naquadah Reactor
Quest line: How to Generate Power

The multiblock version of the Naquadah Reactor works very differently from the singleblock versions.

It uses liquid naquadah or excited nuclear liquid as fuel and outputs the depleted fuel. You can see the liquid fuel information in NEI.

It consumes 2400 L/s of liquid air while running. Without liquid air, it will keep consuming your fuel without outputting power.

You can add coolant to increase efficiency.
IC2 Coolant: 1.05x
Super Coolant: 1.5x
Cryotheum: 2.75x
Tachyon Rich Temporal Fluid: 5.00x

You can also input boosters to increase power.
Molten Caesium: 2x
Molten Uranium-235: 3x
Molten Naquadah: 4x
Molten Atomic Separation Catalyst: 16x
Spatially Enlarged Fluid: 64x
Note: It will consume more fuel to match the output power, unlike coolant, which directly increases the power. The boosters work like 'parallels' for your reactor.

It also supports TecTech's Multi-Amp Dynamo hatches and laser hatches.

PS: This generator can produce up to 664 billion EU/t with the best coolant, boosters and fuel available.

title: How to Generate Power > More Advanced Reactors
text:
Quest: More Advanced Reactors
Quest line: How to Generate Power

Fluid Nukes, Vac Nukes and Wrench Reactors (lol), are more advanced versions of the normal one.

Fluid means you build it differently (with the parts on the right, it's a 5x5 cube surrounding the normal one), with the goal of producing as much hot coolant (cycle in non-hot) as possible, to use that to produce power. It doesn't produce power on its own, but more overall. Send it to the LHE to get SH steam out of it, then go through an HP steam turbine, then a normal steam turbine.

Vac nukes remove heat by sending it to coolant cells instead of coolant. Any cell in a cardinal direction will receive the heat instead of the reactor. Use a vacuum freezer to restore the Helium/NaK cells' durability.

Wrench reactors are when you fill the reactor with fuel rods, turn it on, and wrench it to reset its heat state before it explodes. If you can automate it, you deserve a medal!

If you still don't know what a MOX one is, it produces more power the higher the temperature, so you try to keep it heat neutral, and as hot as possible. Of course, this can cause things nearby to, well, melt. You use MOX or Naquadria fuel cells work for this. You can also get more Plutonium out of MOX than Uranium.

A breeder reactor is when you set up a reactor to get an item out of it rather than power, like Lutetium from Thorium, Plutonium from MOX, etc. Look at the depleted x fuel rod list in NEI or on the wiki to see more.

Since Fluid Nukes are liable to explode if you run out of coolant, make sure you set up a cutoff tied to the temperature or amount of coolant with redstone.

text:
Quest: Runite Plasma - The Mk2 Conclusion
Quest line: How to Generate Power

To complete this chain, you need to activate the Astral Titanium Plasma you have with a special material, also a GT++ one, called Titansteel. This is a considerable powersink, which is why the input amount is so low at 2L, and it forces you to dedicate an ABS at UV tier to feed one mk2 reactor running the Runite plasma recipe. If you decide to upscale this setup, the best option is to simply build a mega ABS, where you can also use EBF coils to save some EU, and in turn make the powergen chain more efficient.

Runite Plasma has a 350M fuel value, which leaves it free to run on Trinium XLs without penalty, whereas Tin Plasma has a 74.5% penalty on the same turbines due to having less than half the fuel value. If you want to upscale your plasma powergen to great numbers, this is an option, but the mk3 chain is probably the one to choose.

The same ratio of 0.144 to 1 reactors also applies here.

It will heat up over time until it reaches 100% efficiency, at which point it starts outputting Steam as well. You can then use Steam Turbines, singleblocks or multiblocks, to generate even more power.

title: How to Generate Power > This is Not How You Get Into Space
text:
Quest: This is Not How You Get Into Space
Quest line: How to Generate Power

This produces power out of Rocket Fuels. To see how to make them, look at the Space Race tab. These are specifically GT++ Rocket Fuels, and automating them for powergen in this multi will also provide you with endless fuel for your space travels.

The math regarding the Rocketdyne is complicated. Looking at the controller's tooltip helps, but the main gist of it is like this: provide Carbon Dioxide and make sure it doesn't run out, choose the EU/t you want to get, calculate the amount of fuel you need for the fuel you will use, and then provide enough Liquid Hydrogen to boost the multi, according to the EU/t value.

You will always want to have the Rocketdyne boosted, for several reasons. Assuming you have at least an IV 4A Dynamo Hatch, outputting close to the maximum on that hatch will lower the fuel efficiency, but not if it's boosted. Additionally, this multi doesn't consume fuel continuously, but with intervals of 1 second between consuming and not consuming, while generating power all the same. Boosting this consumption results in huge fuel efficiency, combined with the high fuel values of the Rocket Fuels.

Beware, letting the dynamo overfill can lead to an explosion! Be sure you have a place to output the energy.

- Retrieve (optional): 8 × Inconel Reinforced Casing; 8 × Air Intake Hatch; Turbodyne Casing

Prerequisites: Mallard Rust Smelly

title: How to Generate Power > We Need Big Toys
text:
Quest: We Need Big Toys
Quest line: How to Generate Power

All your little turbines take up too much space? Are you running out of water? It's time to solve these problems. This Large Steam Turbine can help you produce a tremendous amount of energy. It will also distill water for you, so you can use the same water again inside your Large Boiler. Don't forget to make a rotor for the turbine and put inside the controller, otherwise this multiblock won't do anything.

Each turbine has a specific optimal flow, the Steam flow that gives the highest fuel efficiency, the value shown on the turbine's tooltip. This is the flow you want to match, and you can use a Fluid Regulator as a cover to make it exactly what you want, but you can go beyond this flow to get an even higher EU/t value, at a loss of fuel efficiency. You can make turbines in 4 different sizes, with larger turbines producing more EU/t, but with varying amounts of fuel efficiency. Generally, Large is the best due to having the highest fuel efficiency and a good optimal flow rate

When using turbines, be careful of flow rates. To find the optimal flow rate, you divide the optimal energy flow rate listed on the turbine, by the energy value for the plasma. You can also use the Large Turbine Calculator (there's a link on the main spreadsheet, which is linked to in discord), or scan the multiblock's controller while feeding it a minimal amount of plasma to see what the optimal flow is. Make sure to use a Fluid Regulator set to this flow rate for highest fuel efficiency, or go beyond it to get more EU/t at a cost to efficiency, with Steam Turbines being the worst at retaining efficiency beyond the optimal flow.

If you go beyond the optimal flow, you will get a higher EU/t value, but less fuel efficiency, and the maximum EU/t value depends on the turbine type and its Overflow Efficiency tier. For this type of turbine, tier 1 reaches the max at 150% of optimal flow to produce 112% of the EU/t, tier 2 reaches the max at 200% of optimal flow to produce 133% of the EU/t and tier 3 reaches the max at 250% of optimal flow to produce 156% of the EU/t. The closer you get to this maximum, the more fuel efficiency you're throwing away. Don't exceed your dynamo hatch's maximum EU/t output, though, or you will have problems!

Use NEI with the appropriate long rod to find assembler recipes that will work for you. Or the spreadsheet. Long magnalium for small turbines, long titanium for normal turbines, etc.

Pre-moon, the best rotors are Shadow Metal or Vibrant Alloy.

Post-moon, the best HV rotors are Shadow Metal or Oriharukon (this is IV-tier). Luckily, turbines are now fully functional with multi-amp dynamos, so give those a try if you need extra amps!

For additional choices, see the spreadsheet and Large Turbine Calculator.

title: How to Generate Power > Welcome to the Plasma Chain
text:
Quest: Welcome to the Plasma Chain
Quest line: How to Generate Power

Hello there! If you've unlocked fusion, you can start this questline, but keep in mind that it's divided into three segments (the three fusion chains): one for each tier of Fusion Reactor, from Mk1 to Mk3.

There are more fine details surrounding plasma power generation you can access by using the following Wiki link: https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/Fusion_Reactor

These quests follow the process of creating some truly powerful plasmas that are useful for power generation at the beginning of endgame, when you've scaled up your setup to a Compact Fusion Reactor and XL Plasma Turbines. As you might have seen before, those huge turbines can go very fast with good materials, like Trinium or Infinity, but they will apply EU/t penalties according to the fuel value of the plasma used. This means that Helium and Tin Plasma are both much weaker there than they were in Large Plasma Turbines.

The end product of this whole process is Celestial Tungsten Plasma, which has no penalties even at Spacetime and can somewhat match what Helium Plasma would have produced, per compact reactor. The last step is the slowest, but, if there are no other bottlenecks, you can expect around over 8 billion EU/t assuming a single compact doing the last step with huge infinity turbines in a plasma XL.

However, getting there won't be easy. This whole process uses 15 fusion recipes in total, and a lot more material automation than any of the simple fusion setups. This questline will help explain what is simple, not simple, or possibly a bottleneck. If you complete this, you will be sustained in powergen until the Dyson Swarm, or whatever other option appears later on, and it will continue being useful later on!

title: How to Generate Power > Well, It Doesn't Produce Any Pollution...
text:
Quest: Well, It Doesn't Produce Any Pollution...
Quest line: How to Generate Power

This is a multiblock acid generator available at EV and above. It takes in volatile acids and bases to produce energy through a highly exothermic chemical reaction. These include hydroxides of various alkali metals, giving your LNE a boost of efficiency from 150% up to 500%! Using higher-tier bases also has a reduced rate of consumption, but producing them at a passive rate may prove to be a challenge.

However, you can't just get away with burning acids like that! Burning any acids will produce Toxic Residue based on the fuel value and liters burnt for each tick. Acids with a higher fuel value will produce more Toxic Residue per liter, but overall they still produce less residue than acids with a lower fuel value for the same amount of EU. When Toxic Residue gets too high, the engine will EXPLODE! (As compensation, the engine supports TecTech Dynamo Hatches)

How do you avoid that, then? Firstly, the Toxic Residue will naturally decay. The rate of decay is based on the existing amount of Toxic Residue and also acts every tick. However, it is not very fast, so you will want to boost it. This is done through robot arms as they can help clean the surface of the LNE. Using higher-tier robot arms and multiple robot arms can help clean it faster, though be careful as they may be consumed! The rate of decay and the overall capacity of Toxic Residue is based on the tier of your multiblock, which are unlocked at EV, IV and LuV respectively. Using alkali to boost your multiblock also does not affect the rate of Toxic Residue build-up, so make sure to select the highest tier you can get! Finally, Toxic Residue increases randomly, so you can use a Toxic Residue Sensor Hatch to help detect a sudden increase and automate your engine accordingly.

The Extreme Combustion Engine is an upgrade to the Large Combustion Engine, the IV version that needs Tungstensteel instead of Titanium. The structure is essentially the same, and it's almost a 1:1 ratio between the two materials, so this is a good generator when you've accumulated several stacks of Tungstensteel.

The caveat is that it only accepts High Octane Gasoline. This is the last and most powerful type of combustion fluid made from Oil, and it has the longest processing line of them all. As a reward, it has an excellent 2.5M EU per bucket, and you can burn it here alongside some Liquid Oxygen for almost 4 IV amps per tick.

The Liquid Oxygen is very important, because it greatly boosts the speed of the multi and the fuel efficiency as well. It needs 40 L/s, so you will need more than one Vacuum Freezer to supply it continuously: for an ECE that is always running, you will need a double Vacuum Freezer, 1 EV and 1 HV. You can run fewer freezers if you overclock them, if the ECE isn't working all the time or if you upgrade to a Cryogenic Freezer,

title: How to Generate Power > XL Turbo Plasma Turbine
text:
Quest: XL Turbo Plasma Turbine
Quest line: How to Generate Power

Is plasma flow making the turbines spin? No, it's just water into steam into water, all recycled inside, 12 times over. Check the XL Steam Turbine quest above for an explanation of the mechanics shared across all turbines.

This turbine, unlike the others, has very important differences to the regular multi that you have to keep in mind. Given that plasma power is so easy to upscale with the use of compact reactors, XL Plasma Turbines would have to follow suit and bring progression's EU numbers to ridiculous degrees, off one single plasma. However, this XL now applies an EU/t penalty to its production by comparing the fuel value of the plasma it processes with the rotor material it has inside.

See https://i.imgur.com/vifsk0P.png for various combinations of plasmas and materials. Mk1 plasmas are in green, Mk2 in yellow and Mk3 in red. The bottom 3 are the final plasmas of the fusion chains.

The formula is a bit complicated, but here are some important values:

-> Helium Plasma receives a huge penalty of 86.1% even with Infinity Catalyst, whereas Tin's penalty is only 53.5%, which means that the number of reactors and XLs with this material is twice the expected amount if using Tin Plasma;
-> Trinium changes these numbers to 92.4% and 74.5%, respectively;
-> Infinity further increases the penalty to 97.4% and 91.1%;
-> Spacetime sets these values to 98.3% and 94.4%.

This means that, at the UHV/UEV stage, you will no longer be able to rely on these two plasmas with your XLs. For 1-recipe plasmas, your best option is the mk3 Americium Plasma, which has an insignificant 0.8% penalty with Infinity. If you want faster powergen than that, check out the complete fusion chain that ends at Celestial Tungsten Plasma, which has no penalties in the XL Plasma Turbine and has total EU/t numbers compared to Helium's old ones. Check below for quests regarding the fusion chains.

title: Look to the Edges > Arthana
text:
Quest: Arthana
Quest line: Look to the Edges

An Arthana is a ritualistic knife used by witches and warlocks to both collect special ingredients and to perform some rites. It has the same general properties as a golden sword (damage, enchantability, etc.), although it has the durability of an iron sword. It is repaired with a Gold Ingot.

The main purpose of the dagger is to collect specialist ingredients used in witchcraft, and to this end it will dramatically improve the chance of a mob dropping such ingredients (e.g. Wool of Bat, Tongue of Dog, etc.). It also gives a small chance of undead dropping Spectral Dust.

When only using vanilla Minecraft with Witchery (and no other mods), an Arthana dagger is the only way to get a skull to drop when a skeleton is killed, the drop chance is about 5% (the skull is a key upgrade for an altar). The dagger even gives a very small probability for other head drops (from mobs and players). All drop chances are increased with the Looting enchantment.

An Arthana does not change the drop chance for Wither Skeleton Skulls, that will require the Looting enchantment as usual.

Some Circle Magic rites use an Arthana as a focus, the Arthana is not consumed in the process.

The other main use of attuned stones is to act as a portable power source for circle magic rites, when a nearby altar is not available. To act in such a way, the attuned stone must first be charged with a Rite of Charging.

If you haven't yet obtained a Mana Diamond, checkout the Flower Power tab for more information!

In the case of villagers, two (or more) must be hit by the same brew.

The Brew of Love may be thrown at a group of two or more enthralled zombies (created with a Brew of Raising or enthralled with the Infernal Infusion power), which will cause pairs of them to produce a baby zombie. It will also cause them to become zombie villagers. Zombie villagers can be turned back to villagers either using the normal method, or by casting a Rite of Fertility.

The Brew of Love is created in a kettle using the recipe found in the book Witchcraft: Brews & Infusions. Into the pot, throw a Rose, a Golden Carrot, Whiff of Magic, a Lily Pad, a Water Artichoke Globe and Cocoa Beans.

Wear a Witches Hat (and/or robes) while brewing to get more brews than just three.

title: Look to the Edges > ...Cauldron Bubble
text:
Quest: ...Cauldron Bubble
Quest line: Look to the Edges

The second thing you'll need is a cauldron. It is used to craft most of the basic items, like mutandis. It requires anointing paste, which you will need an MV mixer to make. It is made by placing a regular Cauldron in the world, and then using Anointing Paste on it.

To brew a potion, cast a ritual or create an item, the cauldron must first be filled with water. This can be achieved by using three buckets of water on it, pumping water into it using pipes, or by using a Dispenser containing a Brew of Endless Water.

Once a cauldron is full of water, it must boil. Lighting a fire beneath the cauldron is the only way for this to happen. Using a netherrack block will guarantee the fire does not go out, although if it does go out, it may be set to boil again without any consequences (unlike brewing in a Kettle!).

When the water is boiling, ingredients may be added to the Cauldron (one after another), to create the desired effect. The book, Witches' Brews gives a complete overview of all ingredients and what they can do when added to a brew.

title: Look to the Edges > Fire Burn and...
text:
Quest: Fire Burn and...
Quest line: Look to the Edges

In order to get started with your basic witchery needs, you need a Witches Oven.

The Witches Oven is used to get the most basic ingredients for your recipes - Fumes.

The oven is able to capture the by-products produced in the cooking process. Activating the oven to show the interface screen, you will see an additional slot to the right of the fuel slot. Clay jars must be placed in this slot. If there are clay jars present when something is cooked, there is a chance a by-product will be captured in one of the jars. These by-products are important ingredients in other recipes. If there are no clay jars in the oven when something is cooked, no by-products will be produced.

Upgrading an Oven

An oven can be upgraded by placing either a Fume Funnel or a Filtered Fume Funnel to the left and right of it. Each Fume Funnel will increase the cooking speed by an additional 10 percent (over a furnace) and increase the chance of a by-product being produced by an additional 25 percent for a Fume Funnel or 30 percent for a Filtered Fume Funnel.

A fully upgraded oven will therefore cook at 130 percent speed (compared to a furnace) and have a 90 percent chance of producing a by-product.

title: Look to the Edges > Flame Imp
text:
Quest: Flame Imp
Quest line: Look to the Edges

Flame Imps are demons strongly associated with fiery magic.

Not as physically strong as their dimmer cousins, Flame Imps are mischievous creatures who are very easily swayed with the promise of personal gain. They may even be bound into the service of a witch (or warlock) if the offer is good enough.

Flame Imps are summoned using a Rite of Summoning, and they are most likely to attack the first person they see. It is advisable to make a deal with them quickly.

Making a deal

To bind a Flame Imp into service, a witch must write the agreement into a Demonic Contract and sign it with their own blood (craft with a Taglock Kit).
This contract must then be given to the Flame Imp, who will require a down-payment of Experience Levels (typically 25).

Once a deal is struck, the imp will be bound to the location of the deal, not able to wander too far away. The Imp will attack anyone hostile to its master.

Imps like receiving valuable gifts, once suitably impressed an imp may be prepared to perform various flame related spells at the request of their master.

Spells take the form of contracts describing what must be done and to whom.
Simply craft a Demonic Contract with the necessary components and then the resulting contract with a taglock.
Then give the contract to the Imp. So long as the creature is in the same dimension, the magic will take hold.

A Flame imp may also occasionally give a gift in return for being given valuable things. These have been known to include the souls of demons that can be consumed to allow a witch to cast demonic spells.

A very well treated Flame Imp may even yield knowledge to summon a Lord of Torment.

title: Look to the Edges > Greenhouses on Mountains, Hell on Earth
text:
Quest: Greenhouses on Mountains, Hell on Earth
Quest line: Look to the Edges

You're almost there! To actually use the ritual, you need to recruit a coven first. Find some Coven Witches and complete their quests:
The means to control the dead -> Necromantic Stone
The beating means to master the infernal dimension -> Demon Heart
I must perform many curses, bring me the necessary brew -> Brew of the Grotesquex5
I desire to predict the future -> Crystal Ball
Or just fight something.

Once completed, they'll disappear until you need them. They will sometimes appear near your spawn point if you walk by it, so don't position it over lava or something, since they CAN die and reduce the number of your coven. You can have 6, with one extra appearing for Cauldron work. Consider keeping some extras around in a dungeon just in case.

After you recruit your coven, you just need a few things for the ritual itself: Spider Eye, Toe of Frog, Wool of Bat, Tongue of Dog, Owlet's Wing, Attuned Stone, and Attuned Stone (Charged).

To specify the biome, look in the Book of Biomes, and find 1) the type (Forest, Plains, etc.), and 2) the number. Type determines the foci used, and number determines the amount of Glowstone Dust used to get that specific biome. Make sure to pack up a ritual circle into a circle talisman so you don't have to redraw it, and bring some cobblestone to make a flat area (15x15, any height). Try not to do it at night unless you like dealing with infernals.

To actually do the ritual, have the ritual circle on the ground, the items (including the foci and Glowstone) in the circle, and right-click the center with the Seer's Stone.

The area affected is determined by the number of witches in your coven. It's 16 * (size of coven - 3) radius in a circular area, so 16/32/48 if it doesn't fail.

Unfortunately, sometimes after logging out and back in again, you may find that it didn't work correctly in specific chunks, this is (possibly) due to a lack of chunk updates and it not saving the changed biome ID correctly. Just redoing the ritual doesn't really help, you'll just get patches in the same places, however placing water after the ritual and before logging out may help with this. Or use chickens. Lots of chickens.

Also, if you already have crops in the area, they'll disappear until a block update or relog.

PS: To pack your circle back up, you need to bring an extra Charged Attuned stone and an extra piece of glowstone to get it back into the circle talisman, as seen on page 3 of Witchraft: Circle Magic.

The tamed versions also work.

Congratulations, you've defied the natural order and created new life! Hopefully they didn't run away because you created them outside. :(

Make sure to breed them for the next part. Use Raw Porkchop or Raw Beef for Owls, and Rotten Flesh for Toads to both tame and breed them.

For all your offering needs. And of course, it looks fancy!

An altar is created by placing six altar blocks in a 2x3 pattern or by placing nine altar blocks in a 3x3 pattern. You will know it's correct when a red cloth appears over the top of the altar.

Right-clicking on it will bring up a screen showing how much power the altar has collected, how much it can collect and its current recharge rate. It is important to check that there is sufficient available power to perform a given rite or use a distillery, or certain kettle or cauldron recipes.

The maximum amount of power available is determined by how many natural items are in the vicinity of the altar: dirt, grass, trees, plants, etc. all contribute; stone and sand do not. The important thing is to have a diverse mix of different plants, trees and crops (plants from other mods are supported to an extent as well).

Certain objects (or foci) placed on the altar boost its focusing capabilities. This can increase the rate at which the altar replenishes focus, the focus capacity, and the focus range. Only one of each type of item (skull, chalice, etc.) has an effect. There may also be other less savory foci that dark magic practitioners could make use of. 

 P.S. The 3x3 Altar doesn't provide any practical benefits over its 3x2 counterpart, however enjoy the increased ability to center it within your builds.

title: Look to the Edges > Probably Usable For Soup
text:
Quest: Probably Usable For Soup
Quest line: Look to the Edges

But its main purpose is to brew potions and infusions.

A kettle must be set up in the correct way before it can be used.

Firstly, a fire must be set under the kettle (netherrack is best for this, but wood will do just as well).

Next the kettle must be filled. You can use pipes to automate this.

Thirdly, each of the six ingredients for the brew or infusion must be thrown into the kettle, one at a time (the liquid will change color according to the recipe being used).

Finally, a glass bottle must be used on the kettle to bottle the resulting brew, this must be done multiple times depending on the recipe.

It is important to keep the fire going constantly while the recipe is being prepared, otherwise it will be ruined. Swirls coming from the kettle is a sign all is well, black smoke (and brown liquid) indicates the brew is ruined. When a brew is ruined, the kettle must be emptied with a glass bottle, or just filled with more water, and the whole process repeated.

When a brew is complete, the liquid will be the color of the resulting brew and will splutter (in addition to white swirls).

Some recipes will require magical energy from a nearby Altar before they are bottled. If the brew is bottled when insufficient energy is available, the brew will be ruined. Black swirls coming from the Kettle is a good sign there is not enough power. A kettle must be within 14 (to 16) blocks of an Altar in order to obtain power from it (it can obtain power only from a single altar).

title: Look to the Edges > The Easy Way to Change Biomes
text:
Quest: The Easy Way to Change Biomes
Quest line: Look to the Edges

So you want the easy way? Understandable. The only prerequisite is an altar with at least 5,450 power. Try placing many different crops around the altar and a Dragon Egg on top to boost it. Otherwise, the process is as simple as dropping the following items into the Witch's Cauldron IN ORDER.

  1. Netherwart (+2 Capacity)
  2. Tear of the Goddess (+2 Capacity)
  3. Diamond Vapor (+2 Capacity)
  4. Diamond (+2 Capacity)

  5. Optional, Glowstone Dust (+1 Radius)
  6. Optional, Blaze Rod (+1 Radius)
  7. Optional, Charged Attuned Stone (+1 Radius)

  8. Book of Biomes Page (Chooses Biome; Any Biome OK)
  9. Gunpowder (Add Splash Effect)
  10. Collect with Glass Bottle (Requires 5,450 Altar Power)

The maximum radius is 4 blocks, if all three optional ingredients are included. You may get more than one brew if you are wearing your robes/hat, or have a ton of witchery brewing expertise.

You can optionally substitute in a Nether Star for +4 Capacity in place of the Tear of the Goddess and the Diamond Vapor if you have the extra resources and want to skip the distillery-produced items.

For more detailed info, check out the Witches' Brews book. Click on Brewing, then go to the Brews: Step-by-step page. That should tell you what you need to know. To learn what each of the brews do, see the Effects page.

The spirit world is an alternate reality that mirrors the Overworld in topography. When people dream they often end up in the spirit world without realizing it (often appearing as one of its many denizens). Powerful witches can create Brews of Sleeping that allow them to pass their still awake consciousness into the Spirit World, leaving their bodies and gear behind.

The Spirit World is the only source of Wispy Cotton, Disturbed Cotton, and Mellifluous Hunger - the materials needed to make Dream Weavers. Also Brews of Flowing Spirit can only be made in the Spirit World.

Very few things can pass into, or return from the Spirit World - keep this in mind when heading there (Icy Needle always stays in the inventory). Wispy Cotton, Disturbed Cotton, Mellifluous Hunger and Brews of Flowing Spirit can pass from the Spirit World to the Real World but not the other way.

Two important things to note: Circle magic does not function in the Spirit World; and Endermen cannot enter the Spirit World.

If you got the Dream version instead of nightmare, collect at least 16 Wispy Cotton for later.
