title: Tips and Tricks > Moron's Guide to Better Trees
text:
Quest: Moron's Guide to Better Trees
Quest line: Tips and Tricks; Forestry and Multifarms

Forestry trees have a variety of attributes. Once you get a tree with a useful attribute, you can breed that attribute into other tree species. This way you can get an ultimate tree that combines all the attributes you want - including the type of fruit! You can also extract the genes with Gendustry if you can make the machines.

Please do your Forestry tree-breeding indoors or underground because butterflies cause lag.

Keep in mind that for quests, you will need to breed the species "pure", not a hybrid. You should probably save the crossbreeding until after you get all the good ones.

For faster tree breeding, enclose your trees so that butterflies cannot escape, and breed bees with better traits for area and pollination speed. There's also frames too if you can afford it. The sieve may also help if you want to do it more exactly if you can make an alveary. You need either bees or butterflies, trees won't pollinate each other.

Trees have the following characteristics:
Saplings/Fertility: chance of getting a sapling from a destroyed leaf. Good for making into biomass or other uses. Balsa, Gooseberry and Sweetgum are what you want.

Allele     Drop Chance
Lowest   1%
Lower    2.5%
Low       3.5%
Average 5%
High      10%

Maturation/Matures: the growth speed of a sapling into a tree. Important if you plan to cut it down right away for logs. Golden Raspberry is the fastest.

Allele    Time
Slowest  10
Slower   7
Slow      5
Average 4
Fast      3
Faster   2
Fastest  ?

Height: controls how high the tree grows. Giant Sequoia is the best, though it may be a little too large.

Allele    Value
Smallest  25%
Smaller   50%
Small      75%
Average 100%
Large    125%
Larger   150%
Largest  175%
Gigantic  BIG

Girth: the width of your tree. Wider trees have more leaves and logs, but will also need more saplings to begin growing. All saplings must be the same species and girth. The sapling in the NW corner determines the stats of the new tree, and is where bone meal must be applied to mature the tree. The Giant Sequoia is best here too.

Allele/Size
1x1
2x2
3x3
4x4

Yield: chances of getting a fruit from a destroyed leaf. Orchard Apple and Chili Pepper are the best here.

Allele     Drop Chance
Lowest   2.5%
Lower    5%
Low       10%
Average 20%
High       30%
Higher    ?%

Sappiness: controls two things: (1) the rate at which fruit ripens on leaves, and (2) the amount of biomass a sapling produces in the Forestry Fermenter. Each game tick, a leaf block with fruit has a probability of ripening by one step, and higher sappiness values correspond to a higher ripening chance. You can boost the Fermenter's output by using honey or fruit juice. Blue Mahoe and Red Maple are the best. NEI doesn't show recipes for analyzed saplings, and probably hybrids too, in the fermenter.

Allele     Sappiness  Ripening Speed
Lowest    0.10          1x
Lower     0.20          2x
Low        0.30          3x
Average  0.40          4x
High        0.60          6x
Higher    0.80          8x
Highest   1.00         10x

Allele     Fermenter Biomass (water)
Lowest    50mB
Lower     100mB
Low        150mB
Average  200mB
High        300mB

Fireproof: applies to the wood. Only the Coast and Giant Sequoia have this.

Effect: not used in trees, so it's None for any.

Below is more information on some other parameters:

Growth: Sipiri trees have Tropical instead of Light, can only be bred in a Biome with temperature 90%-190% and humidity 90%-200%, and can only grow in 120%-190% temp and 90%-200% humidity. All other trees just need light to grow.

Territory/Soil: all trees have Average, whatever that means. Probably something related to the below that never really got used.

Tolerates: if it can be planted on sand or not. Only Desert Acacia and Grandidier's Baobab have this. The trait is either Plains or Plains, Desert.

Supports: what kind of fruits it can theoretically have. Determined by Species. Only fruits from families listed under this trait can be produced by the tree, regardless of what appears under the tree's Fruits trait. There are a number of trees from the Extra Trees mod that support all 4 types, but none from Forestry itself.

Fruit: determines what fruit or nut it produces. Each fruit/nut provides different advantages:
Plum and Cherry Plum only produces 100L Fruit Juice, but have a 60% chance of producing Mulch in the Fluid Extractor or Squeezer.
Papaya produces 600L Fruit Juice, but only has a 10% chance to produce Mulch.
Coconuts produce 300L Seed Oil, but only have a 25% chance to produce Mulch.
Use a Forestry Multifarm so you don't have to break the leaf block to get the fruit/nut. Set it to Manual Orchard, and place everything first.

Family: Tells you what family of the fruit listed under the Fruits trait is: Pomes, Prunes, Nuts or Jungle.

title: Tips and Tricks > Moron's Guide to Breeding Better Bees
text:
Quest: Moron's Guide to Breeding Better Bees
Quest line: Tips and Tricks; Be(e) Breeding

First off, don't be scared by the massive amounts of bees you see here once you unlock the breeding trees. There's even more that aren't included and you'll need NEI to find!

Ha ha, just kidding - don't panic! The breeding lines unlock bit by bit showing you what you can go for next, mostly from the top to the bottom. The large icons represent particularly powerful bees. Many of the basic bees have multiple breeding options, only one is shown on the Bee Breeding Tree.

Bees have two sets of traits, active and inactive. The active one affects the behavior of the bee while the inactive one is only relevant for breeding.

Every trait further either Dominant or Recessive, normally respectively colored red and blue. When getting newly bred princesses and drones, check both sets in case you got the desired traits. You can breed the ones with inactive traits to try and make them active in later crosses. A Field Kit or GT scanner cannot see passive traits, you need a Beealyzer for that.

When breeding bees, a good idea is to settle upon a master template bee - a bee that has little to no crossbreeding potential but has all the traits you want - short life, nocturnal, cave dwelling, rain tolerant, humidity tolerance, temperature tolerance, 4x fertility, and so on. Once you have that bee, breed a bunch of pure princesses with those traits as both active and inactive. These will be your breeding stock.

When you are trying to get new species, what you want is a drone - this way you can use your "breeding stock" princess with the drone to get new species without the annoying effects or limitations. Poorly-crossed princesses can be returned to normal by crossing with breeding stock drones, or just thrown into storage if they now have annoying restrictions. Make sure you keep the trait and species you want, and slowly merge the good traits from your breeding stock. You don't have to do this part in an Apiary, you can use a Bee House to swap around traits. Remember that no species mutations occur in a Bee House. Ignoble bees are good to swap traits because they're mostly disposable - they have a chance to die after 100 breeding cycles, increasing slightly more each generation after that, though genetic stability frames can let them live longer.

Once you solidify your species, create a pool of drones. You can use those to convert pristine princesses to the new species. Pristine princesses will not die, but they can become Ignoble under certain circumstances like using tons of production frames. Rocky bees are a great source - all their princesses are always pristine, they have decent traits, and there's a bunch of them underground. If you have an ender quarry, you can collect them with that.

Turning two different species traits into a third species trait is a mutation. Merely turning one species into another is not. The chance of this happening is shown in the bee breeding tab, as well as the conditions. Bees can require things like blocks underneath their structure, certain moon phases, or other things nearby in order for the mutation to happen at all. Mutations happen across Active-Inactive and Inactive-Active pairs. So if you have an A:B princess that you want to turn into a C:C princess, you want to use an A:B drone. This crosses the princess' active A with the drone's inactive B, and the princess' inactive B with the drone's active A. This gives a shot at mutation for both the active and inactive traits for the resulting princess and drones.

A new bee mutant is considered "pure" or "purebred" when both the active and inactive traits are the new species. This is what you need to complete the breeding quests, but also to retain that species indefinitely. If the mutated trait only appears in one trait, the chance of it carrying is basic cross-breeding and not whatever was required to cause the trait to mutate in the first place. New bee species also have a set of default traits, and the new species will try to manifest these traits. You could start with two species that have compatible climate conditions and wind up with one needing completely different temperature and humidity. You want to encourage traits as you finish breeding the pure bee to get the other traits you want out of it. 

Ultimately, the species trait determines what the bee produces and everything else is fair game. All traits can be bred into any bee species, aside from the species itself. Species also determines the initial preferred temperature and humidity. Species require their preferred temperature and humidity to be in the 'jubilant' state and produce their special drops. You can also mimic this with the alveary or industrial apiary, but increasing tolerances will NOT work.

Advanced frames can provide useful boosts to mutation chances or lifespan reduction for faster breeding cycles. However, the excessive multipliers will increase genetic decay, giving a chance for a pristine princess to become ignoble.

A recommended early-game meta for bee breeding is to find an Oblivion Frame in a Stronghold library, and then a means to keep it repaired like with a Thaumic Restorer. This rapidly speeds up the turnaround time to turn a queen into offspring. You monitor the process manually at an apiary, and use any additional frames you can to improve the mutation rate. You can push this well past the point you can make alvearies, but there are alveary components that can further improve on this.

It looks complex, because it is! But it's also a lot of dangerous and useful fun!

title: Tips and Tricks > Moron's Manual for Effective EBFing
text:
Quest: Moron's Manual for Effective EBFing
Quest line: Tips and Tricks; Multiblock Goals

Welcome to the latest Moron's Manual, Effective EBFing! This manual covers common problems encountered when using the GregTech 1000 Electric Blast Furnace.

Setup
When setting up your EBF, make sure to place it a few chunks away from things pollution affects, like farmland. Pollution is nobody's friend!

During setup, make sure the center of the EBF is hollow. Sometimes things can sneak in there without you noticing, like a Thaumcraft light orb!

Make sure your muffler hatch is placed on a middle block. The EBF can't work if it is not spreading those delightful odors!

When placing your power hatches, make sure to minimize the distance between any generators and the EBF. Especially at LV, those few blocks make a big difference! Every amp of energy traveling over a cable loses a little bit - and you'll need as much as you can get! Your best setup is to put two generators right next to each hatch, with a 2A cable. If you're poor, you could use 2 battery buffers with 2 batteries each directly attached to each hatch. Make sure to top off the buffers' generators. If you make 9 slot battery buffers, you can fill them up over time to get longer running time until you get stable power.

Output hatches and buses will automatically push into tanks and inventories placed next to them such as chests or BC tanks.

When building multiple EBFs, the GregTech 1000 Electric Blast Furnace can share walls. This can save you on input, output, and maintenance hatches too. Not recommended for energy hatches!

title: Tier 4 - EV > Move the Heat
text:
Quest: Move the Heat
Quest line: Tier 4 - EV; How to Generate Power

Heat exchangers are a passive way to pull heat from the reactor or adjacent components and spread it out across a wider area. Their performance is measured in heat units per tick (Hu/t), and there are a few different types that all work slightly differently. Moving heat around is not enough on its own. Heat vents or coolant cells are required to actually dissipate it.

Heat Exchanger: Pulls 4 Hu/t from the reactor and 12 Hu/t from adjacent components.

Advanced Heat Exchanger: Pulls 8 Hu/t from the reactor and 24 Hu/t from adjacent components.

Reactor Heat Exchanger: Pulls 72 Hu/t from the reactor.

Component Heat Exchanger: Pulls 36 Hu/t from adjacent components.

title: Tier 0.5 - Steam > Multiblock Revolution
text:
Quest: Multiblock Revolution
Quest line: Tier 0.5 - Steam; Mass Processing

The steam machines you have been using until now have served you well, but there will be a time when you need to process even more items. That's where the so-called multiblocks come in. There's a variety of steam multiblocks available to you - go have a look at the Mass Processing quest tab!

This tab introduces you to a wide range of extremely powerful multiblock machines that can replace your old, worn-out singleblocks (and some that can replace your old multiblocks!). Many of these new machines will require you to handle additional mechanics and requirements, but it will be worth it!

Here are some terms you should be familiar with as you enter the world of multiblocks:

Overclock (OC):
Whenever a machine is running a recipe of a lower tier than it's energy hatch it will gain a speed boost at the cost of more energy usage.

Imperfect Overclock (aka. Normal, 2/4 OC):
For each tier above recipe machine will be 2x faster at the cost of 4x energy (2/4 OC)

Perfect Overclock (Often phrased as "Does not lose efficiency when overclocked", 4/4 OC):
Some machines conditionally (or unconditionally) perform perfect overclocks. In this case, the machine will be 4x as fast, but it will run at 4x the EU/t (4/4 OC), leading to both increased speed and no net increase in the total EU usage!

Parallel (Often phrased as "Processes x items"):
Machines which parallel act as if they are running multiple of themselves - that is to say, they are able to perform multiple of the same recipe at the same time, using the recipe's EU/t multiplied by the number of parallels. Machines which parallel will PRIORITIZE this behavior over overclocking, which is good for you! Parallels are more efficient.

Input Separation:
Refers to a machine's behavior when choosing inputs for a recipe. With Input Separation on, you must have all required items for a recipe in one bus. With Input Separation off, you can split item inputs of a recipe between multiple busses.

When working with multiblocks, if power is interrupted during operation, your inputs will be lost forever... careful!

title: Tips and Tricks > NEI Next Level Recipe Search
text:
Quest: NEI Next Level Recipe Search
Quest line: Tips and Tricks; Tier 0 - Stone Age

There are even more NEI search options!

If you are scrolling through recipes, you might have noticed the magnifier symbol on the top, left to the page number. Clicking it opens the recipe search field. A search term you enter here will filter all the current recipes to the ones where an input or output matches the term. An easy way to narrow down all screwdriver recipes to just the one from a particular material you want!

If you use "extended+" search mode the recipe search becomes even more powerful!

Here backticks `` are used around the search queries, but you don't need them when searching.

By default the search works like in the extended mode, searching in any of the inputs and outputs of a recipe. So if you search a recipe by `-dust`, it will return all recipes where there's at least one item that doesn't have "dust".

Let's say you want to search only in inputs. Put < before your search query to do that. For example: `<iron` returns all the recipes with "iron" in one of the inputs, `<steel@gregtech` returns the recipes with at least one item from any mod containing Gregtech in their name, using "steel".

But then, if you search by `<-dust` it still returns the recipes with "dust" on the left. Why is that? Because < searches among all items. So if there's one item that doesn't have "dust", then it would still match the recipe, even if the rest of the inputs are dusts.

To solve this, use <& instead. Like this: `<&-dust`. It returns all the recipes without "dust" among the inputs! <& sets a strict condition on all inputs, unlike < that sets a condition on any input.

To filter the outputs use > and >&. They work the same way, but allow you to filter the outputs of a recipe. So `>gold` gives you the recipes with at least one output with "gold". And `>&gold` gives you the recipes with "gold" in every outputted item.

Want to combine multiple conditions? Sure, just put them one after another in any order. E.g. you could search for `<iron>steel`, `<& -$dust < cell`, `>&-dust cell`.

Or even for `dust>cell`. Here the non-prefixed part works like default, searching among all items from the inputs and outputs. So this query returns the recipes with "dust" in one of the inputs or outputs and "cell" in one of the outputs.

In some recipes you might have items that don't belong to inputs or outputs. In order to filter them use `^` and `^&` respectively.

You can add spaces for readability too, because (unless you have space mode on) spaces can be used anywhere while in extended+ mode.

Prerequisites: NEI Next Level Search

title: Tips and Tricks > NEI Next Level Search
text:
Quest: NEI Next Level Search
Quest line: Tips and Tricks; Tier 0 - Stone Age

NEI search got improved even further!

Select a search mode extended+ to try it out!

Extended+ works pretty much like extended, but it doesn't support * and ? expanding in the names. Also the following symbols have to be escaped with a `\`: `-` (dash) `<` and `>` (less-than and more-than) `^` (caret) `{` and `}` (curly brackets) `|` (vertical bar) `\` (backslash) ` ` (space) `"` (quote) alongside with the prefixes that you have enabled like @ or $.

Examples: @Electro\-Magic, iron\ ingot, PB\&J.

Extended+ adds some QoL to your everyday search experience and an improved recipe search (next quest). In the following backticks `` are used around the search queries. You don't need them when searching.

Want to search for something without having to put a backslash before every other symbol? Use quotes! You could use a quote inside quotes too, but you would have to escape it. Like this: `"\""`.

Use curly brackets {} to group conditions. Searching for `{mytryl|manasteel} hammer head` would show you hammer heads made out of mytryl or manasteel.

Space is no longer necessary to use. So `{mytryl|manasteel}hammer` works too!

There's a space mode support, so if you want your spaces to work literally turn it on!

Quotes no longer require a closing quote. So you could search for `"iron ingot` and it would work! You still do need a quote if you want your quotes to end though.

Regex syntax got simplified (though the old one is still supported). Now instead of `r/some regex/` you could search for `/some regex` and it would work too! You still do need a slash if you want your regex to end. Regex doesn't require escaping, the same way quotes don't, with the only exception being the `/`. So to find a slash with a regex you would search with `/\/`.

You can use quotes or regex after prefix to search with them instead of a plain text. For example, use `@"chest minecarts` to search for items from the Iron Chest Minecarts mod. Or `@/chest minecarts` to do the same with a regex.

title: Tips and Tricks > NEI is EVEN MORE POWERFUL NOW?
text:
Quest: NEI is EVEN MORE POWERFUL NOW?

NEI now automatically collapses similar items into one slot making browsing much faster! To collapse/expand a group use ALT+LMB.
You can also create your own presets with custom groups!

Also now NEI has JEI-like Advanced Search:

@ - search by mod (@minecraft)

There are even more special characters that you can use but most of them are off by default (e.g. no need to use # to search in tooltip), below are all the special characters, check which ones are on/off in NEI settings.

Space is used as a logical AND between different conditions
# - search by tooltip (#UV-Tier)
& - search by id: (extratrees:door)
$ - search by ore dictionary ($ore)
% - search by subsets (%block)
| - logical or. multi-item search (wrench|hammer)
- - logical not. exclude items that match the following expression (-@minecraft)
" - multiple words wrapped in quotes are treated as one condition rather than several ("White Stained Glass")

Search Mode (apply on search parts, not full string):
Plain - simple string
Extended - allow only ?, * rules (by default)
Regex - allow full regex

In Extended Search Mode:
? - any character (@min?craft)
* - any few characters (@m*ft = @minecraft)
r/.../ - standard java regex (@r/m\w{6}ft/ = @minecraft)

You can disable this functionality in NEI settings.

You can add bookmarks with the A key while hovering over an item, also:
Hold SHIFT to bookmark the whole recipe
Hold CTRL to bookmark number of items
Hold SHIFT + CTRL to bookmark both recipe and all the number of all the items it contains

title: And So, It Begins > Numbers in the Corner?
text:
Quest: Numbers in the Corner?
Quest line: And So, It Begins; Tips and Tricks

What's with the numbers in the corner? That is the In-Game Info (IGI) mod. Some of the info it gives is useful right away, some of it shines later on in progression.

For now, the most important thing it does is showing if you are in an ore chunk. Further quests will explain what it means.

If you want to hide it, type "/igi disable" in the chat. Type "/igi enable" if you want to turn it back on.

The command "/igi config" opens the configuration window to control its position, scale, and size.

The command "/xu_tps" from the mod Extra Utilities toggles numbers to measure ticktime in milliseconds and the TPS (Ticks Per Second). TPS is a measure of how well your server is running. The ideal TPS is 20.00 (meaning a ticktime of at most 50.00). If your TPS is less than 15, things are going to start lagging noticeably. At 10 or less TPS, it is going to be hard to play.
The tooltip shows three types of measurement: instantaneous, average, and worst-case. Each one first shows the ticktime and then the TPS in brackets.

If you need suggestions on solving TPS problems, feel free to ask for help in the GTNH Discord.

While GTNH comes with recommended default settings, in particular when it comes to balance, there are many commands and configurations to customize your experience. They range from accessibility or debug tools to visual customization all the way to various cheats. You can find a small overview on https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/Commands_and_Configurations.

title: Tips and Tricks > Powerfail Notifications
text:
Quest: Powerfail Notifications
Quest line: Tips and Tricks; Multiblock Goals

Congratulations on your first EBF!

Throughout your GTNH gameplay you will end up creating hundreds of multiblocks, and will very likely run into a multitude of power failures at some point. 

Fortunately, we have a dedicated system for helping you stay informed of exactly when and where these power failures occur (though the 'why' portion is up to you to figure out!).

When a multiblock powerfails, you will receive a notification in chat, in addition to a visible icon on screen, and an icon visible on your map. 

You can clear these notifications by:
- Clicking into the multiblock that has powerfailed
- Deleting the notification in JourneyMap
- Typing /powerfails clear

For those playing multiplayer, anyone who is on your team will receive the same notifications. One person clearing a notification should clear it for all players.

This feature uses the same team system as wireless EU. Use </gtnhteam invite [Player Name]> to team up.

All of these features can be turned off in the gregtech config. If you want the on screen icon to disappear use /powerfails hide. For all in-game options use /powerfails help.

Quest: Power in the Ether
Quest line: Tier 11 - UIV; Storing and Transforming EU

These new hatches allow you to wirelessly store and receive energy from any location in any dimension. They can be placed in any existing multi block structure and will function as normal energy hatches. 

Additionally, the wireless covers can be used for singleblock machines such as a World Accelerator or a BioLab.

The wireless network can store a total of 2^(2^31) EU, far exceeding even a max tier LSC.

You can share a wireless network with others by adding them to your network with /gt global_energy_join user1 user2. This will make user1 use user2's energy when interacting with the global network. You can leave a network at any time by doing /gt global_energy_join your_name your_name.

You cannot connect wires to these blocks. These are also designed to be highly lag efficient, meaning EU is added at large intervals to prevent needless calculations from occurring. This will also save you some TPS lag from vast wire networks.

If your calculator is giving up, 2^(2^31) is a number with 646,456,994 digits.

title: Tips and Tricks > Safety First
text:
Quest: Safety First
Quest line: Tips and Tricks; Tier 0.5 - Steam; Storing and Transforming EU

For those new to GregTech, here are some tips and warnings about electricity.

Machines don't like being out in the rain, and will start fires nearby. Fires next to a machine have a random chance of an explosion. Also, sending a higher voltage than a machine's tier causes an explosion. Or several, if you pack things together, like many people. Sending more amps than a machine can use doesn't harm anything though.

Sending too high a voltage or too many amps down a cable will cause the cable to burn up and start fires, which may then cause machine explosions. Make sure the number of amps provided by generators and buffers to a cable does not exceed the amps it is capable of carrying.

A generator that supplies 1A can possibly feed multiple machines, if their recipes require less than the full voltage. For example, macerators processing ore only need 2 EU/t, so you could run several from a single 1A generator, as long as the wires aren't too long. Why does that matter? Because there's loss for every amp for every block, listed on the wire/cable. Note that cables are better than wires. But be careful! Sometimes a recipe needs a lot more EU than you expect, like a macerator sand -> quartz dust recipe.

Most machines only use 1A, however there are exceptions, such as the thermal centrifuge, world accelerators, and the UUM machines. Note that machines can accept more amps than they use (usually 2) in order to top up their energy supply, especially if they didn't receive most of the amp because of loss (mostly a problem in LV). The formula is (EU/t of Recipe * 2) / Voltage Tier + 1. Keep this in mind when deciding on cables.

Some machines are specifically there to help you deal with multiple amps, such as battery buffers, transformers, and diodes. Check out the quest tab Storing and Transforming EU for more on those.

If you want to send more amps, use a larger cable or a superconductor (MV+, but ULV and LV have their own lossless cables). You can use laser hatches much later to send even more. There even are wireless options, but not right now.

A single block machine starved of EU will restart progress but not lose the recipe items. A multiblock machine will lose the items.

Note that any block that emits EU has loss when doing so: 2 ^ (tier-1) per amp. So 1 EU at LV, 2 EU at MV, and so on. Using large numbers of battery buffers in a row is thus very wasteful of your power. You have to be careful with losses when making your first EBF later in LV, maybe rather power them directly? Of course, if you want to keep your amps topped up over longer distances, you'll need to place BBs occasionally to 'top up' the amps, though this is less the case the further ingame you get, as the loss becomes less of something to worry about.

If this info isn't enough for you, head on over to https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/Electricity to read more.

If you prefer to learn via video there are also great YouTube resources such as HamCorp's Electricity Guide: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lpDPY8J-4QY

title: Tier 12 - UMV > Sentient Overclocker
text:
Quest: Sentient Overclocker
Quest line: Tier 12 - UMV; Multiblock Goals

The Sentient Overclocker (SO) module is the sixth module of the Exo-Foundry, and the only one unlocked in UMV.

The SO module, as you might imagine, increases the overclock factor of the Foundry by 0.35. This means that for every overclock provided to this machine, it will give a 35% speed boost. 

For example, if your Foundry has 1 overclock it should run at 2x base speed. However with this module it would instead run at 2.35x base speed (235%). This then compounds if another overclock is added, so instead of running at 2x the speed of the first overclock, it will run again at 2.35x the speed of the first overclock, bringing it to a total of 5.52x speed (552%).

Additionally, this module can pair with the Proto-Volt Stabilizer (PVS) module to unlock "Harmonic Efficiency" giving the Foundry a 50% EU discount and an additional 0.1 overclock factor (2.45x instead of 2.35x).

Only one of these modules may be installed per Foundry.

title: Tier 6 - LuV > Turbine Time
text:
Quest: Turbine Time
Quest line: Tier 6 - LuV; How to Generate Power

Your fancy new Large Plasma Turbine will need a rotor to go inside of it. You can make it out of any GT material, but the best right now is NORMAL Draconium.

Always test in creative or the GTNH Power Planner (linked below) first!
https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1FTFdfmY_UWbTbFOyNzARKeI90pbHvPBH6M3JHJmaC-E/edit?usp=dsharing

When using turbines, be careful of flow rates. To find the optimal flow rate manually, divide the optimal energy flow rate listed on the turbine, by the plasma's energy density (EU/L). You can also scan the multiblock's controller while feeding it a minimal amount of plasma to see what the optimal flow is. Make sure to use a Fluid Regulator set to this flow rate for highest fuel efficiency, or go beyond it to get more EU/t at a lower efficiency. Plasma Turbines are the best at retaining efficiency beyond the optimal flow.

If you go beyond the optimal flow, you will get a higher EU/t value, but less fuel efficiency, and the maximum EU/t value depends on the turbine type and its Overflow Efficiency tier. For this type of turbine, tier 1 reaches the max at 250% of optimal flow to produce 158% of the EU/t, tier 2 reaches the max at 400% of optimal flow to produce 214% of the EU/t and tier 3 reaches the max at 550% of optimal flow to produce 301% of the EU/t. The closer you get to this maximum, the more fuel efficiency you're throwing away. The choice is yours!

For a lot of extra information on fusion, check out the new quest line called Powerful Nuclear Physics.

At this number, you'll be a lot less limited by the turbine material, and it's possible to increase the total power output of one Fusion Reactor considerably. You can cover the total Helium Plasma output from one reactor with 3 Plasma Turbines, if you choose the right materials:

Large High Durability Compound Steel 235% 473,759 EU/t
Large Atomic Separation Catalyst 206% 409,663 EU/t
Large Adamantium 206% 413,280 EU/t
Large Draconium 175% 220,500 EU/t (durable)
Large Neutronium 165% 249,480 EU/t (very durable)

The power output and final efficiency can vary a lot, based on which turbines you're using. Some of them, like Ichorium and Neutronium, last basically forever, while others will need to be replaced from time to time but offer higher efficiency. If you want to get more power per turbine, to reach closer to the dynamo's limit, you can increase the flow of plasma to the turbine, but be careful! You can't go beyond the dynamo's limit, and you will also lose efficiency as you increase the flow amount. More concrete values for efficiency loss can be found in the Plasma Turbine quest in the LuV page.

Also, check out the XL Plasma Turbine.

title: Tier 4 - EV > Venting Heat
text:
Quest: Venting Heat
Quest line: Tier 4 - EV; How to Generate Power

Heat vents are a passive way to remove heat from your reactor. Their performance is measured in heat units per tick (Hu/t), and there are a few different types that all work slightly differently.

These heat vents simply cool themselves after absorbing heat from adjacent fuel rods and heat exchangers:

Heat Vent: Cools itself by 6 Hu/t

Advanced Heat Vent: Cools itself by 12 Hu/t

These heat vents absorb heat and cool themselves much like the ones above, but they also pull heat directly from the reactor core to themselves:

Reactor Heat Vent: Cools itself by 5 Hu/t and the reactor by 5 Hu/t

Overclocked Heat Vent: Cools itself by 20 Hu/t and the reactor by 36 Hu/tSince it pulls more heat from the reactor than it dissipates, these are prone to melting if their heat is not balanced by a heat exchanger

The Component Heat Vent works differently to the other vents. Rather than absorbing heat and cooling itself or the reactor, it simply cools adjacent components (but not fuel rods) by 4 Hu/t

title: Novice Thaumaturgy > 3 Plus 4, Carry the 2...
text:
Quest: 3 Plus 4, Carry the 2...
Quest line: Novice Thaumaturgy

When doing infusions, it's always good to know how close you are in stability. The Arcane Abacus will tell you at a quick glance how stable your infusion altar is, and any asymmetries present. 

For now, you can have one in exchange for a few types of common infusion stabilization blocks- but if you need to replace it, it will cost you some circuits!

title: Novice Thaumaturgy > Comparing at a Distance
text:
Quest: Comparing at a Distance
Quest line: Novice Thaumaturgy

Comparators are wonderfully useful devices, but their need to be directly next to whatever they are comparing is quite limiting. If you could do so remotely that would free you from one major constraint.

Remote Comparators allow you to do just that. Sneak-right-click with a crystalline eye to bind the block you want to watch, and place the eye in a remote comparator to start monitoring the block remotely.

Given the extra distance, though the range of the remote comparator is quite limited, you should expect the tiniest amount of signal lag compared to a direct comparator. You're doubtful that is ever going to be a limiting factor, though.

title: Novice Thaumaturgy > Counting Items
text:
Quest: Counting Items
Quest line: Novice Thaumaturgy

The Remote Comparator makes it significantly easier to get comparator signals out of whatever block you want, but looking at your storage chests you can't help but see no reason to bother. So what if they're nearly full? You want to know what they're nearly full of.

Tally Boxes can be pointed at a container - either directly or, using a Remote Comparator, remotely - and given a Runic Whitelist that specifies conditions where you want a Tally Box to send a redstone signal. Quantity, metadata and NBT matching are options, as is using a basic name filter.

Note that the redstone side is always opposite the reading side, and Remote Comparators must be placed on top of Tally Boxes to work together, meaning redstone is always output on the down face in that case.

Runic Whitelists don't let you use NEI ghost items to set their filters, unfortunately.

title: Novice Thaumaturgy > Essentia Storage
text:
Quest: Essentia Storage
Quest line: Novice Thaumaturgy

At long last, you have all the tools to smelt items into Essentia, keep it stable, and store it for later use.

The last step was creating Warded Jars, relatively simple creations that keep Essentia in a quasi-liquid state, which makes it easier to keep Essentia from turning into Flux. Unlike phials, which must hold 8 Essentia exactly to keep it stable, Warded Jars can store anywhere from 1 to 64 Essentia.

These Warded Jars are safe to pick up and carry around, which you suspect will not be the case for most objects storing much more Essentia than these jars do. Right-click them with a label to filter that jar to a specific type of Essentia. Use a preset label if the jar is still empty.

Sneak-right-click with an empty hand to remove a label from a jar, or void the Essentia it contains if it doesn't have a label. Voiding Essentia from jars will not generate Flux, because... magic, I guess. It's very convenient, so just politely don't question it too much.

title: Novice Thaumaturgy > Keeping Out the Riff-Raff
text:
Quest: Keeping Out the Riff-Raff
Quest line: Novice Thaumaturgy

You're starting to get tired of having to build everything like some kind of fortress just to make sure no unwanted guests come in. Sure, that's just the nature of living in a world where infinite hoards of restless undead haunt every other dark corner, but is having a secure entryway that isn't conveniently door-shaped too much to ask?

Not anymore. Paving Stone of Warding, assuming nothing sits on top of it, will project a two block tall invisible force-field above itself that block non-player mobs from passing through, at least the common riff-raff. As a bonus spiders cannot climb the force-field, so no need for overhangs to keep them out too.

That said, since the force-field cannot tell an arrow fired by you from one fired at you, mundane objects will still pass through regardless. And the force-field does as much to block line of sight as the term invisible would suggest.

Of course, you're not concerned about that part. Being able to shoot things with your crossbow while they can't reach you is very much in your favor, all told.

title: Novice Thaumaturgy > Scanning Made Easy
text:
Quest: Scanning Made Easy
Quest line: Novice Thaumaturgy

We get it; The early-game of Thaumcraft requires a lot of research and you don't want to throw every one of your 1000 items on the ground and scan them for aspects. That's why we added 2 cool QoL features which makes this tedious task very quick and easy.

1. You don't actually have to throw the item on the ground. You can scan it directly from your inventory! Simply hover your Thaumometer over the item you want to scan, and after a short duration it will be scanned.

2. You've probably accumulated dozens of double chests full of junk that you don't want to sift through and scan, so there's a second feature now: Scanning entire chests! Simply shift right-click while hovering over a chest with your thaumometer and it'll scan EVERY item inside of the chest. Though before you can do so you have to learn a bit more about deconstruction in the Thaumonomicon.

Hint: To unlock the research to scan entire chests, go to your Thaumonomicon, open "Basic Information" (the first tab), and complete this research path: Research -> Research Expertise -> Deconstruction Table -> Container Scanning.

Or you can EBF it after your EBF is done. Remember that the Sulfur Dioxide you get is based on your muffler tier. This is probably easier than searching in the Nether for Cobalt.

title: Novice Thaumaturgy > Taint Warnings
text:
Quest: Taint Warnings
Quest line: Novice Thaumaturgy

Now that you have started using Vis in the form of Essentia, a warning about Taint.

Vis in the state of Essentia is unstable if not stored properly. Left alone too long, or emptied out of the Crucible, Essentia will break down. But not into Vis. Rather, it will turn into Flux.

Flux manifests as a liquid or a gas, but is, itself, only a nuisance. Thaumaturges exposed to the stuff can end up getting Flux Flue, a condition which makes it harder to channel Vis, but it is only temporary.

Larger concentrations of Flux will solidify into Thaumic Slimes, bizarre creatures that try to merge with each other to grow larger. They can be dangerous, but are no less susceptible to crossbow bolts than most things.

However, if too much flux is allowed to linger for too long, it will corrupt the land and solidify into tendrils. This is a manifestation of the blight called Taint. Fibrous Tendrils (as well as condensed blocks thereof) spread the Tainted Lands, feeding on the magic it twists. Nodes are especially vulnerable, becoming Tainted themselves if exposed to this twisted magic.

Destroying the tendrils stops the spread, but unless all are destroyed this is only temporary. A more effective solution is to destroy the Tainted Land itself, as outside this specific biome tendrils quickly starve and die off.

If you are exceedingly careless with your Crucible you can, in fact, create Tainted Lands. So you would be wise to try wasting as little Essentia as possible, and clean up any you do waste.

title: Novice Thaumaturgy > Tube Madness
text:
Quest: Tube Madness
Quest line: Novice Thaumaturgy

So you want to move essentia from your Alchemical furnace to your warded Jars without getting it all gunked up with different essentia types?

Well you came to the right place, with the use of buffered tubes and your handy wand you can move your essentia in tubes to fill all your jars without having to manually break and replace one jar at a time.

To create a simple setup place the buffered tubes in a main line from your Arcane Alembic with tubes coming out of the main buffered tube line. These standard tubes will then go directly into a warded jar. To get the essentia to flow correctly into the buffered tubes, shift-right-click the output side of the buffered tube with your wand until it is red. This will change the band to a red band which will limit the suction of the Essentia.

The Essentia will be forced from the buffered tube to a normal tube then into your Warded jars. Chain your buffered tubes as needed until all your Warded Jars will fit.

Note: This system will get gunked up with essentia if any of your Warded Jars are full!

If you would like more information please check out the guide 'A Thaumaturge Guide to Laying Pipe' by xlstadal for more in-depth Thaumcraft 4 Tube knowledge.

title: Novice Thaumaturgy > Understanding Wand Progression
text:
Quest: Understanding Wand Progression
Quest line: Novice Thaumaturgy

More advanced Thaumcraft recipes require larger and larger amounts of vis that your initial wands can't handle. You need to progress bit by bit to increase your capabilities. The progression is two-fold:

First, you need to craft more advanced wands, the Greatwood Wand is next. And secondly, you need to improve your crafting discounts. They reduce the vis cost of crafts and thus also let you craft higher vis recipes.

In your progression you will need to rely on both aspects. Better wands and higher discounts. However, as you progress, there are many different ways on how to proceed. Some ways focus more on discounts, others more on wands. Therefore, the questbook can only give you some general advice.

For example, when making a new wand type, it is always cheapest to first make it with iron caps and then try to improve it afterwards. One way you can improve your wand is by swapping the cores & caps for higher tiers as you unlock them (see "Substitution" research). However, if you are able to obtain enough discounts you can directly make the wand with gold caps or better, skipping the iron capped wand altogether.

But before all these options really open up, let us work on that Greatwood Wand!

Prerequisites: Improving Your Wand

Thaumcraft offers considerable power from its devices and tools. But power comes with a price.... That price is represented by Warp: A corruption of the character's mind and soul, inflicting progressively more dire effects upon them.

While the effects of warp can range from annoying to deadly, accumulating enough of it can also grant you access to greater power... at the cost of increasing madness, and attention from dark powers. At least, others may call it madness... but is it truly insanity, when the voices in your head grant useful knowledge?

Warp Theory adds a bunch of new Warp Effects to the Player. Be very careful because you don't want to spawn a Wither in your base.

If you're still early on in your thaumcraft journey, Warp shouldn't be something that scares you away from progressing further. title: Paying the Highest Price > Convocation of the Damned
text:
Quest: Convocation of the Damned
Quest line: Paying the Highest Price

Time to open a portal to the Demonic Realm. What could possibly go wrong? (It's recommended to do this ritual in a space dimension, as the demon city spreads up to 1000x1000 blocks)

You should also be starting the ritual from the ground rather than in the air for the best results!

Requirements:
- 15M LP (Archmage Blood Orb and >= 13 Runes of the Orb)
- 8 Crystal Belljars (one filled with each of: magicales, potentia, incendium, terrae, tenebrae, sanctus, aether, and aquasalus)
- 1 Sacrifice (Bottle a lesser demon/elemental in a soul vial)
- 1 Master Ritual Stone, 128 Ritual Stones, and 1 Blood Altar
- 1 Awakened Activation Crystal

Steps to the Ritual:
1. Use a Ritual Diviner to place all the Ritual Stones.
2. Place the Belljars atop the 8 pillars surrounding the center.
3. Link the Belljars to the Master Ritual Stone.
4. Place the Blood Altar on top of the Master Ritual Stone.
5. Start the ritual with the Awakened Activation Crystal.
6. The Belljars are drained of their reagents.
7. Kill the lesser demon/elemental with a Dagger of Sacrifice.
8. The Demon Portal is opened.

For more details and images, visit https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/Convocation_of_the_Damned

The OW is now blacklisted for the portal. Too many people did not follow the recommendation and servers suffered for it. It also does not work well in the Personal Dimension.

title: Paying the Highest Price > Incense Crucible
text:

Quest line: Paying the Highest Price

The forefather of the 1.12.2 Incense Altar.

Each incense is meant to be tiered one after another. Currently you can only use Wood Ash and Byrrus (Red).

White smoke will come out when there is an incense in the crucible, and the crucible will light up when it finds a player to increase the incense value of.
Once the player has an incense value greater than 0, their sacrificial knife will get super-charged, allowing the player to completely sacrifice all of their hearts but one.

Putting Wood Ash in the crucible will increase the incense value from 0 to 400.
Byrrus increases it from 400 to 800. It cannot get you from 0 to 800 alone.

The LP you get from self-sacrifice will get a boost depending on your Incense Value.

LP = 200LP * HeartSacrificed * IncenseModifier

IncenseModifier = 1 + IncenseValue * 0.001

title: Paying the Highest Price > Ritual of Gaia's Transformation
text:
Quest: Ritual of Gaia's Transformation
Quest line: Paying the Highest Price

The Ritual of Gaia's Transformation is the Blood Magic way of changing biomes. It consists of 116 Ritual Stones, including the Dusk ones, and requires an Awakened Activation Crystal.

To use the ritual, simply activate it, and it will transform an area up to 21x21.

If you want to change the biome you get from the ritual, use Arcane Plinths. The ritual starts from 0.5 humidity and 0.5 temperature, then consumes the items placed on the plinths to increase or decrease those values. It also starts by assuming a range of 0.1 is acceptable in both directions.

The items that modify these values are as follows:
- Sand -> Humidity -0.1
- Sandstone -> Humidity -0.2
- Netherrack -> Humidity -0.4
- Lapis -> Humidity +0.1
- Water Bucket -> Humidity +0.2
- Lapis Block -> Humidity +0.4
- Coal -> Temperature +0.1
- Coal Block -> Temperature +0.2
- Lava Bucket -> Temperature +0.4
- Snowball -> Temperature -0.1
- Snow Block -> Temperature -0.2
- Ice Block -> Temperature -0.4

Once you have used the items to reach your desired environment, the ritual will give you a biome from it. If there are multiple biomes with that humidity and temperature, you can use wool to determine the exact one, for up to 17 conflicting biomes. If the ritual cannot find a valid biome, it will default to Plains.

Some cool ones include, but are not limited to:
- Sky (also known as End) -> Orange Wool
- Eldritch -> Cyan Wool
- Eerie -> Light Gray Wool
- TF Forest -> Pink Wool
- Sacred Springs -> Yellow Wool
- Tainted Land -> Purple or Blue Wool
- Moon -> 0% Humidity, No Wool
- Mars Flat -> 0% Humidity, White Wool
- Asteroids -> 0% Humidity, Orange Wool
- Space -> 0% Humidity, Magenta Wool
- Toxic Everglades -> 70% Humidity, No Wool

For the biome change to show up properly on the client, you may need to relog.

Tin Plasma is worth using, of course, but the Molecular Transformer recipe to convert Silver to Tin isn't available in the singleblock anymore, so you might want the easier option, since you're rocking two reactors and all. With the 2x overclock they still produce millions of EU/t with the right Plasma Turbines, assuming you have them ready.

If you want to continue expanding, you can look at the Mk2 fusion chain that ends at Runite Plasma. This process uses Force Plasma from the Mk1 fusion chain, so it needs those 5 fusion recipes, plus another 5. Despite being an extremely powerful powergen option, it's unlikely you need something in this scale right now. Keep in mind, however, that you might need it in UHV or UEV.

The solution for this is a GT cover. The Robot Arm does the same action of moving items around as the Conveyor, but it moves to specific slots. title: Powerful Nuclear Physics > Basis for All Reactors
text:
Quest: Basis for All Reactors
Quest line: Powerful Nuclear Physics

Nuclear energy is first available in EV. However, it comes in all shapes and forms, and it can be hard to choose one kind of setup to use amongst all of those that are available. To start this questbook page, this first quest will be a summary of how nuclear power can be produced, and when it is available. Other quests down the line will have more details about each specific setup, but this is an overview of all of them.

The first nuclear source you have access to is the Industrialcraft 2 Nuclear Reactor, usually called a nuke. It's a small singleblock that can have additional chambers attached to it to make a multiblock structure, and the amount of chambers decides the amount of space available for the nuke's components. Inside it, fuel rods with radioactive materials generate power, and every other item serves to control the temperature of the reactor and keep it from exploding. It generates EU directly, but it can be upgraded to a fluid nuke, which outputs hot coolant instead, for the Large Heat Exchanger, but with more efficiency. Lastly, there's also the vacuum nuke, which is very similar to regular nukes but it cools down by using Coolant Cells, which wear out and are only reusable by using Vacuum Freezers. Usual fuels for all of these are Thorium, in EV, and Uranium, in IV.

Between IV and LuV, there's another kind of reactor, the Liquid Fluoride Thorium Reactor (LFTR). In this large multi, the Thorium and Uranium are mixed with very hot, molten salts (which need to be prepared in another multi), improving the power generation at the cost of additional processing. It's an expensive setup, but the depleted fuel can be recycled into many more byproducts than usual, especially at LuV, where you can get almost all the noble gases amongst other things, alongside huge amounts of power.

At those same tiers (albeit mostly for LuV and above), there are also two larger multis, the Thorium High Temperature Reactor (THTR) and the High Temperature Gas-cooled Reactor (HTGR). The THTR is mostly for power, needing an input of about 0.5 IV amps and outputting LuV power at a varied amount of amps, whereas the HTGR is a breeder reactor, outputting 1/20 the amount of hot coolant, which is where the power generation comes from, but with much better ratios for breeding into Lutetium and other elements.

Another kind of nuclear reactor is the Good Generators Naquadah Reactor, which coincidentally has recipes to consume Thorium Liquid Fuel and Uranium Liquid Fuel, alongside the several types of Naquadah fuel that exist. With these two, this reactor can process those elements much faster than regular nukes, which is helpful for power and for breeding, but it requires more processing until those fuels are ready to be consumed. Additionally, there are fuel rods for the IC2 nukes that use different Thorium and Uranium fuels, more or less related to these.

In LuV and beyond, there's also fusion power. The infamous GregTech Fusion Reactors work by fusing two elements into a new one, which is often a required step for progression, but they also turn the power they require into exponentially more in the way of plasma. Helium and Tin Plasma are some of the most used for power, and putting them into Plasma Turbines is an excellent source of power for lategame, in ZPM to UEV and so on. There are 5 tiers to the regular Fusion Reactors, but there is also compact fusion and some other kinks to fusion that you might explore later on.

This page will mostly serve to guide you into making a choice between all of these possibilities. It's pretty much guaranteed that you'll use at least 2-3 of these setups, so try to get comfortable with these quest descriptions.

- Tick the checkbox
Prerequisites: Tier 4 (EV)
Unlocks: Build the Assembly Line First; Improved Fission; Thorium as Early Power

title: Powerful Nuclear Physics > Bismuth Plasma For Soldering
text:
Quest: Bismuth Plasma For Soldering
Quest line: Powerful Nuclear Physics

Who in their right mind would use a plasma to solder things together? That's mental. Well, all the progression at this point is mental, that's all there is to it.

It's not directly with the plasma, though. It is once again about the Mutated Living Solder, and now its fluid inputs: Tin Plasma and Bismuth Plasma. These are the two main components of the previous solders, and that's the reason they're needed now. Tin Plasma is t2 fusion, and you might have already made a lot of it to generate power, but Bismuth Plasma is t3, with the inputs being Zinc Plasma and Molten Tantalum, which is actually Tritium, Copper and Tantalum in the end.

The recipes are cheap in power, you just have to make sure the inputs are there. Tritium can be centrifuged from Deuterium, which itself can be centrifuged from Hydrogen Gas, and the other two inputs are easy. You will need 18000L of each plasma for 40000L of the solder, or almost half the amount for each.

title: Powerful Nuclear Physics > Can We Get Uranium Here?
text:
Quest: Can We Get Uranium Here?
Quest line: Powerful Nuclear Physics

Yes, you can. In fact, you can get it much earlier than EV, but the speed at which you get it can vary wildly, depending on how you approach this problem. Uranium is the main upgrade to Thorium in nukes, with a lot more power to give and a different useful breeding byproduct, but you need about 3 stacks of Uranium 238 to set up the most powerful basic IC2 Uranium Nuke.

How do you get it, though? The one answer is, you get it from Thorium. Looking at NEI, the Thorium ore processing has a chance to give Uranium dusts, which you can use as fuel, but this happens very slowly, especially considering that Thorium is a rare ore in the Nether, even if each ore block gives 4 crushed dust. The reality seems to be that fast Uranium only happens when you can mine from t2 planets, but this is not the only way. There is a secret, and this secret involves CropsNH.

How does it work? Well, it's simple. The CropsNH crop that corresponds to Thorium, the God of Thunder, can quadruple each Crushed Thorium Ore into 4 Purified Thorium Ore, but it also outputs, in fluid form, one Uranium Ingot! This means that each Thorium Ore gives you 4 Uranium Ingots, and with around 42 ore, you can do one cycle of that big reactor setup. God of Thunder needs the ore under it, though, so make sure you save some for that purpose.

EV Uranium nukes are an achievement intended mostly for crop users, so this quest won't demand something like that. Still, it's a useful secret, so here it is. Additionally, the Uranium crop quest in the questbook awards you with 32 Pitchblende when you complete it, which might prove useful for both for quadrupling Uranium and getting Radium for Radon!

Tasks:
- Retrieve (optional): 63 × cropsnh:materialLeaf:19; 2 × Thorium Ore; 7 × Uranium 238 Ingot
- Retrieve: 2 × Uranium 238 Dust
Prerequisites: Fuel Input Automation
Unlocks: EV vs. IV; Uranium Basic Nukes

title: Powerful Nuclear Physics > Duranium and the Beam Crafter
text:
Quest: Duranium and the Beam Crafter
Quest line: Powerful Nuclear Physics

In the previous quest, Duranium was introduced as a material used to make Tritanium. While it becomes required for this reason, there is more to it than that. Another recipe that uses it is a Beam Crafter recipe, which has a chance to produce a Quantum Anomaly.

First off, what is the Beam Crafter? That is a multiblock that works a bit like fusion, but only for the purpose of making new materials. It collides single particles with one another, or against fluids, to generate new items while consuming power. You can see more detailed information in the "Crafting, but with Beams!" quest found in Multiblock Goals. Duranium can be used in this machine to create Quantum Anomalies. This is a chance craft, but the Anomaly has a special property: when used to convert some blocks to others, it will not be consumed. Therefore, for that purpose, you only need to get one.

Is this required? Well, yes. When you arrive at a certain stage of the game, you might find yourself needing a new kind of soldering alloy, called Mutated Living Solder. To craft this, you need a Chemical Plant made with Botmium, which is an alloy that required Advanced Nitinol. This, in turn, is one of the blocks that need a Quantum Anomaly for its conversion. Given that Duranium is the only fluid choice to make the Anomaly, then it becomes required for this as well, but only a couple tiers from ZPM.

Additionally, there are other recipes, like the Elemental Duplicator. This is a very powerful replicator that will give you a great boost in automation due to its speed and the replication recipes it can do, but the Quantum Anomaly used in this recipe will be consumed, so watch out: if you only have one, don't use it for this. Later on, however, you will encounter other recipes that consume the anomaly, namely the casings for the Quantum Force Transformer, so it will be important to automate their production by then.

- Tick the checkbox
Prerequisites: Tin Plasma From T2; Fusing Americium and Tritanium

title: Powerful Nuclear Physics > EV vs. IV
text:
Quest: EV vs. IV
Quest line: Powerful Nuclear Physics

Your sourcing of Uranium is gonna be very small in EV, unless you use crops. Similarly, your ability to put together the multiblocks needed for the fluid nuke will be better in IV, since you can mine Small Titanium Ore directly, and use GT++ multis.

All in all, the Tier 2 Rocket makes things a lot easier by letting you mine ores on Mars and Phobos to get Uranium and Tungstate/Scheelite. However, building it requires considerable progression in EV, due to TPV Coils, which need Titanium and Platinum, and the Field Generators that the rocket needs. In EV and IV, vacuum nukes are one of the best choices for power, but the setup is complicated and needs Uranium and/or Plutonium.

Either way, it's recommended to have a Multiblock Miner in either the Nether, for Thorium or Phobos/Deimos, for Uranium.
