title: Space Race > Fancy Stripes!
text:
Quest: Fancy Stripes!
Quest line: Space Race

An engine is required to accelerate your Mothership. There are two different tiers of engines and bases, and you can attach between 1-10 engine bases to a single engine in a horizontal line. Each additional base additively increases thrust. You may use multiple engines if desired, but their bases must be separate, and all engines should face the same direction for maximum efficiency. The engine and its bases will combine into a single clickable entity that can be filled with fuel.

The Mothership determines its fuel consumption and total travel time based on the available thrust and the distance being traveled. However, the Mothership will not allow departure if the travel time exceeds one in-game day, meaning you must have sufficient thrust to reach your destination.

The minimum configurations required to reach the Ra system using each engine tier are listed below:

A Rocket Engine Jet (T1) will produce 2MN of thrust per Rocket Engine Base and require 2L/t of Naquadah Based Fuel MK-II during travel. At minimum, to make it to the Ra system you will need 9 Rocket Engine Bases and 92,440L of fuel.

An Ion Thruster Jet (T2) will produce 25MN of thrust per Ion Thruster Base and require both 1L/t of Xenon and 10EU/t of power during travel. At minimum, to make it to the Ra system you will need 7 Ion Thruster Bases, 20,970L of Xenon, and 31,970EU.

Note that for both configurations, when starting from the Overworld, you must first stop at Proxima Centauri to refuel before continuing on to the Ra system.

It's highly recommended to go with the T1 route since the required materials are much cheaper!

title: Space Race > Grapple
text:
Quest: Grapple
Quest line: Space Race

The Grapple is a grappling hook and rope which can be thrown by a player, and then used to swing the player in the direction it was thrown. Useful for reaching places that are otherwise too high to jump to, or traveling around the Asteroids. (Or just, you know, fly.)

Right-click to aim the Grapple at a block you want to reach, similar to aiming a Bow. Release the right-click - similar to firing an arrow from a bow - to grapple yourself in that direction.

For best results, aim the Grapple at a point 1 or 2 blocks higher than the point you want to reach.

If there is no safe platform to land at that point, you can fall back down and you will take fall damage, so it takes some skill to use the Grapple safely.

Take care using the Grapple near a Nether Portal, End Portal or at a low height (less than Y30) on a Space Station. There can be strange consequences if it crosses into another dimension.

title: Space Race > Moon Day and Night time
text:
Quest: Moon Day and Night time
Quest line: Space Race

The Moon's day-night cycle is 2h 40min long, equaling 8 Overworld days and it is linked to the Moon phases seen on the Overworld. The daytime on the moon lasts from a full moon to the next new moon (4 Overworld days, equaling 1h 20min) and, logically, the nighttime lasts from the new moon to the next full moon.

Since the 1st Overworld night is full moon, you can safely land within the 1st 4 Overworld days, and then the next 4 Overworld days are more dangerous since hostile mobs will be able to spawn in the dark, and so on. If you miscount, the moon phases can tell you when it is daytime or nighttime on the moon. Full moon is the start of the moon day, new (or dark) moon is the start of the moon night.

During the nighttime, the environment light levels get very low, allowing hostile mobs to spawn on the surface.

title: Space Race > RP-1 Rocket Fuel
text:
Quest: RP-1 Rocket Fuel
Quest line: Space Race

One option to fuel your T1 and T2 rocket is RP-1 Rocket Fuel. First, you'll need either Diesel or Coal Tar. Coal Tar is the better option in the long run, since you'll need the other products of distilling it to make other rocket fuels, but for now you can use Diesel.

If you're using Diesel, you need 20 cells, if using Coal Tar, you need 30. Unless you use a DT, in which case it doesn't divide evenly anymore.

Distill it in the Distillery to get Kerosene, then distill it again to get RP-1. You'll need a Chemical Plant for the last step.

RP-1 Rocket Fuel is a T4 240 EU/t recipe, so you'll need to make the Chemical Plant out of Stainless Steel and HV Machine Casings.

Since there is no oxygen in space, you will also need an oxidizer. But since the Galacticraft rocket can only take one fluid we have simplified that a bit. Just combine Liquid Oxygen and RP-1 to make the fully functional RP-1 Rocket Fuel.

If you're confused about how to use/make the Chemical Plant, refer to the manual with the same name or the quest in the GT++ quest tab.

PS: You can also use Rocket Fuels for power in Rocket Engines, or the Rocketdyne F-1A Engine multi.

This quest chain will guide you through the progression of rocket fuels.

title: Space Race > Serious Upgrades
text:
Quest: Serious Upgrades
Quest line: Space Race

So if you thought 'hey, the purple stuff wasn't that bad, why not make the green?', well, first of all, you may need professional help. Second, you're going to need to be in ZPM to make the casings you need, full stop. You need a ZPM ABS for the components, so come back once you've made a ZPM Energy Hatch.

You can probably figure most of it out on your own, but keep in mind that some of the materials need to be created in the ABS, solidified, macerated, and then used in another ABS recipe. The examples here are Hastelloy-N for Lafium Compound and, Rhenium for Laurenium. Rhenium itself is made with a nonstandard ABS recipe. You also need Dysprosium which requires either making Rare Earth (III) or going to the Toxic Everglades. You'll also need either Rare Earth (II) or Rare Earth (III) for Ytterbium unless, again, you visit the Everglades for it. The Everglades ore veins might be very hard to find, due to their rarity. You could also get Ytterbium from Almandine Ore if you are willing to try GT++ Milling and Froth Flotation.

Have fun with that!

You'll almost certainly need more than this, but the exact amount, as always, depends on your hatches and buses.

text:

Quest line: Space Race

Once the player has used the Cryogenic Chamber, there is a 300 second cooldown before they can use it again. Breaking and replacing the chamber, or trying to use a different chamber, will not reset the cooldown unless the player dies.

The chamber does not require energy to work.

title: Space Race > Space Pumping
text:
Quest: Space Pumping
Quest line: Space Race

At some point you may have wondered: There are these enormous gas planets in the solar system - could there be a way to "harvest" them? Indeed there is. By constructing the "Planetary Gas Siphon" multiblock, you are able to pump from the infinite supply of gas found on Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune. You just need to build a space station around a gas planet to get close enough to reach the gas without falling into it.

Different gases can be extracted by pumping at different depths which is controlled by a Programmed Circuit. You need to supply (64 * depth) Mining Pipes to reach the selected depth.

While operational, the multiblock needs d*4^(T+2) EU/t where T is the tier of the space station and d is the depth.

You do not need a minimum tier of coil to siphon particular gas types, but you will get a 10% speed boost per coil tier.

You probably also want a good overview of what you can get with your Planetary Gas Siphon, and the tiers of the gas giants. So here we go:

Jupiter (Tier 3)
1 Hydrogen - 15000 L/s
2 Helium - 500 L/s
3 Nitrogen - 300 L/s
4 Oxygen - 200 L/s

Saturn (Tier 5)
1 Hydrogen - 18000 L/s
2 Helium - 800 L/s
3 Oxygen - 500 L/s
4 Liquid Oxygen - 150 L/s

Uranus (Tier 5)
1 Deuterium - 5000 L/s
2 Neon - 450 L/s
3 Argon - 250 L/s
4 Krypton - 100 L/s

Neptune (Tier 6)
1 Tritium - 3000 L/s
2 Helium-3 - 500 L/s
3 Ammonia - 400 L/s
4 Xenon - 350 L/s

Days on space stations last longer than on the overworld, so you can generate more solar power.

You can build space stations here:
1. Moon - T1
2. Mars - T2
3. Jupiter - T3
4. Venus - T4
5. Saturn - T5
6. Uranus - T5
7. Neptune - T6

Each Retrieval Task in this quest corresponds (in order) to the resources you will need in order to build a space station at one of the planets listed above. The "T#" afterwards refers to the tier of rocket you will need to get there.

You will need to complete at least one task to complete this quest!

It is likely that you will lose your rocket when flying back to Earth or another space station. Make sure you have an alternative way to return (some form of teleportation) or use another planet/moon as proxy (if you get an error while doing so, you spawn on the planet/moon and can launch your rocket again).

title: Storing and Transforming EU > Battery Buffer
text:
Quest: Battery Buffer
Quest line: Storing and Transforming EU

Batteries work pretty much the same in a battery buffer as in a regular machine's battery slot. Battery buffers are used to buffer power to stabilize output.

They come in different sizes: 1, 4, 9(!) and 16 slots. They can draw 2A and output 1A per battery inserted - watch your wire amperage! Cables come in 1x, 2x, 4x, 8x, 12x, and 16x, with tin transferring 1A per size. Make sure not to mess up, or your cable will melt, becoming a fire, and possibly an explosion.

Remember that there's loss when outputting EU from any GT machine, so putting 4 4-slot ones in a row loses 8 power compared to 2 from 1 16-slot one. And this is for every amp too.

You can import batteries into one, but ONLY empty acid batteries can be exported from one. No, you can't get around this.

title: Storing and Transforming EU > Infinite Energy Storage
text:
Quest: Infinite Energy Storage
Quest line: Storing and Transforming EU

You shouldn't click on links from strangers! Although this sounds like clickbait it is true. From a certain point of view.

Use the (potential) force! And store energy that way. Simply construct a dam and flood vast areas with water. You may add energy to your storage by pumping more water into it or just drain it back into energy whenever you need. This works especially well with fluctuating energy sources like wind, water, and solar. Or you dump excess energy into it so you can use it another time. The capacity is huge and the choice is yours.

Sounds great! But...? - Indeed. There is a catch: Pumps and Turbines will have efficiency correlated loss. Still interested? Let's get to crafting!

The multi-block has an unusual shape: the back is open. The lake will spawn inside the multi-block and spread block-by-block as far as it can/is allowed. It will replace plants like water (make sure to secure your Crops!) but not replace any solid blocks. Additionally, you can specify limits in any direction. The water will NEVER spread past these limits. You can set those limits in a second GUI by right-clicking the controller with a screwdriver.

When you enter a limit, it will correct itself to the nearest valid setting. Especially if you try to spread past the server limits. You may talk your admin into raising these limits (these limits are designed to limit griefing). Further, water is not able to spread into foreign towns.
You will also find 3 magical buttons in the top-right of this GUI. From left to right: The first will slowly despawn the lake blocks. You can use this to shrink the lake if it spread past a barrier for example. The multi-block will also initialize with this configuration so there is no accidental flooding. The second and third buttons will slowly spawn more lake blocks. Additionally, the second button will render those lake blocks pink so you see where they are so you may plug holes and such. In this "debug" mode you can walk/breathe/act in the lake like in air. This should make it easy to create a sunken village for decoration purposes. The third button is for normal operations so you can see the water and enjoy a swim in your energy buffer.

Of course, there is also a normal GUI (simple right-click). It shows you the energy stored in the dam. To reach higher water levels you are required to use stronger pumps. For this purpose, you may configure the voltage tier of the GUI with a circuit in the circuit slot. Don't worry: It is only optical. You cannot void any energy if you set a low voltage tier. It is only for the player information. You may give it a try with the reward you earn...

If you have any further questions, find missing information, or have suggestions please do not hesitate to post on the official GT New Horizons Discord. Please add '@SinTh0r4s' to your post to make sure I'll see it.

A warning though: there have been a lot of mentions of bugs and even world corruptions caused by the Hydro Dam. Use at your own risk. If you have more detailed information, please report these problems on the GTNH GitHub.

title: Storing and Transforming EU > Low Voltage Transformer
text:
Quest: Low Voltage Transformer
Quest line: Storing and Transforming EU

It is possible to run MV machines while still in LV - build a transformer and use 4 power sources 32 EU/t to power one 128 EU/t machine.

It transforms power up or down, depending on the mode, which you can switch with a soft mallet. Step-up means 4A LV in, 1A MV out, while step-down means the reverse.

Make sure you understand the following if you prefer your base not being a crater:
A step-down mode is the default one. In this mode, the large dot is the input. In a step-up mode, it's the output. Do not mix it up. LV machines that receive MV power will explode.

If the transformer is connected to power, or was in the past, then do not change the mode with stuff connected. It's better to break and place it again to get rid of the stored power rather than rotate it with the wrench and blow things up. Make sure to also disconnect the nearby wires with a wire cutter.

As a reminder, machines don't blow up if they are given more amps than they can consume. They blow up from higher voltage tier.

Then this multiblock is for you, the Tesla Tower comes with high amperage output and full TecTech energy hatch support with this powerful multiblock.

To get started you will need to fill the tower with capacitors matching the tier of the Primary Tesla Windings within the capacitor bank. The Tesla Winding determines the tier of power that the tower transfers power at and the amount of capacitors determines the maximum amperage that can be output.

A total of 16 capacitors can be placed into one capacitor bank so you might need many banks depending on your power needs.

Once the tower is constructed click open the controller to configure the maximum transfer distance of the tower to fit the needs of your base. The range setting is currently buggy which means that at least for now you can do so without needing any plasmas. This option is called “Tesla Towers Transfer Radius Setting”.

Now that your tower is all configured how do you get power out of it to your machines? Well I am glad you asked. To get power to the machines of the base you will need to use the Tesla Coil Covers. Place them on the tops of your machines, energy hatches and even transformers to get power flowing from the tower. Energy hatches are a bit picky however and the hatch likes to be facing upwards to receive power.

Warning! The Tesla Tower will output only one tier of amp such as EV, IV etc. When upgrading the Primary Tesla Windings, please make sure to check that all of your coil covers and transceivers in the base can handle the upgraded power. Failure to do so will result in a machine explosion.

Failure to turn off the controller before adjustment can also cause an explosion.

title: The Green Revolution > A Summary of Crossbreeding
text:
Quest: A Summary of Crossbreeding
Quest line: The Green Revolution

There are two things you must always remember when breeding anything:

- Parents must be at least 80% mature in order to cross-breed, regardless of it's ability to keep growing.
- Offsprings cannot appear without meeting all their growth requirements.

When breeding, the resulting stats are based on the rounded-down average of the participating parents' stats plus or minus a random value.

The range of this random value depends on 2 factors: The number of parents and the amount of fertilizer stored within them.

- Early on, breeding with multiple parents is the only way to attempt to improve your stats, but it's very slow.
- Applying fertilizer widen the range of values for multi-parent breeding and stabilizes stats during simple propagation.
- Using a Crop Manager to apply fertilizer allows you to rapidly improve the stats of your crops.

Multiple parent:
- 0 to 49 fertilizer: -1 -> +1 (higher chance for -1 and 1)
- 50-100 fertilizer: -2 -> +2
- 101+ fertilizer: 0 -> +4 (40% chance for 0)

Single parent:
- 0-49 fertilizer: -1 -> 0 (higher chance for 0)
- 50-100 fertilizer: no variation
- 100+ fertilizer: 0 -> +4 (40% chance for 0)

When breeding crops, there is a 50% chance for the offspring to be of the same species as one of the parents. When this happens, all the parents matching the species of the offspring are used to compute the rounded-down average.

There are 2 ways to obtain new species: Random Mutations and Deterministic Mutations.

Most crops have access to something called Mutation Pools. These pools are like a set of tags associated with each crop. When breeding, if of the parents some share one or more mutation pools, a Random mutation may occur. The resulting offspring will always be another species tagged with one of those shared pools.

Once you've obtained your first 31/31/31 seed, it can be helpful to use these random pool mutations to collect many different types of crops.

Deterministic breeding is similar to how bees work, where you must bring the right species together. Some situations require more than two parents, and all parents must be adjacent to the double crop stick. During the early stages, you can often emulate deterministic breeding by tailoring the soil, sub-soil and environment of a double cropstick to control the outcome of a random mutation. This process is usually much slower than deterministic mutations, and might require a lot of baby sitting if the crop you wan\u0027t can be singled out/

Deterministic Mutations always take priority over Random Mutations.

Advanced crops (MV and above materials) will require the breeding machine.

title: The Green Revolution > Breeding With Technology
text:
Quest: Breeding With Technology
Quest line: The Green Revolution

The Crop Breeder is a single-block machine that allows you to breed new crops deterministically. It will consume the parent seeds, some Enriched Fertilizer and a catalyst item for material-based crops.

The stats of an offspring created by the breeder will always be the rounded down average of seeds that were consumed to create it. Breeding two or more maxed-out crops will always give a maxed-out offspring.

The Enriched Fertilizer cost is 144L per tier of the offspring crop + 72L for each stat point on the new seed. So a 31/31/31 tier 5 offspring would cost roughly 7.4KL to breed.

Some crops require a minimum machine tier to be bred:
- Iridine, Osmianth and Stargatium are all IV recipes
- Titania is EV
- Bauxia is MV
- An HV machine is required to breed 31/31/31

Success chance starts at 40% and increases by 10% for every tier past LV, meaning that at ZPM, it's guaranteed. A failed breed will void the parent seeds used.

As a final note: when two crops share breeding requirements (ie Tearstalks and Evil Ore), be careful to insert the seeds in the proper order as to not trigger the mutation with fewer parents.

You only need one of the machines for this quest.

title: The Green Revolution > Crop Nutrients
text:
Quest: Crop Nutrients
Quest line: The Green Revolution

The speed at which a crop grows is based on its Nutrient Score. There are a number of different ways to obtain Nutrient Points for your crops, but to keep your crops from getting sick try to make sure they are always receiving at least a couple of the below bonuses:

- +10 Points can be gained from having water in your crop sticks (scales 1-10 based on hydration level).
- +10 Points can be gained from having fertilizer in your crop sticks (scales 1-10 based on fertilizer level).
- +2 Points can be gained from allowing the crop to see the sky.
       - Crops in the Industrial Farm will always have this bonus.
- +28 Points can be gained from preferred biome tags
       - If no preferred tags are found, high humidity will give up to +14 Points. 
       - See more on this in the Environmental Preferences quest.

All crops have a base Nutrient Score of 5.

You can check the Nutrient Score of a crop by using a Portable Scanner on any crop sticks or Industrial Farm controller, even if it's empty.

Crop tier determines the Nutrient Score requirements for growth. 
The following cutoffs apply:

Tier 4 - Last tier where crops can be planted anywhere

Tier 5 - Last tier where crops can be planted anywhere as long as they can see the sky

Tier 11 - Last tier where crop can be anywhere as long as crops are in an 80%+ humidity biome

Tier 12 - Last tier where crops can be anywhere as long as crops are in a 80%+ humidity biome and can see the sky

Tasks:
- Tick the checkbox
Prerequisites: Crop Sticks

title: The Green Revolution > Crop Stats
text:
Quest: Crop Stats
Quest line: The Green Revolution

A key part of CropsNH is improving the stats of your crops. There is almost always a chance for this to occur whenever a new crop grows - whether by self propagation or crossing...

Growth:
Improves growth speed
- Increases the number of progress points per growth tick by up to about 525% with some variation depending on the tier of the crop.
Can cause weeds to spawn
- When growth is above 23 (or 7 for Necrobloom), crops will begin spreading weeds and diseases to nearby crops.
- You can prevent this by either using Weed-EX or by increasing the resistance stat so it's equal to or above the growth stat.

Gain:
Improves harvest size
- Up to 2.5x per harvest at 31 gain.
- Has a gain/100 chance of increasing the stack size of any drop by 1.

Resistance:
Improves seed harvest chances
- A resistance of 10 will guarantee a seed drop when harvesting a mature crop with a reinforced spade.
- This scales by rate of resistance/10:
  - 20: 2 seeds
  - 25: 2 seeds + 50% chance for a 3rd
  - 31: 3 seeds + 10% chance for a 4th
- A resistance of 31 will guarantee a seed drop even without a spade.
Increases weed resistance
- When a crop's growth is above 23, resistance will prevent weed spreading as long as it's greater than or equal to the growth stat.
Improves a crop's resistance to diseases
- Each point reduces a crop's chance of becoming infected.
- With 31 resistance, crops are immune to diseases.
This includes sickness from lack of Nutrient Score, however, the crop still will not grow without the necessary nutrient level being reached.

- Tick the checkbox
Rewards: 8 × Coin "The Farmer 1"
Prerequisites: Crop Sticks

title: The Green Revolution > Crop Sticks
text:
Quest: Crop Sticks
Quest line: The Green Revolution

To do anything in CropsNH, you first need crop sticks. These will act as the supports for your plants to grow upon. Empty crop sticks can be doubled by right-clicking another crop stick onto them. These double-crop sticks allow you to breed any adjacent mature crops.

As new species grow on your crop sticks, you can harvest them by right-clicking, which won't remove the seed. Left-clicking harvests the crop and removes it, potentially dropping a seed depending on the resistance. Spades will help you improve your chances of obtaining seeds when you do this, as will the Resistance trait.

The chance to drop a seed from any crop without a spade is measured
as resistance/31. So crops with a maxed resistance stat will always drop a seed when broken.

Don't forget to check the seed tooltips or NEI page for the varying types of soil, sub-soil, and other environmental requirements!

If you're already an experienced farmhand, collect a single stonelily seed and I'll let you skip subsequent introductory trainings for now.

Tip #2: Also remember that crops require all their growth requirements to be met in order to breed, even when breeding via mutation pools.

Tip #3: This requirement can actually be used to filter the outcome of a pool mutation so that only a subset of them may appear. Though this doesn't actually reduce number of crops that can be picked from the pools shared by the parents. (and therefore doesn't directly increase your chance of getting what you want).

Tip #4: If you want to properly increase your chance of getting something through mutation pools, try lowering the number of shared pools between the parents.

title: The Green Revolution > Enriched Fertilizer
text:
Quest: Enriched Fertilizer
Quest line: The Green Revolution

Enriched fertilizer allows you to advance to the next stage of crop technology! 

It is used in countless ways moving forward, for example:

- Apply it to your crops for more efficient fertilization.
- Used to breed novel crops in the Crop Breeder.
- Used to replicate seeds in the Seed Generator.

Enriched Fertilizer is 10 times more potent than regular Fertilizer when applied.

- With a Crop Manager, a single unit of fluid adds 10 fertilizer units to the machine's internal storage.
- With an Industrial Farm, you only need to provide 1/10th of the amount indicated on the tooltips. (Except when using a Fertilization Unit.)

It will always be superior to the item based Fertilizers of the past, so moving forward you should be using it whenever possible.

When using the Crop Breeder or Seed Generator, the Enriched Fertilizer recipe costs scale with the stats of the resulting seeds. Keep this in mind as early tier machines all have a lower than usual fluid capacity. You'll need at least HV machines in order to create maxed seeds. By default NEI shows you the costs for a maxed seed, so keep this in mind when looking up recipes.

title: The Green Revolution > Environmental Preferences
text:
Quest: Environmental Preferences
Quest line: The Green Revolution

Each crop has a set of preferred biome tags. These can be viewed in NEI along with the other growth requirements.

Having the proper biome tags will provide a significant Nutrient Point boost to your crops (+14 Points per tag).

You can only benefit from up to 2 biome tags (+28 Points).

It is possible to emulate a single preferred biome tag by planting your crops in a high-humidity location. The bonus scales linearly with humidity between 50% and 80%. Values below 50% provide no bonus, while values above 80% will hit the cap at an equivalent of 1 preferred biome tag (+14 Points).

If any favored biome tag is present in the current biome, the high humidity bonus will be ignored.


The Nature's Compass will allow you to view the tags of each biome as subtext within its menu. Sorting biomes by tags is the simplest method.

title: The Green Revolution > Gene Extractor
text:
Quest: Gene Extractor
Quest line: The Green Revolution

The Crop Gene Extractor and Crop Synthesizers can be made in EV and allows you to create new seeds using UU-Matter and a few Data Orbs.

Crop Gene Extractor
The Crop Gene Extractor is used to extract "Genes" from a crop. You can control which gene is extracted from a crop by using a programmed circuit:
1. Species
2. Growth
3. Gain
4. Resistance

Extracting will usually have a base recipe time of 150 seconds (with the exception of the species gene, taking 300 seconds at base)

Crop Synthesizer
The Crop Synthesizer is used to create new seeds from the extracted genes at the cost of some UU-Matter.

The UU-Matter cost will depend on the stats and tier of the seed being synthesized.
- 750L per crop tier.
- 100L per stat point on the seed.

Using the Crop Synthesizer is the only way to obtain and replicate maxed out Primordial Berry seeds.

Quest: Last Universal Common Seed

Before going further into CropsNH, there is but one chore I need you to do. To prevent future hardship, collect a fully statted 31/31/31 seed.

This may seem daunting at first, but with enough blood, sweat, fertilizer, and a trusty crop manager, you can do it. I believe in you!

Ensure you pick a species which is related via mutation pools and determinism to other Crops you want. If you don't know what to choose, may I suggest the any of the natura berries (Raspberry, Blueberry, Blackberry or Maloberry), Cactus, or Brown Mushrooms? 

- The berries have a fairly low growth times which can grow fairly quickly and have access to the Food pool which opens up access to a lot of other useful pools.

While there is a reason behind keeping some seeds low statted (lowering enriched fertilizer costs in machines), the time saved by working with max stat crops compared to low stat crops is just too significant to ignore.

This quest will accept any CropsNH seed with a perfect statline.

title: The Green Revolution > Multiblock Farming
text:
Quest: Multiblock Farming
Quest line: The Green Revolution

Now this... this is how you show those B**keepers what's what. 

The Industrial Farm (IF) is a long term, scalable, solution to Crop production. At its most basic, it will grow, harvest, and hydrate your crops, but with several upgrades and tier based size scaling, it is not a simple machine to make use of. The IF has three modes:

Input - Pulls seeds and sub-soil blocks into the machine from an Input Bus.
Farm - Grows the seeds and pushes products into an Output Bus.
Output - Exports the seeds and undersoil blocks from the machine into an Output Bus.

You can cycle through them in the machine menu by clicking on the mode button.

To start, you should construct the most basic IF possible. Once you've done that, place your seeds (and any relevant sub-soil blocks) into the Input Bus. 

Seeds that have sub-soil requirements won't be inserted into the farm unless a block of the sub-soil is also available to the machine. The sub-soil block doesn't need to be in the same Input Bus as the seeds for it to work.

Once you've input your seeds (and sub-soil blocks), you can begin using Farm mode to grow your crops.

When you wish to switch out seeds, enter Output mode before re-inserting the new seeds via the Input mode.

The length of your IF is controlled by the tier of your Seed Bed. An MV farm will require MV Seed Beds and therefore can only have one row of Seed Beds. This also means you can only insert one upgrade block (by replacing the wooden frame on the top layer). Each subsequent tier of Seed Bed increases the length of the machine, the base power consumption, the number of upgrades you can install and the number of seeds that can be inserted into the controller.

The power, water and fertilizer consumption of the industrial farm do not scale with the number of seeds inside the farm, so there is no benefit to running the farm under capacity.

Crops grown in the Industrial Farm are assumed to grow in the following environment:
- They have sky access (+2 Nutrient Points)
- They have 200 water (+10 Nutrient Points)
- They have 200 fertilizer when using fertilizer (+10 Nutrient Points)
- The biome at the location of the controller controls the biome tags and humidity with the biome tags added by the env modules (up to +28 Nutrient Points)

- Retrieve (optional): 26 × Bricked Agricultural Casing; 3 × Seed Bed (MV); 4 × Glass; Wood Frame Box; Input Hatch (MV); Input Bus (MV); Output Bus (MV); MV Energy Hatch; Maintenance Hatch

You'll need to follow these steps in order to get your hands on oil-berry seeds if your parents have maxed stats:

1. Down-stat one of the parents via manual breeding.
2. Use a spade to get some spare seeds.
3. Use the lower stat seeds to create an oil berry seed using the MV Crop Breeder.
4. Max out the stats of the oil berry seed like you originally did when you got your first maxed crop.
5. Use a spade to farm enough seeds to fill your fields.

Alternatively, if you don't want to bother with this process you can just wait until you can get your hands on the HV Breeder and Seed Generator.

If you want to go with the MV route, using random breeding is the easiest way to get your hands on a mid-stat version of the parents. For oil berry, the simplest solution simply involves breeding Withereed with a 1/1/1 sugar cane until you breed a new mid-stat Withereed.

title: The Green Revolution > Taking Pools Seriously
text:
Quest: Taking Pools Seriously
Quest line: The Green Revolution

With that 31/31/31 seed now in hand you will (ideally) never have to complete the entire statting process again. 

Once replicated, you can cross this perfect seed with itself to access the pools that it has access to! This is the intended path for early game crop discovery. While it is much more random than deterministic breeding, it will let you collect a wider range of species quicker.

Don't forget to fertilize your crops using a crop manager or else your stats might go down while breeding!

Keep in mind that: when pool breeding occurs, the offspring has a chance to be any crop found within any of the pools shared by 2 or more of the parent crops. The mutation selection occurs prior to the check for environment. In practice this means that if you're searching for a specific species in say, the Food pool, it will take much longer to appear than one in the Reed pool because there are fewer alternative species. No matter the environment.

Once you've gotten your hands on a solid number of species, deterministic breeding becomes a simpler and more effective method for obtaining new species.

As some of you may have discovered, some crops don't particularly enjoy being stepped on and will damage or even poison you if you dare walk over them. While sneaking may prevent this, wearing proper protective gear is the better solution.

Boots that provide hazmat protection prevent damage while walking through these dangerous crops, though you will still take a bit of damage as you walk through your crops. Rechargeable hazmat-providing boots (such as nano boots) and those that offer spacesuit protection take no damage while walking through your crops.

The first pair of protective boots you can get your hands on is the humble rubber boots.

Leather boots (and their variants) can also help by reducing incoming damage by 75%, but they will rapidly take damage while protecting you.

title: The Green Revolution > Tools of the Trade 5 - Reinforced Spade

Quest line: The Green Revolution

1 Resist = 10% seed drop
10 Resist = 1 guaranteed seed drop
15 Resist = 1 guaranteed seed drop + 50% chance for a second seed drop!
31 Resist = 3 guaranteed seed drops + 10% chance for a fourth seed drop!!

Time to scale up farmhand.

If you're removing a crop with your spade, sneaking will let you remove the crop without having to worry about the spade breaking the crop stick.

title: Tier 0.5 - Steam > A Better Way to Find Items
text:
Quest: A Better Way to Find Items
Quest line: Tier 0.5 - Steam

NEI has a built in search feature for finding an item stored in an inventory nearby. A Stockroom Catalog can give you a list of everything stored in your inventories.

Sneak-right-click a block with an inventory (a chest, bookcase, barrel, anything with an inventory) to add that inventory to the list of inventories for the catalog to keep track of.

Sneak-right-click the same block again to remove that block from the list.

A small particle effect will render on any block that has been selected with the catalog when holding the Stockroom Catalog to let you know that block is being tracked.

Right-click to open the GUI and see the list. You can sort the list in ascending or descending order by quantity (Count) or alphabetical order.

You can also see a list of all the inventories that have a particular item and easily add the location of one of those inventories to a stockroom catalog so you can easily find your stuff.

The Stockroom Catalog can also be copied with the typesetting table and printing press.

Click on the title to change it to anything so you can custom label your stockroom catalog.

Click on the small chest icons on the right hand side of each listing to open the inventory list view.

If you want, you can craft a waypoint compass and use that to point you towards the chest. Since we have JourneyMaps and NEI, it's not really necessary.

The Catalog seems to be a bit broken though and doesn't work well with GT items.

Prerequisites: Books

Buttons will emit one for about 2 seconds before resetting.

Levers will emit a signal until switched back off.

title: Tier 0.5 - Steam > Lit Way to Get Charred
text:
Quest: Lit Way to Get Charred
Quest line: Tier 0.5 - Steam

The "Charcoal Pile Igniter" is an alternative option for mass-producing charcoal. It does not consume any power or steam, but generates a lot of pollution. Follow the steps below to get it working.

1. Build a brick floor no bigger than 11x11 in size.
2. Place 1-5 layers of logs atop the brick floor. No air gaps allowed.
3. Place the Charcoal Pile Igniter above the top-center log.
4. Surround the remaining logs in dirt or grass.
5. The Charcoal Pile Igniter immediately starts processing
6. After some time, the logs are converted to brittle charcoal blocks.
7. Break the blocks with an axe for the charcoal (Luck/Fortune has NO effect on the drop rates).

If this is your first multiblock, read the extended tooltip (hold shift) for construction requirements, or visit https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/Charcoal_Pile_Igniter for more information and step-by-step images.

Tasks:

Another downside to crafting Nether Furnaces is that they cannot be used as a component for the Electric Blast Furnace (EBF) craft later on. Blast Furnaces can.

Then again, Nether dust is practically free, and unlike Blast Furnaces these can process every type of furnace recipe, so what's the loss? You can always use them to bake stacks of bread!

title: Tier 0.5 - Steam > More Advanced Alloys
text:
Quest: More Advanced Alloys
Quest line: Tier 0.5 - Steam

Your smeltery does a great job mixing metals into alloys, but it's not very efficient, and limited in its complexity. You need something new, so why not put your steam to some use? The Alloy Smelter can make bronze for you directly, using ingots, dusts, or even nuggets. You can make a nugget mold as well to turn ingots into nuggets if you have steel.

It might also come in handy when processing raw rubber. You should keep an eye on recipes to see when machines offer better options to make items...

NOTE: Like all steam machines, the output port is a steam outlet when recipes complete. It must not be blocked. Also, steam is hot, remember? Change the output side by whacking the machine with a wrench. The 3x3 grid will show you which side the output will move to when you whack it.

You can empty the machine by putting a hopper beneath it.

WARNING: The Alloy Smelter recipes take a lot of steam. Do them one by one until you understand how fast you use steam, and how much you will need buffered. Large pipes are a decent "poor man's" buffer, and the boiler can hold quite a bit of steam, as well as the machine itself. Once you get a little further along, make a larger steam buffer with an iron or steel railcraft tank.

Tasks:

title: Tier 0.5 - Steam > Reinforced X? Unbreakable
text:
Quest: Reinforced X? Unbreakable
Quest line: Tier 0.5 - Steam

With your steel tool you are able to mine obsidian. You can make the Reinforcement which gives a reinforced modifier which increases the durability of your tool. Reinforced level X makes a tool unbreakable.

PS: In many cases this is not worth it, since the tools don't degrade that fast, it doesn't cost much to repair, and you get better materials (with higher durability) to make them out of reasonably fast. Plus, by the time you got it to unbreakable, you'd be auto-mining everything with a miner anyway. Just use redstone, or maybe luck/silky. However, there are a few very nice use cases like lumber axes and tools for automation setups.

text:

Be sure to bring a tough companion along to keep you alive. If you have no friends, why not make an Iron Golem and push it through first, or bring the materials for more along with you?

Also, when you die here, not if, your graves will spawn skeletons because of the darkness. Make sure you light up areas where you might die, and when recovering graves light up the area first so that you don't end up dying over and over and making a mess.

Watch out for some mobs! They'll take minimal damage from any weapon that is not their weakness. So if you seem to not be doing much damage, you probably aren't! Think about other options to hurt/kill the monster.

title: Tier 0.5 - Steam > Tame an Ocelot to Get a Friend
text:
Quest: Tame an Ocelot to Get a Friend
Quest line: Tier 0.5 - Steam

Once you have the required materials, you will need to find an ocelot to tame.

Ocelots can be found in Jungle Biomes.

If you are having trouble finding an ocelot, you can always summon an ocelot using a spawn egg.

You can tame an ocelot by giving it a raw fish. So add the raw fish to your inventory and select the raw fish in your hotbar.

Just like vanilla Minecraft, a tamed ocelot turns into a cat. The cat will repel creepers.

TIP: Make sure you are in a large space when trying to tame the ocelot so that the ocelot has lots of room to move. If you are in a space that is too small, you will not be able to tame the ocelot.

Next, while holding the raw fish, do not move. If you move, you will scare away the ocelot. If you are very still, the ocelot will eventually notice the fish in your hand and begin to walk over to you.

You need Silver from small ores to craft Solar Boilers. Later in LV you can get much more in the Twilight Forest.

title: Tier 0.5 - Steam > The one book to rule them all
text:
Quest: The one book to rule them all
Quest line: Tier 0.5 - Steam

This Tome can store multiple documentation books from other mods. It will be empty when crafted, but you can add books by combining it with the desired book in a crafting grid.

Right-clicking with the Tome in hand will open an interface showing all the added books; clicking on a book will transform the tome into the selected book. To revert it back to the Tome, left-click while sneaking.

To retrieve a stored book, transform the Tome into the desired book and throw it away while sneaking - this will drop the selected book and leave the tome in your inventory.

Some warnings:

The extended version of the Book of Biomes from Witchery is not compatible with this tome.

You should not throw it through the Botania portal. The elves might steal your Tome and return only their own copy of the Lexica Botania.

text:

Quest line: Tier 0.5 - Steam

You can find amethyst blocks, crystals, and calcite blocks in underground geodes. 

During the Steam Age, calcite blocks become incredibly useful because you can put them into a Forge Hammer to obtain valuable calcite dust, which is used for crafting the Bricked Blast Furnace. They can usually be found between Y-levels 5 and 46.

Amethyst can also be mined and used as a source of silicon dioxide. One amethyst block drops 9 amethyst dust, making it a great option for obtaining silicon dioxide.

You can use an Ore Finder with calcite dust inserted into it to locate calcite deposits more easily.

title: Tier 0.5 - Steam > Welcome to Tier 0.5, Steam!
text:
Quest: Welcome to Tier 0.5, Steam!
Quest line: Tier 0.5 - Steam

Welcome, and well done so far! This tier is all about your first machines, getting more stuff from your ores and making bronze ingots in a more efficient manner.

For water, check out the Water Tank multiblock in the "Water Dilemma" quest. (Multiblock Goals tab)

To connect up your boilers, be sure to provide water from the bottom, they'll accept only water from this side, so no risk of melting your pipe. Wooden pipes are fine for this. Make sure you never run out of water - adding water to a dry hot boiler will cause it to explode!

Steam will come out from the sides. Remember, steam is hot! It will destroy wooden pipes. And it can burn you if you walk on bronze pipes full of steam. Cover them with wooden planks or paper. Or just don't walk on/next to them.

And no, you can't automate it. Make an electric one if you want to do that.

Tip: Water is consumed at a rate of 1L of water per 160L of steam for all boilers unless otherwise noted.

title: Tier 0 - Stone Age > Animal Farms
text:
Quest: Animal Farms
Quest line: Tier 0 - Stone Age

Trying to get some leather or wool? You'd probably need to spend a lot of time hunting animals and traveling around, or you could simply make a farm to get a decent amount of leather, wool, and meat close to home. Make sure you don't put too many animals in the pen or they will overcrowd and kill each other. This happens to villagers as well.

Animals will prioritize moving towards grass blocks over any other blocks, and if there's no grass blocks around, they prefer lit blocks over dark blocks. You can encourage animals to stay in pens, or at least not crowd the edges, by removing grass from around both sides of the fence and under it, and by placing a torch in the center of the pen. For sheep that need the grass to eat, which reduces time to mature and replaces sheared wool instantly, place it in the center of a cleared out area with a border of non-grass.

Also, large quantities can cause server lag, especially if they are bumping into each other a lot. So if you are in multiplayer, make sure you limit animals to no more than roughly one per block for small entities like chickens and one per two blocks for large entities like cows.

As an alternative, most animal and mob drops can be obtained from less laggy CropsNH farms.

title: Tier 0 - Stone Age > Coins! Coins! Coins!
text:
Quest: Coins! Coins! Coins!

Finally, a use for all of these coins!

The Vending Machine is a unique multiblock that allows you to exchange coins for valuable resources. You will progressively unlock new trades as you complete quests. Quests that unlock Vending Machine trades upon completion will show this information under the section labeled "Associated Vending Machine Exchanges".

Alternatively you can click "U" on the Vending Machine in NEI to see all available trades and what quests they are unlocked by. If an item can be traded for it will show up when clicking "R" under the Vending Machine tab.

You can put your coins directly into the input and they will appear in the internal storage. Additional inputs (including non-consumable) should be placed here as well. There is also a button for ejecting the coins if you need to reclaim them. Breaking the Vending Machine will not cause the coins to fall out or get deleted, they will be there when you replace it.

You can also share coins between a team. Using the /gtnhteam command you can team with other players and switch at will between using either your personal wallet, or your team wallet. Additionally, while in a team you can purchase VM items on behalf of a teammate.

Be aware, some trades have much longer timeout periods between claims!

title: Tier 0 - Stone Age > Divine Rod of the Gods?
text:
Quest: Divine Rod of the Gods?
Quest line: Tier 0 - Stone Age

The Ore Finder Wand reduces the tedium of locating needed veins. If you're not sure how to craft Magnetic Iron Rod for it, check its Shapeless Crafting tab in NEI.

Once you put an ore sample into the wand, it will tell you if this ore is nearby. When you get close to the target, you will hear the sound, and the wand will tilt down to the point of being upside-down if there's a lot of target ore nearby.

Use NEI to figure out which ore is the best for your search. If you don't have the needed ore, some basic ones can be purchased in the Vending Machine.

Open the wand's inventory with Shift+RMB when looking at the ground. Put the sample ore into the slot.
The rod has a 60-block range both up and down, so it can miss a vein that is located very low or if you are above the sea level.

The rod appears to work based on the GT's Material system, so anything of the same material will work.
That includes crushed ores, dusts, ingots, gems, rods, you name it. For things that don't belong to a particular Material, the rod appears to search only for that exact block - for instance, you won't detect small ores with the usual ore block.

If the detected ore is a part of a vein, you will see a discovery message in the chat, and the vein will be automatically logged into the visual prospecting tab of your journey map.

The wand also works from inventory and hotbar, so you don't need to be actively holding it, but you get style points if you do.

The ore in the wand is stored with the player, not the wand. In other words, remove the ore if you want to give the wand to your teammate.

The Ore Finder Wand doesn't work in space! The vast cosmic energies of the sun interfere with its inner workings! Or the devs want you to use something more complicated than a stick. You choose.

title: Tier 0 - Stone Age > More Food, More Hearts
text:
Quest: More Food, More Hearts
Quest line: Tier 0 - Stone Age

So, food is great, right? But what's even greater is eating tons of it! Too boring and pointless you say? Well, what if I told you, that you can get extra hearts just by expanding your palate. You get 1 point for every half shank of hunger from a food eaten, and after 50 points, you get 1 extra heart! Now you have a reason to make all those Pam's foods. Each food contributes its shank-value once. Eating something from a lunch box counts as if you took it out and ate it manually.

If you want to see what foods you've eaten, you can use the Food Journal, but it's clunky. Realistically, you want to use NEI to both see foods eaten and not eaten. You can search for 'not yet eaten' to see foods left, and 'assisted' to see foods eaten. You need to have started diminishing returns first to see this.

If it doesn't work, go to NEI options at bottom-left when the inventory is open, then click on Inventory, and change Search Mode to Regex. Then restart your client and try searching again.

There are also two commands:

/foodlist size
Tells you the overall progress, and the progress to the next heart.

/foodlist sync <PlayerName>
Sync your food progression with the server if it gets out of sync.

Quest line: Tier 0 - Stone Age

As you might know: tanned leather is more resistant and good enough for a backpack. Let's get a digger's backpack and a miner's backpack. Each pack holds different items. So use both for your first true back-packed mining experience.

Some tips:
- You can change a backpack's mode with Sneak + Right Click while holding it. Default mode picks up items from the ground, Resupply mode fills matching stacks in your inventory from the backpack, and Locked mode prevents the backpack from accepting items.

- You can hover over a backpack in your inventory and press the "Activate item in inventory" hotkey (G by default) to open it directly. This does not work while the backpack is in your hotbar.

- While holding a backpack, you can use Sneak + Right Click on a chest, drawer, or any other block face that accepts items to transfer the backpack's contents into that inventory. This can be used to empty backpacks quickly.

Screwdriver - Used on covers to change their behavior or on machines to change their input mode.

Wrench - Used to change the output direction on a GT machine, or to break it. Can also disconnect/connect pipes or enable their built in shutter.

Crowbar - Remove covers from machines or pipes.

Wire cutters - Connecting/disconnecting/breaking wires/cables.

Soft mallet - Turning machines on/off.

Hammer - Prospecting for ores in a limited way in front of you, smashing ore blocks into crushed ores, and muffling machine sounds.

Plunger - Drain fluids from a machine or tank

On a side note, Tin Pipes need a Steel Wrench to dismantle, so don't place them randomly, and pay attention to material levels!

title: Tier 0 - Stone Age > Your First Tool

Quest: Your First Tool
Quest line: Tier 0 - Stone Age

When your tinkers tables are ready, you can craft your first real tool. If you didn't find a village yet to grab some parts from the chest, you can only craft flint tools.

Let's start with a pickaxe, an axe, and a shovel.

Keep in mind that most of the original tool parts from Tinker's Construct are not shown in NEI. That doesn't mean that you can't craft them - use the tooltips on patterns and molds as guidance.

Your new tools are weak at first, but the more you use them the better they will get. You get a modifier slot after some levels, needing more as you level it up. They will level up to level 99 if you play long enough, with 20 modifier slots. Tool parts can be replaced for a bit of level XP, however the tool must be fully repaired first.

You need to level up the mining level each time you replace the parts to unleash the full power of the pickaxe. Stone->Copper for this pickaxe. If you manage to get a Zombie, Skeleton, or Creeper head, you can use it to skip the level-up process. This doesn't use up a modifier level, but does change the look until you change the pickaxe part out.

Item=Usable when mining level is X or less
Zombie=1
Skeleton=2
Creeper=4
Wither Skeleton=7
Nether Star=8

You could use a paper binding to add an extra modifier, but you will also get modifiers with tool levels.

Trophy number two brings us to chapter two of our journey through GTNHs past, the early UEV era.

The year 2022 has just begun and the UEV tier, albeit still quite empty, has become more useful than before. UEV-UMV energy hatches now have proper recipes (although with UEV parts) and optical SMDs are a thing now, hooray.
There finally are better powergen options than regular plasma turbine spam, namely naq fuel and compact fusions + XL plasma turbine spam. Technically dyson too, but that is horribly bugged and its 'legit' power output reasonably can't exceed around 6 billion EU/t (around the same as a compact MK4 running helium plasma).
Some useful newly introduced multis are the PrAss, MCR & Mega Oil Cracker and overclocks past MAX voltage are possible on megas now.
Stargate has once again become a distant goal, as it now requires exorbitant amounts of infinity catalyst and bio circuits, requiring the player to utilize the new tech to its fullest.

Two players, Phineasor & GDCloud were determined to be first to completing this goal, and after months of a close friendly race, the winner had been decided. 
GDCloud won the race and conquered this round of nerfs on the 27th of May, 2022.

P.S.: Once again, if you want to be faithful to the challenge, try completing it without these additions:
-PCB Factory, Space Elevator, Component Assemblyline, AAL, EEC, EIG, MABS
-Any bee related GT machines
-Any UEV or above multis (except weak dyson and naq refineries)
-LEG

Sometimes, basic automation isn't enough. We've heard you - we are now offering the Advanced Routing Package to allow more complex automation of your components!

The Nanopart Splitter allows splitting, merging and filtering of your components between different colored VCI and VCO hatches. In the configuration GUI, you can define rules such as:
- Merging any colors of your choice into one color
- Evenly splitting inputs from one color into many output colors
- Filtering specific components from one color to another
and many more!

We have expanded the functionality of Nanopart Splitter rules with feedback from our customers to also include ease-of-use features such as:
- Middle clicking item filters to set them to a custom rename
- Wildcard input color if no input color is selected
- Even distribution to output colors if multiple output colors are selected
- Filtering items using their normal form rather than requiring the component wrapped form

Additionally, if you purchase the Premium Package, you gain access to the Nanochip Redstone Input hatch, allowing for fine-grained redstone control of your routing. Each redstone hatch has a "channel" setting, which can then be configured in a rule for it to use that specific hatch's redstone signal. The hatch can also be used on some other modules, like the Board module (sold separately).

Ultra-high Energy Etching Array Owner's Manual:

The NAC™ will track the most recent 100,000 circuits crafted, and can be calibrated to a specific circuit type by reaching a certain percentage of circuits of this type. Mainframes count as one circuit crafted, with each tier below it counting for half as much as the last. At 60% (60,000) crystal circuits crafted, the NAC™ will become "fully calibrated" to crystal circuits.

Once that has been met, the Laser Source Hatch on the Etching Array will provide two bonuses:
- The EU Cost will be divided by each amperage interval over 256A. Example - 1,024A will divide by 2, 4,096A will divide by 3, etc.
- The Recipe Duration will be divided by (hatch tier - 9). Example - UIV will divide by 2, UMV will divide by 3, etc.

text:

Quest line: Tier 10 - UEV

We get it, this isn't the most exciting piece of the puzzle. However, the Fundamentals Package is essential to the entire operation.

Allowing things such as:
- Part Preparation for your surface mounted devices
- Wafer Cutting for your advanced silicon parts among others
- Wire Tracing for all your fine wires
- Superconductor Splitting for your most expensive circuits
- Encasement Wrapping for all your mainframe needs
- Board Immersion for the base of your circuits*

One key detail for operating your modules at maximum recommended efficiency is the input separation rule. Each module included in this and other packages offers an input separation toggle, allowing one of two operating methods:
1. Disabled: Input components will be processed separately per color, outputting to the same colored VCO

Optically Optimized Organizer Owner's Manual

The Optically Optimized Organizer requires two different grades of purified water to function. However, these are not just an extra running cost! Each grade of water 3 and above provides a bonus to the module's running stats:
- Grade 3 (1000L/s): 0.8x Water Cost (applies to both)
- Grade 4 (800L/s): 0.6x Water Cost (applies to both)
- Grade 5 (800L/s): 0.9x Recipe Duration Modifier
- Grade 6 (600L/s): 0.7x Recipe Duration Modifier
- Grade 7 (600L/s): 0.9x Recipe EU Cost
- Grade 8 (400L/s): 0.7x Recipe EU Cost

Water is only consumed while the module is running. Similar water bonuses (such as Grade 5 + Grade 6) can be applied together.

The NAC™ will track the most recent 100,000 circuits crafted, and can be calibrated to a specific circuit type by reaching a certain percentage of circuits of this type. Mainframes count as one circuit crafted, with each tier below it counting for half as much as the last. At 60% (60,000) optical circuits crafted, the NAC™ will become "fully calibrated" to optical circuits.

Once that has been met, the bonuses from each chosen water type are applied twice.

Optical circuits created by the Assembly Matrix have a 50% chance of being output in an unorganized form, requiring them to be routed back through the Optical Organizer.

title: Tier 11 - UIV > A Diode, But For Condensate
text:
Quest: A Diode, But For Condensate

At this scale, moving condensate is no longer a matter of pressure or pipe capacity. Every connected conduit becomes part of the same quantum network, allowing its contents to be observed and extracted from anywhere. What you need is a way to impose direction upon something that does not particularly care which way it travels.

Like the theoretical demon whose name it bears, the Maxwell Gate separates one state from another. Networks connected to its output may observe and pull condensate from the input, while the input remains blind to everything beyond the gate. A filter in the controller can further restrict this passage to a single type of condensate.

There is one exception: the Entanglement Apparatus sees the gate backwards. It may only push condensate from the output network toward the input network.

The Maxwell Gate is optional. It does not move condensate by itself; it only controls which side may access it.

The Gate consumes a constant 1A of UIV power whenever active, even when no condensate is passing through it.

title: Tier 11 - UIV > Assembly To The MAX+
text:
Quest: Assembly To The MAX+
Quest line: Tier 11 - UIV

The Observation Array is less an assembler than an enormous quantum router. It draws condensate from every Containment Field visible to its network, supplies power to its linked Teleportation Nodes, and presents those Nodes with the nanites demanded by each stage of their recipes. Up to sixteen Nodes may be linked to one Array, with their combined energy cost paid here.

The nanites are never consumed, but they must be exchanged constantly. Providing a higher tier than requested actually slows processing, while mixing nanite types causes the entire collection to behave as the lowest tier present. Precision, not brute force, is the key.

More than three unrequested condensates on the network will immediately fail every active recipe. Even fewer contaminants significantly reduce processing speed.

Running the same recipe across synchronized Nodes is strongly recommended. Different recipes may request incompatible nanites and contaminate one another's condensate network.

title: Tier 11 - UIV > Fluid^2 Extractor
text:
Quest: Fluid^2 Extractor
Quest line: Tier 11 - UIV

Welcome to the BEC Line! It's recommended you read the wiki for full context on these machines: https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/Bose-Einstein_Condensate_Line

Until now, manufacturing has been a matter of imposing order upon matter: heat it, compress it, shape it, and force its atoms into the arrangement you require. But the materials ahead of you have become too complex for such crude methods. No amount of mechanical precision can control every particle individually.

At temperatures approaching absolute zero, another possibility emerges. As a cloud of bosons loses its thermal motion, the quantum waves describing its particles spread and begin to overlap. Enough of them eventually occupy the same low energy state that the cloud ceases to behave like a collection of independent particles. Instead, it acts as a single coherent quantum system: a Bose-Einstein condensate.

The first step is using the Entanglement Apparatus to convert ordinary fluids into entangled condensate by brute-forcing this delicate state on an industrial scale. It cannot overclock; instead, it expands the experiment across unlimited parallels, processing as much material as the supplied power can sustain. Multi-amp and laser energy hatches will be necessary if you intend to feed the rest of the BEC Line at any meaningful rate.

Different fluids may be entangled simultaneously, although the entire batch runs for the duration of the slowest active conversion.

Insert ordinary fluids through the input hatch at the front. Entangled condensate leaves through the BEC Hatch at the rear and is pushed into the connected Containment Field network.

The Apparatus does not check whether sufficient storage is available before processing. Use a BEC Detector Hatch to disable it before your Containment Fields overflow and begin voiding condensate.

Quest line: Tier 11 - UIV

The solution? Using the sheer force of gravity. By using extreme amounts of explosive force on your fourth-dimensionally engineered tesseracts, you can tear tiny rifts in the fabric of space, enough to create a seed which can birth a black hole. If you can build a machine which can harness it, it will be able to compress even the strongest materials to the most dense states possible.

Taming a black hole is no easy task - even with all of your precautions, it defies your efforts to stabilize it and attempts to collapse itself constantly. Meaningfully extending the lifespan of the black hole will be extremely difficult. By bending spacetime through carefully aligned glass, you can reverse the flow of hawking radiation back into the black hole and keep it completely stable - problematically, however, the amount of spacetime required to maintain this process increases at an exponential rate.

As the black hole decays, it becomes even more powerful - but be wary, as it will eventually become unstable and you will no longer be able to recover your items from the edge of the event horizon. To safely close the black hole and restart this process, you have engineered a collapser out of the same fourth-dimensional materials.

The Pseudostable Black Hole Containment Field is the most powerful compressor in the game, capable of creating superdense plates out of any material, as well as being able to perform more advanced neutronium compressor recipes that will save incredible amounts of resources.

You must use programmed circuits in the input buses to determine if the machine will act as a Compressor or Neutronium Compressor!

title: Tier 11 - UIV > Quantum Tank X
text:
Quest: Quantum Tank X
Quest line: Tier 11 - UIV

A Bose-Einstein condensate cannot simply be poured into a larger tank. Its particles have surrendered their individual identities, behaving as a single coherent quantum state. Storing it requires continuously forcing that state to remain confined and the moment that force disappears, so does everything you stored.

The Containment Field holds every variety of entangled condensate on its network. Its field strength determines both its capacity and its appetite for power: every unit of strength provides another litre of storage while consuming another EU/t. The contents cannot be partitioned or filtered, so careful monitoring will be essential.

Exceeding the configured capacity does not stop more condensate from entering. Instead, the unstable field begins destroying 11% of every stored condensate each second until it returns below the limit.

A power failure or manually disabling the machine immediately voids the entire contents of the Containment Field. Keep its power supply exceptionally reliable.

A BEC Detector Hatch can monitor total or filtered condensate levels and disable the Entanglement Apparatus before the field overflows.

title: Tier 11 - UIV > Tunnels Of Light
text:
Quest: Tunnels Of Light
Quest line: Tier 11 - UIV

Despite its name, the Teleportation Node does not send your components elsewhere to be assembled. The entire recipe is processed inside the Node; power, condensate, and nanites are brought to it remotely by the Observation Array.

Once the solid inputs arrive, the Node begins processing immediately, even if the required condensate has not yet been provided. The Observation Array must deliver everything before the recipe completes, or the process fails and the inputs are lost. There is no energy hatch on the Node; its full power cost is paid through the linked Observation Array.

The Line-of-Sight Hatches on the Node and Observation Array must face one another, share the same Y-level, and be no more than 128 blocks apart. No cable is required between them.

Increasing parallels only allows larger batches. Processing speed falls proportionally, so total throughput does not increase. Scale the line by building additional Teleportation Nodes instead.

Introducing the final multiblock in the game, and by far the most expensive.
It introduces 4 new materials: Raw Stellar Plasma, White and Black Dwarf Matter and finally Universium.

It has 3 different tiered casings with 9 tiers each:

Spacetime Compression Field Generator:
- Determines the tier of the planet block that can be run and decreases the processing time by 3% per tier.

Time Dilation Field Generator:
- Decreases recipe time by 50% per tier, while decreasing the chance of a recipe succeeding by 9.25% per tier.

Stabilisation Field Generator:
- Increases the chance of a recipe succeeding by 5% per tier, while decreasing the output of a recipe by 5% per tier.

Lower tier Stabilization Field Generators have a power output penalty.

Finding the best setup of different casing tiers might be a hard task, so use this calculator to evaluate setups and visualize drops: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1FTFdfmY_UWbTbFOyNzARKeI90pbHvPBH6M3JHJmaC-E/edit?usp=sharing

Be sure to read the tooltip of the Eye of Harmony controller, it explains everything in detail! Depending on your GUI scale it might have multiple pages.

Well... it explains mostly everything. The Eye of Harmony has an inbuilt pity system to make sure you don't lose your mind. Here's a quick rundown on how it operates:

(All chances are decimals here)
There is a counter C that starts at the current recipe success chance P. If a recipe fails, (1-P)*P is added to C. If C reaches >= 1, the next roll is guaranteed to succeed and C resets to P. 
If a recipe succeeds before C reaches >= 1, it resets in a similar manner.
If you switch recipes, C will be reset to P of the new recipe, even if the next roll would be a guarantee.
The guarantee can be canceled out by overflow penalties as they apply after the pity does. However, they do not reset C, so the guarantee is shifted to the next recipe cycle.
If parallels are > 1, pity doesn't apply.

title: Tier 12 - UMV > Convergence
text:
Quest: Convergence
Quest line: Tier 12 - UMV

Running your Dimensionally Transcendent Plasma Forge for an extended period (8 hours) allows the Multidimensional Spaces to align perfectly.

With your newly acquired technology, you can now tap into these spaces in perfect sync, enabling your plasma forges to operate at incredible speeds.

The Transdimensional Alignment Matrix allows the DTPF to run with Perfect Overclocks. To achieve this, you need a full discount, and the extra power cost is offset by using more of the same catalyst.

Overall, it is more efficient and totally worth it.

This process is extremely catalyst-hungry. Ensure you're producing enough to sustain it.

For recipes without a catalyst, you must specify the catalyst in the GUI by right-clicking the Convergence button, otherwise it will default to Crude.

Math for the curious:

To clear up what exactly happens in the background, here's an explanation on how the extra catalyst values are calculated using an example:

The example recipe of choice is the molten neutronium recipe using prosaic catalyst, running at 64A UMV (8,589,934,592 EU/t).
The recipe uses 14,753L of Prosaic catalyst and 36,484,545,600 EU per recipe without OCs or the catalyst discount. With the discount, the catalyst amount gets cut in half, meaning 7,376.5L of catalyst, which are rounded to 7,376L, and due to the 64A UMV the machine is supplied with the recipe overclocks 3 times, meaning each recipe actually uses 36,484,545,600 * 2^3 = 291,876,364,800 EU.

Knowing the amount of OCs and the base voltage of the recipe, the difference of the needed EU per recipe with and without perfect OC can be calculated, that being 291,876,364,800 - 36,484,545,600 = 255,391,819,200 extra EU due to imperfect OCs.
To get the value of needed extra catalyst, this extra EU value has to be divided by the energy density of the relevant catalyst, prosaic in this case.

The division equates to 255,391,819,200 EU / 66,768,460 EU/L = 3,825.037 L, rounded to 3,825L extra prosaic catalyst per recipe. For the final step, this value has to be multiplied by 0.5 as it's affected by the discount, meaning the total extra catalyst that gets added to the recipe is 3,825L * 0.5 = 1,912.5 L, rounded to 1,912L.

To summarize it all in a formula:
Amount extra catalyst per recipe = (B * ((2^x) - 1))/2L
where:
B is base total EU of the recipe
x is the number of overclocks
L is the EU/L of the relevant catalyst

title: Tier 12 - UMV > Stars, So Many Stars

Quest: Stars, So Many Stars
Quest line: Tier 12 - UMV

You know the drill, you give 2 stargates' worth of stuff, you get your trophy. Simple as that.

Our journey through time continues onwards, entering the UMV, aka DTPF era.

Surprisingly, it still is the year 2022, but there have been a huge amount of changes since our last stop in the UEV era. The DTPF exists now, hypogen & eternal coils included, and machine parts up to UMV thus are craftable. Wireless energy is a thing now too, both the LSC and the regular hatch kind, and AE2FC is in the pack, allowing direct fluid crafting (meaning no more volumetric flask shuffling).
The power situation hasn't changed much since the UEV era, except for dyson being even more bugged and giving free uncapped infinite power (abusing this was obviously labeled as bugabuse).
Some other new useful things are the MABS, Integrated Ore Factory, Space Elevator, UIV and UMV singleblocks, EIG, EEC, industrial & mega apiary, yottanks, stocking buses, data bank chaining and the Draconic Fusion Crafter.
The stargate's cost has now skyrocketed far more than ever before, marking the beginning of this new era of GT:NH endgame, the era of expansion.

This time around the leading GDCloud was challenged by the team Neo Caelestia, who were progressing at a staggering speed, inching ever closer to being first to gate, but ultimately weren't able to fully catch up and thus GDCloud once again was first to conquer the challenge on the 19th of November, 2022.

-Multi-Amp wireless hatches
-Sub 1-tick OC, Batch Mode, inbuilt Void Protection on multis

title: Tier 1 - LV > Analyzing the Soil
text:
Quest: Analyzing the Soil
Quest line: Tier 1 - LV

Tired of looking for ores by hand? Want to find underground oil that will last a long time? A seismic prospector will tell you the ores in the surrounding chunks in a (sorta) handy book you can read, and also the underground fluids beneath you. It doesn't need to be powered.

To determine which kind of fluid there is in the chunk you need to scan the soil by right-clicking an Advanced Seismic Prospector with 2 Powderbarrels, 4 Glyceryl Trinitrate cells, 8 iTNT or 16 TNT. This one doesn't explode the user too on use. Features! There are four types of oil or natural gas for the overworld. See the quest in Tips and Tricks once you've made an oil drill.

1) Right-click explosives.
2) Use a single Data Stick to extract the data by right-clicking on it after the animation has finished. Each will hold ONE result.
3) Next you need to put the data stick in a GT scanner to have it analyzed.
4) Place the analyzed data stick in the bottom right slot of a printer and add 3 paper in the top left slot and make sure you have at least 144L squid ink in it.
5) Take the printed pages and combine it with a piece of leather in an assembling machine filled with at least 20 mb of refined glue.

TADA! Now you have a book with detailed info about the chunks you scanned. Visual Prospecting adds the information to your map the moment you make the book.

Data Sticks are not easy (or possible) to make right now, so do not lose them. You can put it in a crafting table to erase it when done.

Ore locations are given as the center of the chunk. Ores that are marginal in that chunk may not be found in the center but on an edge. Look at where ores are located and determine the center of the vein. At higher tiers, it scans more chunks for ores. If you just want to know about fluids, use the lower tier version so the book isn't as long.

Each underground fluid field is 8x8 chunks. This starts at 0,0 and continues for 8 chunks east and south, containing 64 chunks. Not all fields have anything in them though. Within the field the amount can vary +/- 25 percent. The amount reported in the book is the minimum and maximum per field across all chunks in the field. The prospector reports on 3x3 fields (as in, 9 fields of 8x8 chunks) at all tiers with the center field where the seismic prospector is located. Fluid extraction rate depends on many factors, check the wiki for details. In general, anything above 300 is really good. The total amount in the chunk is complicated.

Tasks:

Rewards: 4 × Data Stick; 64 × Powderbarrel; enhancedlootbags:lootbag:4; 5 × Coin "The Technician 10"

title: Tier 1 - LV > Biomes Everywhere, But Not the One You Want?
text:
Quest: Biomes Everywhere, But Not the One You Want?
Quest line: Tier 1 - LV

Tired of searching all over the map for that Bamboo Forest or Tropical Rainforest? Desperate for clay dust and need to find a Canyon or Mesa biome? Nature's compass will lead you to the biome you're looking for, if it's within its range.

The compass menu has the following functionality:
* When Sorted By: Name, you can filter the list by name or its parts. The search is case-insensitive.
* You can search by keys and their combinations. For instance, name: bamboo, climate: warm, bh: -1.8, tag: forest.
All available keys are:
name,
climate [hellish, hot, warm, normal, cold, icy],
baseheight | bh (float, can be negative),
heightvariation | hv (float),
rainfall | rain (float),
temperature | temp (float),
humidity [damp, normal, arid],
tags.

Some things to keep in mind:
* Biomes from other dimensions show up on the list, don't bother searching for those unless you're in that dimension.
* In general, the full list has biomes that are not generated by Realistic World Generator, like Sunflower Plains.
* Radius 10000 means it couldn't find the biome. In this case after the initial search, its menu will show only the biomes in the 10k radius. Use Shift+RMB to see the whole list again.
* You can try again at a different location - the range is 10k from your current position.
* Artificially created biomes count, so remove them if you want to find a natural one.
* There's lots of different 'versions' of biomes under the same category, so if you want a tropical one for tropical bees, there are actually a bunch of places you can get it.
* For those who don't mind the freeze when searching, the radius can be changed in a config. The HUD position can also be changed in the config.

title: Tier 1 - LV > Choices, Choices
text:
Quest: Choices, Choices
Quest line: Tier 1 - LV

Need a map on fuel choices? Well, we don't have that, but we have suggestions. You can use Steam up to IV, but beyond MV it gets pretty painful.

In LV you can start refining oil for either Light Fuel for a Combustion Generator or Refinery Gas for a Gas Turbine. Or you can use Creosote in a Semi-Fluid Generator.

Once you hit MV, you can switch from Steam to renewable Benzene (Gas) from your logs. Other renewable alternatives are Fish Oil or Seed Oil based bio diesel (combustion). Seed Oil can be sourced from Pam's peanuts, Canola or Forestry tree nuts.

At MV you can also upgrade your Light Fuel with Heavy Fuel to get Diesel. When you reach HV turn diesel or bio diesel into Cetane Boosted Diesel. In EV, you can make High Octane Gasoline (HOG), but it's complex, and you'll need to rejigger your whole oil distillation setup, since it uses different fluids than Cetane does.

EV introduces the Large Gas Turbine, Large Steam Turbine, Large HP Steam Turbine, and Large Combustion Engine, which are more efficient versions of the earlier ones. The first 3 require turbines.

You can also make Nukes, or Wind and Water Kinetics.

For low-power operations, or dedicated players willing to set up autocrafting, you can begin using Solar Panels at MV.

Prerequisites: Welcome to Tier 1, LV
