title: Tier 1 - LV > Gallium Arsenide Crystal
text:
Quest: Gallium Arsenide Crystal
Quest line: Tier 1 - LV

The diode requires gallium arsenide, and you may be wondering how to get gallium or arsenic this early in the game.

Sphalerite and zinc are the primary sources of gallium at this tier.

You can find sphalerite in sulfur veins at Y 5-20, and the small zinc ores in the Overworld or the Nether at Y 80-210. You won't find much on the Overworld because of obvious reasons. To get additional zinc crushed ore drops, use a Tinker's Construct tool with the Luck (Fortune) enchant on it, probably the best use for all that lapis you got while looking for calcite. Or use a miner, if you don't mind how slow it is.

- Sphalerite can be electrolyzed for a small chance of a gallium dust. Better put in a lot or you might get unlucky.
- Zinc crushed ore can be washed and then thermal centrifuged or forge hammered and then centrifuged. But you don't always get the crushed ore as a drop, the impure dust doesn't give gallium.

You can get arsenic from realgar small ores in the Nether at Y 15-85. Centrifuge the dusts in a centrifuge.

Other sources are Tinker's Construct cobalt ore in the nether and cobaltite ore in the Twilight Forest. You can use your EBF for that. You also need to level up your pickaxe to ardite or make an Ironwood Pickaxe or LV Miner to harvest cobalt ore.

Another way to get gallium and arsenic is with XP buckets in a crafting grid if you're really desperate.

With your EBF you can combine these two dusts to make a Gallium Arsenide Crystal.

Tasks:
- Retrieve (optional): Gallium Dust; Arsenic Dust
- Retrieve: Gallium Arsenide Crystal
Rewards: choose one of: Gallium Dust; Arsenic Dust; enhancedlootbags:lootbag:4; 3 × Coin "The Chemist 10"; 3 × Coin "The Technician 10"
Prerequisites: EBF-Time; Electrically Separating Dusts

title: Tier 1 - LV > Getting Ready for Tier 2, MV
text:
Quest: Getting Ready for Tier 2, MV
Quest line: Tier 1 - LV

In order to proceed forward, you need to get Raw Aluminum. A lot of it. But for now, 8 is enough to complete this quest.

Your first option is alumina dust. Probably the best source for alumina is clay or terracotta from canyons, however you need an MV machine for that, so you need to find an alternative until you have enough dust for your initial setup. For now, you can get it by centrifuging various impure piles from your ores or by smelting ruby, sapphire, or green sapphire in an EBF with carbon. Check the EBF quest in the Multiblock Goals.

You will also need an EBF to turn the alumina into aluminium ingots. For that you need cryolite. Go visit the Twilight Forest for that and find a Cryolite vein. The related quest "Lead, Galena, Silver and Cryolite" is in the Novice Thaumaturgy tab.

Your second option is to use aluminium dust. However, you can not smelt that directly yet, even if you have an EBF. That will require higher heat levels. For now, you will have to either use a Tinker's Smeltery or a GT Compressor to turn the dust into raw aluminium which you can then smelt into ingots in the EBF.

By the time you've completed this, you'll probably be done with most of the tab, but you'll still need Good Circuits (MV) to actually open up the next tier if you haven't done that yet.

You might also want to check the Getting Around and Without Dying tabs for new unlocks.

When you unlock them, Super buffers can be lag sources, so be careful to keep them as empty as possible. If you end up using a multiblock packager, be sure to change the buffer from Stocking mode to Transfer Size mode.

title: Tier 1 - LV > Long Distance Fluid Pipeline
text:
Quest: Long Distance Fluid Pipeline
Quest line: Tier 1 - LV

Wouldn't it be great if you could transport your oil from a far away oil spout or oil field by pipes to your base?

This is not a problem anymore. Connect your setup on the start and end point with a Long Distance Fluid Pipeline block. In between use the associated pipe blocks - the total distance between endpoints must be more than 64 blocks apart (4 or more chunks). There can only be one start and end point per pipeline.

To actually connect it, you need to align the start LDFP block such that the arrows are facing inwards, and the opposite side of it has a LDFPP block. Put a pump on the side of the block that has the arrows and set to import. It will now attempt to import fluid to the endpoint LDFP. This will go as fast as you can put fluid into it.

Do the opposite on the far side, except you don't need a pump.

Now you only need to chunkload the start and end points and the fluid will be "teleported" to you.

Of course, later on you'll probably use ender tanks to actually teleport the fluid, especially from other dims.

This setup is lag-free in the pipe blocks, so it's useful in your base as well if you want to reduce lag.

Tasks:
- Retrieve: 2 × Long Distance Fluid Pipeline
- Retrieve: 64 × Long Distance Fluid Pipeline Pipe
Rewards: 2 × Electric Pump (LV); 2 × irontank:goldTank; 15 × Coin "The Technician 1"
Prerequisites: Hello Baron, How's Your Black Gold Today?

In between use the associated pipe blocks - the total distance between endpoints must be more than 64 blocks apart (4 or more chunks). There can only be one start and end point per pipeline.

To actually connect it, you need to align the start LDIP block such that the arrows are facing inwards, and the opposite side of it has a LDIPP block. Put a conveyor on the side of the block that has the arrows and set to import. It will now attempt to import stuff to the endpoint LDIP. This will go as fast as you can put items into it.

Do the opposite on the far side, except you don't need a conveyor.

Now you only need to chunkload the start and end points and the items will be "teleported" to you.

Of course, later on you'll probably use ender chests to actually teleport the ore, especially from other dims.

This setup is lag-free in the pipe blocks, so it's useful in your base as well if you want to reduce lag.

title: Tier 1 - LV > Reading the Grid
text:
Quest: Reading the Grid
Quest line: Tier 1 - LV

While the GT EU Meter can inspect one cable or machine at a time, troubleshooting a large power network that way quickly becomes rather tedious. If only there was a dedicated tool for that...

The Network Analyzer displays the entire connected EU network directly in the world, allowing you to follow power from generators to machines and identify dangerous sections before they become craters.

Right-click a GT cable to bind the Analyzer to its network, then keep it in your hand to display the overlay. You can also use it on a multiblock controller to inspect the networks connected to all of its Energy and Dynamo Hatches.

You can shift-right-click to cycle through its five modes:
- Topology displays the complete network and its worst case condition.
- Critical displays only overloaded or otherwise dangerous sections.
- Active displays cables that are currently carrying amperage.
- Amperage compares the expected load with each cable’s capacity.
- Voltage displays expected cable loss and warns about cables or machines receiving excessive voltage.

Orange nodes are power sources, cyan nodes are consumers, and green nodes are forks in the network. Gray indicates an idle or unknown section, green is safe, yellow warns of significant voltage loss, and red indicates an overload, a cable that may burn, or a machine that may explode.

Look directly at a node to see more detailed information about amperage, voltage loss, and any detected problems.

Amperage mode displays the potential load of the connected machines, while Active mode shows what is actually carrying power at that moment.

Machines from other mods cannot always report their real amperage requirements. The Analyzer must estimate their consumption, so readings for IC2 machines, reactors, and other non-GT consumers may be inaccurate.

title: Tier 1 - LV > You're Gonna Hate This #2
text:
Quest: You're Gonna Hate This #2
Quest line: Tier 1 - LV

The second item you'll need a lot of. When you want to get fluid out of tanks you'll need one.

Attach it to fluid pipes or GT machines/blocks. Adjust the flow direction and redstone behavior with a screwdriver. Place it on the side facing the tank or machine. When looking at a pipe or machine, you can use the grid to place it on a side already touching another thing. You can use the grid with a screwdriver to adjust a cover on that side as well.

When a GT pipe or machine has any cover, including a pump cover, wrenching the machine back into an item keeps the cover on that machine. The cover stays with the machine in the same direction when it is placed down again. This way you can arrange pump and conveyor covers on a machine outside a tight spot and place it there. To remove covers, use the crowbar.

It can also be further upgraded into a fluid regulator that allows precise control of fluid transfer speed.

You can access covers interface with Shift+RMB.

title: Tier 2 - MV > Conduit Probe
text:
Quest: Conduit Probe
Quest line: Tier 2 - MV

The Conduit Probe is an incredibly useful tool for managing and troubleshooting your Ender IO conduit networks.

It features two modes:

• Probe Mode
Right-click an Energy Conduit to view detailed network information
Right-click an Item Conduit to simulate item transport using the item in your hand
Right-click a Redstone Conduit to see connection details, including signal levels sent and received

• Copy/Paste Mode
Shift + Right-click a conduit connection to copy its settings
Right-click another conduit to paste those settings

This is especially useful when configuring multiple machines with identical setups and helps prevent mistakes.

You can switch between modes by: Using Shift + Mouse Wheel, or pressing the Yeta Wrench Mode keybind (unbound by default) while holding the probe.

The detector's setting can be changed by clicking on the +/- texture with a screwdriver. Also, in general, better (and larger) turbines work better at cleaning up pollution. The code is too complex to fully explain here, but that's basically it. More EU turbine = more pollution cleaning turbine.

This quest covers one method of combating pollution - there are others, including not making as much to begin with.

text:

After that you need to process it like a normal ore until you get Rare Earth (I) Dust.

After running the Dust through your Dehydrator, you get a number of strange materials, only some of which you recognize. But if you run these materials through an Electrolyzer or through the Dehydrator again, you may get some use out of them. Some of them may take quite a few to do so, but you have been stockpiling, right? You'll need 204 Rare Earth.

You believe if you had more powerful acids and machines, you could extract even more valuable materials out of the Rare Earth.

title: Tier 2 - MV > Gut-Enough For You? Bet You Thought Newspapers Were Dead!
text:
Quest: Gut-Enough For You? Bet You Thought Newspapers Were Dead!
Quest line: Tier 2 - MV

When used together, the Typesetting Table and Printing Press allow you to duplicate enchanted books. You'll need a lot of XP, so either build a mob grinder or get farming. A Fortune III book, for example, requires 40 levels to convert into an enchanted plate.

To use the Typesetting Table, place a print press chase in the top slot and an enchanted book in the bottom left slot. Sneak right-click the enchanted book to convert it into an enchanted plate if you have enough XP.

To use the Printing Press, place an enchanted plate in the center of the machine, ink sacs on the top metal plate, and books on the bottom left side of the counter. It immediately starts processing without any power or redstone signal.

Wearing Reading Glasses, Tinted Glasses, or a Monocle will display more information about these blocks when looking at them.

Each enchanted plate can make three enchanted books before breaking, but the trick is to make two books and then repair it in a Thaumic Restorer for unlimited uses.

You'll need some Thaumium ingots. You can get into Thaumcraft, find some in a chest, or try breeding the Thaumium oreberry crop.

Whether these are worth it to save a little power or not is up to you of course. Also note that although they're wires, you aren't hurt by coming into contact with them.

title: Tier 2 - MV > Ore Processing, Kind Of...
text:
Quest: Ore Processing, Kind Of...
Quest line: Tier 2 - MV

The endless war between macerators and SAG mills rages on eternally, so why does it matter which one you choose?

HV Macerators are still required for the final byproducts on many ore chains, but a SAG mill still shines through with upgraded grinding heads! SAG mills are the perfect machine for getting the most from your ores without using bees and crops. You can get bonus outputs with tungsten grinding heads, but that doesn't mean you can dupe materials (like ingots) with it. Plus for many of them you'll get the final output directly without any need for further processing. Handy for processing Redstone to get Chrome!

It's great for lead, copper, tin, silver, nickel, redstone, ruby, lapis, certus quartz, and malachite ores. Other ores will give you better outputs as well if you use a good enough head.

Even coal, charcoal, bones, wheat, ender pearls, and charcoal non-ores will give bonus outputs.

That said, the GT ones are still way faster later on.

text:
Quest: Pipes, Pipes Everywhere
Quest line: Tier 2 - MV

The reward - restrictive item pipes - allow you to prioritize destinations. Locations on the other side of a restrictive pipe are treated as much further away than locations on the same side of a pipe. Very handy when you want overflow (or non-matching) items to go somewhere else!

For higher tiers, look up "item pipe" in NEI or use the wiki: https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/Fluid_%26_Item_Pipes

title: Tier 2 - MV > Portable Prospecting Tool
text:
Quest: Portable Prospecting Tool
Quest line: Tier 2 - MV

Now that you have some tech, you've discovered a way to prospect for ores.

Unfortunately, the tech to make it repairable or rechargeable doesn't work, so you'll have to make a new one each time it breaks. It does work better at higher tiers and lasts longer with better materials.

It doesn't make a convenient book like the Seismic Prospector, but you can look at the results of scanning on the map, thanks to Visual Prospecting.

It can be hard to choose a good material for the Basic Prospector. Here are some good choices for you in their respective tiers, the size searched, and the average amount of veins they can scan:

LV Vanadiumsteel 3x3 - 50
MV Vanadiumsteel 3x3 - 213
HV Vibrant Alloy 5x5 - 299
EV Shadow Metal 7x7 - 1080
IV Oriharukon 7x7 - 2649

As you can see, the prospectors become better and better with each tier, but it might also be worth looking around for better materials.

Good luck.

However, the raw silicon dust you obtained is not pure enough! We will need to work on that. There are two reasonable options to do so. Let us look at the first one here. The Chlorine and Sodium are not lost during this process. To recover them, just electrolyze the Salt you get at the end and send it back to the Chemical Reactors, for a complete loop that turns Raw Silicon into Solar Grade Silicon.

By simply burning coal as fuel, this machine produces RF power. Enough for a basic machine setup. This machine will also accept compressed and multiple-compressed blocks. Want to burn something for 250+ days? Also, with double or octadic capacitors the output will increase and efficiency will improve.

GT wiring can convert EU to RF, but not the other way around. Note that with the eNet changes a GT wire network will need at least one GT energy consumer - a machine hull of the matching voltage will work.

Ender IO machines and GT cables and Wires can be left safely out in the rain.

It might be useful for Genetics machines since they consume excessive power when attached to GT wiring - Forestry and EnderIO machines work fine (except for the Thermionic Fabricator). Or use a Capacitor Bank.

title: Tier 2 - MV > Welcome to the Church of Benzene
text:
Quest: Welcome to the Church of Benzene
Quest line: Tier 2 - MV

If you made it to MV using steam, you're probably wondering how to survive going further. One option is to switch to Light Fuel, discussed in LV. Another option is to use Benzene. Benzene is made from Wood Tar. There are a couple of pathways for that. Both start with logs from trees.

One path is to use Coke Ovens or Advanced Coke Ovens to make Charcoal, and fluid-extract Wood Tar from it. Then distill the Wood Tar to make Benzene. This method produces less pollution, but will also provide less Benzene.

The second path is to use the Pyrolyze Oven multiblock and Nitrogen gas to extract Wood Tar and Charcoal. Fluid-extract the Charcoal for additional Wood Tar. Then proceed as above. This method will create pollution from the Pyrolyze Oven, but will provide more Benzene per log.

Excess wood tar can also be turned into Toluene, a key ingredient for explosives that you'll need later on to make rockets.

If you use the Charcoal Byproducts recipe, you can get a plethora of useful byproducts as well, but you'll need 4 DTs.

Later on, you will get an even better option: the Industrial Coke Oven.

title: Tier 3 - HV > Fluoro-who now?
text:
Quest: Fluoro-who now?
Quest line: Tier 3 - HV

Fluorophlogopite is the industrial answer to Mica-based foils, and something you'll want to start investing in as higher tier coils cost increasingly more foil to make.

The recipe for making Raw Fluorophlogopite Dust is done in the MV mixer. While all of the new dusts involved may look a little daunting, they're not that bad. You will need the following:

- Some variant of quartz dust: Any one of Quartz Sand, Quartzite, Nether Quartz, or Certus Quartz
- Alumina
- Potassiumfluorosilicate, which is made in two steps by combining Rock Salt, Hydrofluoric Acid, and Raw Silicon
- Potassium Carbonate, made by combining Potassium Dust and Oxygen (or Potash to cover both) with Carbon Dioxide in a Chemical Reactor

The exact ratios of each ingredient depend on the form of quartz that you're using, as does the exact amount of raw dust that you get from the recipe.

Technically, this process is entirely optional, but highly recommended. The raw dust is also used in ZPM, but Mica can be substituted for that use case if you would like.

title: Tier 3 - HV > Integrated Processor
text:

This one doesn't really have a consistent naming scheme unlike the later ones, but it still works the same way, aside from the fact that you get your first EV and IV circuits from it, all the rest only have 1 new tier of circuit. Because of this you'll need to make 2 new CAs to finish it.

The first one is the Integrated Processor, the final type of MV circuits. You also don't need to craft any other circuits to make it, so it's the cheapest. This repeats each circuit tier.

This and all circuits past it need a cleanroom.

Then, we find that a fluid solidifier isn't good enough, so we need to use our Vacuum Freezer to solidify the molten material in a plate mold.

You can simply use your new HV Bender to bend the plates into a foil, and there we have it! No more scouring the planet for rare Mica veins every time you want to make more coils!

Quest line: Tier 3 - HV

There are a number of chemical recipes that are unlocked with an HV Chemical Reactor; you will finally be able to make Ender Eyes, Ammonia, Gelled Toluene, and plenty of other useful components. 

Alternatively, if you're up for it, you can head over to the Mass Processing tab and build yourself a Large Chemical Reactor (LCR) instead! In addition to having a more efficient overclock, the LCR can input multiple liquids so you won't need to mess with those pesky cells any longer. 

If you choose to go the LCR route, be sure to take a look at the PTFE questline just ahead of this one, starting with "Teflon Don".

P.S. You can skip any of the following rubber/plastic questlines by holding 128 of the respective sheets in your hand!

title: Tier 3 - HV > Personal Dimension
text:
Quest: Personal Dimension
Quest line: Tier 3 - HV

Tired of mobs in your base? Want to build somewhere... different? Probably in a personal dimension? Then this is your chance.

When you first activate the portal, you can configure the world to your liking: it can be a void world, or a superflat world made up of any blocks you find available on the list.

Be careful! Once you configure the world, you can only change the cosmetic settings such as sky color by shift-right-clicking the portal.

Editing world generation settings after the world is created is only possible if a server administrator unlocks it for you via the /pspace allow-worldgen-change DIMID command.

PS: The Last Millenium is also a void dimension you could use.

If you're used to the buggy garden/void dimensions from UtilityWorlds, this is now a new mod that should resolve most of the previously known issues with blood magic, etc.

Prerequisites: Titanium, Finally

You may also consider centrifuging ashes if you use a benzene setup, extracting it from combs if you use bees, or obtaining it from the Fertilia crop. title: Tier 3 - HV > Some Rare High Tier Metals
text:
Quest: Some Rare High Tier Metals
Quest line: Tier 3 - HV

Platinum, Palladium, Iridium and Osmium can be extracted with a chemical reaction from Chalcopyrite and Pentlandite using sulfuric acid. You don't have the technology to process them properly right now but later on you need large amounts of them.

Note that this is not the proper method to get rare metals. This means none of them are pure, and cannot be utilized without the platline method, aside from EBF-ing platinum. title: Tier 3 - HV > UU-Matter
text:
Quest: UU-Matter
Quest line: Tier 3 - HV

Now you can actually make the UUM with a Mass Fabricator. Well, technically you could make it without UUA, but that's way more expensive. To make sure it only runs with UUA, put a programmed circuit (any value) in the machine's slot. UU-Matter can be used for some very specific things, such as replicating some materials (check NEI, mostly/all periodic table), used with crops to create an ore, some specific high-level recipes need it, and...you can also sit in it to get regen.

The energy usage and overclocking of the Mass Fabricator is different from the usual GT way. To have fixed EU to UUM ratios for all tiers, the machine does 2/2 OC. It also starts with a very high amperage in LV. The following chart should make it more clear:

Tier  Amps       EU/t         Time
LV     8A         256          160
MV     4A         512           80
HV     2A        1024           40
EV     1A        2048           20
IV     0.5A      4096           10
etc.

Put in power (and hopefully UUA), and out comes UUM.

For now, just stockpile the UU matter. You need data orbs to use the replicator, and that's explained next tier.

You only need to fulfill one of the listed Mass Fabricator requirements.

title: Tier 4 - EV > Power of the Sun from Nuclear
text:
Quest: Power of the Sun from Nuclear
Quest line: Tier 4 - EV

Your good old singleblock Molecular Transformer is gone. So, how do you obtain Sunnarium? Well, there are a couple of ways, but at EV you'll need to radiate Glowstone and convert it to Sunnarium.

The Glowstone rod will slowly charge up if you put it next to any fuel rod in your IC2 reactor. The exact charging speed is (number of rods adjacent) * (floor(hull temperature/3000) + 1) per second. A dual rod counts as 2 rods, and a quad fuel rod counts as 4 rods for this purpose. The Glowstone rod will neither emit heat, nor cause other components to emit more heat. You can treat this rod as reactor plating in the IC2 Reactor Planner.

As you can see, the speed is directly proportional to hull temperature and adjacent rods. At the very extreme, you can fully charge up a Glowstone rod in less than half a minute and output one Sunnarium every 10 seconds (on average, since cells aren't charged at the same speed due to their different positions), but that requires a very considerable amount of resources to set up. It also involves a vacuum freezer to cool down the coolant cells and running the reactor at 66000+ hull temperature. Balance your needs and your resource situation wisely.

The wiki has good advice for reactor planning: https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/Nuclear_Reactors

Replace the Containment Reactor Plating with actual Glowstone rods and you should be good to go. You can also use fewer reactor chambers by using less plating. Enjoy!

- Retrieve: Fuel Rod (Sunnarium)
- Retrieve: Sunnarium Dust

After it decays, you can electrolyze Radon out of it and progress into the next circuit line. However, you will not be able to do the Radon loop here, that can only be done with Plutonium 239.

The Infinite Spray Can never runs out of paint, and contains all sixteen colors (as well as solvent!) Of course, line mode and Ring of Loki support are included. There are also many convenience features. Middle-click to open a color choice GUI. Middle-click a painted block to copy its color to the spray can. Left-click to cycle the active color (sneak to go backwards.) Sneak-middle-click to lock the can; while locked, you can't accidentally change the color. Sneak-middle-click to unlock.

You can also hold it in your offhand to automatically spray any colorable block you place with your main hand.

Naturally, you'll have to craft the infinite spray can yourself. It's a Dire Crafting recipe, so hopefully you have a dire crafting table. It requires a lot of platinum line materials, of course. And, apparently, a rainbow cactus, so a small detour into magic will be necessary. And a bunch of random-looking AE2 parts. And an IV world accelerator. And... a fence?

title: Tier 5 - IV > Long term planner?
text:
Quest: Long term planner?
Quest line: Tier 5 - IV

Well get ready for a processing line.

First you need to react Thorium Dust with Hydrofluoric Acid and eight buckets of Nitric Acid. I hope you have a Nitric Acid setup.

Then react the Thorium Nitrate with Sodium Hydroxide to produce Thorium Hydroxide. Then react with even more Hydrofluoric Acid to get Thorium Tetrafluoride.

Then pump it into a Centrifuge to separate the normal Thorium away from the Thorium 232. Sadly it is still in a liquid form so you will need to blast it with Zinc Chloride and Calcium.

Then finally use your Blast Furnace again for the Zn-Th alloy ingot to separate the Zinc from the Thorium 232 to obtain the Thorium 232 Dust and even get your Zinc back in fluid form.

Well I hope you enjoyed the processing line for Thorium 232 EBF edition.

title: Tier 5 - IV > Thorium 232?
text:
Quest: Thorium 232?
Quest line: Tier 5 - IV

So you were looking at Thorium 232 and wondering how to make it?

You could centrifuge it using a long recipe with a horrible output chance, but there are better ways to obtain it.

There are three processing paths, although the third is not unlocked until after you unlock Fusion and gain access to the Neutron Activator.

The first path requires the Chemical Plant multiblock, which you may not be familiar with. It is the fastest path, requiring only two steps to obtain Thorium 232, but it requires borax. You can obtain borax by mining salt veins (as a byproduct), from bees, or through CropsNH.

The second path is a six-step processing chain that requires Chemical Reactors, a Centrifuge, and an EBF. Although it is longer, it offers a much better conversion ratio (75%, rather than 25% in the Chemical Plant). Instead of borax, it requires 100 L of fluorine per dust; the nitric acid can be fully recycled, so this path scales better than the borax route.

title: Tier 6 - LuV > Fetching Cubic Zirconia

Quest: Fetching Cubic Zirconia
Quest line: Tier 6 - LuV

For Cubic Zirconia, you'll need to combine Zirconium and Yttrium Oxide in the EBF as well. Fortunately you only need the dusts.

You can get Zirconium from:
1) The Red Zircon ore on Ross128b <- Do this one
2) Sifting Cassiterite, Tin, or Ilmenite <- Do this one if you hate Ross

Oxygen isn't hard to get, but the Yttrium more than makes up for it. You have a couple options:
1) Make Rare Earth (I) out of Rare Earth (see the MV quest)
2) Make Rare Earth (II) out of Rare Earth using a stronger acid and get it from Yttriaite
3) When you have a T6 rocket, you can pick some Yttrium ore up from Triton, making you cry at how much easier it is
4) In ZPM you can try going to the Toxic Everglades to grab weird GT++ ores, some of which have Yttrium in them (Yay RNG ore worldgen!)
5) Process Almandine Ore (found in Twilight Forest) in an Isamill Grinder & Flotation Cell for the froth, then set in a Vacuum Furnace.

To get Rare Earth you can use Redstone or Skystone, but you can also get it out of Monazite directly or some other ores as a byproduct. Hopefully you saved it up?

Quest line: Tier 6 - LuV

Place one on a tank and open the GUI.
Channel: Covers with the same text will connect.

Public: Links to any of the same color not set to private. Use an internet program to find out what the numbers mean, and get colors you like.
Private: Does not link to public version of that color. Meaningless in SP.

Export: Fluid moves from Attached Block -> Cover Network
Import: Fluid moves from Cover Network -> Attached Block

You can use multiple as inputs and/or outputs. It runs at 8000L/t.

You can send from an output hatch or to an input hatch for multis. Probably won't work well for anything with multiple I/O, like a singleblock Chemical Reactor.

Quest: Fusion Rocketry
Quest line: Tier 6 - LuV

So you completed your Fusion Reactor and made your rocket, great! Now time to get some new ore! (like that isn't getting old) You don't need your hand held anymore, so I'll just list what's new.

Enceladus, Miranda, Oberon, Ross128ba and Titan are the new planets. Miranda is the 1st moon of Uranus, while Oberon is the last. Enceladus is the 2nd moon of Saturn, while Titan is the second last. Ross128ba is Ross128b's moon in the Ross128 System to the South.

The new veins are Nickel, Tungsten, and Vanadium. The ores are: Chrome, Deep Iron, Iridium, Gold, Magnetite, Nickel, Osmium, Silicon, Shadow Iron, Tungsten, and Vanadium.

You can get Neutronium from small ores on Enceladus, Oberon, and Titan.

And grab some planet blocks while you're at it too.

You can get the schematic for T6 on Enceladus.

I'm sure you can tell by now, but it's not like every planet is required, so go to the ones you want to, and skip the ones you don't want to go to. Use NEI to figure out where you NEED to go.

title: Tier 6 - LuV > Mutating Things is Cool

Quest: Mutating Things is Cool
Quest line: Tier 6 - LuV

When making Raw Crystal Chips, you have two other options if using Europium constantly is too expensive for you: Bacterial Sludge, and Mutagen.

Mutagen is obviously better than the sludge, but how do you get it? I'll teach you how.

First, get the Bacterial Sludge you got from Mars, and run it through a Brewery along with some U-238 to get Enriched Bacterial Sludge. Then Ferment it to get Fermented Bacterial Sludge. And finally you Distill it to get Mutagen.

But is a single bucket enough for you? Hardly! But now that we have some, we can make more with the vat. Use the Mutagen you got along with some of that Mysterious Crystal Dust to make a culture. Unfortunately the chances are pretty low, so you'll almost certainly have to do it several times.

Once you have your culture you can use it in the vat along with some of the dust again to make more. You'll need LuV-tier glass, and Plutonium rods.

If you want to get more Bacterial Sludge more easily, you can use the vat to make that too! The culture is much easier to make.

Mutagen is also used for Gendustry, so if you want to do that, make a bunch.

title: Tier 6 - LuV > Starting Fusion
text:
Quest: Starting Fusion
Quest line: Tier 6 - LuV

Nuclear fusion is the next major step in your progression, and to accomplish it you will need a Fusion Reactor Mark I. You will unlock new materials across the next few tiers with fusion, making this a required multiblock. Europium is what you will need first to make it to ZPM.

At the same time, fusion can generate power for you, primarily via Helium Plasma in this first tier. The speed of the reactor can make for significant EU/t, but actually consuming this plasma fast enough at this early stage is difficult. You will have Large Plasma Turbines, which can use a 4A Dynamo Hatch. This might require a lot of spam compared to powergen setups you might be using, such as UCFE, vac nukes or other options. Later, you will unlock XL turbines and a fusion line for them. 

For your first reactor, you will need a controller, 1-16 fluid input hatches, 1-16 fluid output hatches, and 16 LuV+ energy hatches. Each energy hatch has an energy capacity of 10M EU and draws up to 2048 EU/t.

That means you can do any fusion recipe with a start cost of 160M EU or less, and takes 32768 EU/t or less. Using more fluid hatches means you need less fusion casings. While this doesn't matter as much for the mk1 reactor, this principle helps tremendously with the higher reactor tiers.

You'll notice that there is an option to create a Compact Fusion Reactor MKI instead of the normal size. This is available as an option for every tier of Fusion Reactor. They are not required by any means, but they are demonstrably quicker if you're willing to spend extra resources.

Tasks:
- Retrieve: Fusion Control Computer Mk-I; Compact Fusion Computer Mk-I
- Retrieve (optional): 108 × LuV Machine Casing; 32 × Superconducting Coil Block; 16 × LuV Energy Hatch
Rewards: choose one of: enhancedlootbags:lootbag:41; 4 × Electric Motor (LuV); 2 × Electric Pump (LuV); 2 × Conveyor Module (LuV); 2 × Electric Piston (LuV); 64 × gregtech:gt.blockmachines:2400; Coin "The Technician 1000"

title: Tier 7 - ZPM > Configuring TecTech Multiblocks
text:
Quest: Configuring TecTech Multiblocks
Quest line: Tier 7 - ZPM

Many TecTech multis can be customized by adjusting certain internal numbers called parameters. You can directly adjust them in the GUI.

If there are lit up sections in the parameters part of the multi interface (see the TecTech Multiblocks quest), you can configure the multi, otherwise there is nothing to do.

We'll be using the Quantum Computer as our example, since that is what you probably want it for.

First we need to understand the parameter naming, like ID:0:1:I. The first number represents the parameter block. For the QC only block 0 is used. Each such block can have up to 4 used parameters, 2 inputs and 2 outputs. The letter at the end specifies if a parameter is an input or output with I or O and the number in the middle distinguishes the 2 parameters of this kind in the block. It is either 0 or 1.

Inputs are something that is either set or is a default. Outputs give information that the machine sends to you, that indicates things. (like heat or Computation)

And lastly, the Parametrizer Memory Card lets you copy settings from one machine to another easily.

Tasks:

You will need a Maintenance Hatch and at least an EV Energy Hatch, though the power requirements can be much higher if you use many Data Access Hatches and Data Bank Master Connectors, for now you should start with an LuV energy hatch. Trying to run the Data Bank and then scanning the controller will tell you how much EU/t is needed.

You will need more blocks than what is asked for in this quest, as the number of Data Access Hatches and Connectors is up to you. You can have a maximum of 15 combined.

The Assembly Line Reception Connector replaces your old Data Access Hatch on the Assembly Line. Connect it to a Master Connector on the Data Bank with Optical Fiber Cable and make sure to color the hatches and the cable.

If you can't figure out what blocks to place, pay attention to the tooltip in the bottom-left when using the Multiblock Structure Hologram Projector. In this case the filler blocks are Computer Casing.

They're also so powerful that only a few machines support them outside of the ever wonderful TecTech: LSC, MBF, EnF, and PSS. Remember to paint the Laser Vacuum Pipes, the Source Hatch, and the Target Hatch. Also, Source = Output, Target = Input. Laser Vacuum Pipes do not split or bend. To turn your laser, use an Active Transformer. Later on, you can use a Laser Vacuum Mirror to bend your Laser Vacuum Pipes; this will not allow splitting.

Laser hatches can have their operational amperage adjusted in their GUI.

Be careful with using very high amp hatches as every Laser Hatch has 1EU/s * max amps passive power loss. For example, a 256A Laser Source Hatch and 256A Laser Target Hatch will both lose 256 EU/s regardless of the amount of power flowing through.

Control buttons - Buttons might change their behavior and appearance depending on machine but usually they work like this, starting from top:

3) Power Pass - Toggles Power Pass.

title: Tier 7 - ZPM > Wormhole Generator
text:
Quest: Wormhole Generator
Quest line: Tier 7 - ZPM

The Miniature Wormhole Generator uses Quantum Entangled Singularities to transmit power over any distance, including across dimensions.

To use it, you must link two generators together using AE2 Entangled Singularities by placing one in each controller. Once linked, both wormholes must be started by placing a full (non-entangled) AE2 Singularity into an input bus on each machine. The wormhole will continue running as long as power is being transferred between them. If power transfer stops, the link will shut down and must be restarted using another Singularity on both ends.

Power is transferred through Laser Source Hatches and Laser Target Hatches. Each wormhole can support up to 4 laser hatches. These must be placed in the center block of one of the side faces, excluding the controller side. Hatch pairs link based on relative position between the two wormholes, not cardinal direction. For example, a Source Hatch placed on the top of the sending side must connect to a Target Hatch placed on the bottom of the receiving wormhole.

Additionally, unlike AE2 P2P tunnels, this does not come with a 5% power loss but rather a much more manageable 0.5% loss. 

The glass and input hatch must be tiered accordingly with the tier of the laser hatches. But remember, there is no amperage limit on this machine, so use whatever makes it cheapest for you.

Like the previous recipe, NEI doesn't show it correctly (they should be around the same page in NEI, they both also appear to produce Sterilized Petri Dishes, (even if that's not true) and both use unique Modules).

In order to make this, you'll need to make the Rotten Flesh Bacteria culture, get the DNA Sample, and then get the Data Orb. It changes its name to beta-Lactamase, that's normal.

Then, do the same thing for Common Yeast (get the right Yeast!).

Then you need to use the recipe to combine the information from the Data Orbs and get the Common Yeast Plasmid from that.

Lastly, use the Rotten Flesh Bacteria culture, the Common Yeast Plasmid, Penicillin (make it by centrifuging Common Yeast Fluid), and Distilled Water. You want the Transformation Module for this. It's a 100% chance.

You'll want to use the normal recipe to make more cultures, since it also becomes beta-Lactamase once you turn it into a DNA Sample.

title: Tier 8 - UV > Quantum Computer
text:
Quest: Quantum Computer
Quest line: Tier 8 - UV

The Quantum Computer (QC) is an incredibly complicated machine used to generate computation for the Research Station and a few other multiblocks. There are a few things you need to understand before using one.

CONSTRUCTION. Much like an assembly line, the QC is built as a series of slices. The first and last slice are the only valid locations for hatches. The slices in between are primarily for computer racks. The Multiblock Structure Hologram Projector shows the minimum length QC, but holding multiple in a single stack will show/build longer versions up to the maximum length of 16. There is also a mandatory air block in front of the computer heat vents.

OUTPUT. Computation is nothing more than an integer input for certain recipes--much like EU. There may exist a minimum throughput requirement, a threshold to reach, or both (NEI will tell you everything). Computation is generated every second by the QC, transmitted by an Optical Transmission Connector, received by an Optical Reception Connector, and "consumed" by the machine or process that needs it. There is no storing computation and there can only be ONE transmission or reception hatch connected to the same Optical Fiber Cables at a time. If absolutely necessary, the Network Switch with QoS can split/join connections but know that it takes both power and maintenance to run.

Additional QC can be chained together using another set of Optical Transmission and Optical Reception Connectors between machines, but they cannot wallshare the same Optical Transmission Connector.

UNCERTAINTY. The QC has a unique maintenance requirement that can only be corrected by balancing the Schrödinger Matrix inside an Uncertainty Resolver- an additional hatch that must go on either the first or last slice of the machine. Start with the Uncertainty Resolver X, but know that there is another tier unlocked later on (Uncertainty Resolution) that will solve the puzzle on its own.

The interface of the Uncertainty Resolver X has the Schrödinger Matrix in the middle and two sets of 8 buttons on the left and right. Clicking on one button and then another will switch the states of the two corresponding cells in the matrix. This means switching their shade/color. The goal of the puzzle is to balance the states of the matrix around the glowing LED lights, turning all of them green.

PARAMETERS. In the GUI of the controller, there are two configurable parameters, overclock and overvolt, that change how computation and heat are generated. Higher overclock values contribute the most to computation and higher overvolt values contribute the most to heat. Alone, this would encourage the player to make overclock as high as possible and overvolt as low as possible, but there is a penalty to computation for large differences between these two parameters. Furthermore, overvolt values <1 will cause the QC to randomly drop computation proportional to its distance from 1. It is highly encouraged to play around with these parameters, as all the best setups do.

See the adjacent quest for more information on computer racks and generating computation.

Tasks:
- Retrieve (optional): 6 × Computer Heat Vent; 17 × Computer Casing; 10 × Advanced Computer Casing; 2 × Computer Rack

title: Tier 8 - UV > Quantum Mechanics is Hot
text:
Quest: Quantum Mechanics is Hot
Quest line: Tier 8 - UV

The QC has 2-24 computer racks depending on the length of the machine. Each rack has four total slots for either circuits (to generate heat and computation) or vents (to dissipate heat). Although conceptually similar to a nuclear reactor, the location of the components inside does not matter at all. Every rack is also completely independent from every other rack which means it is not possible to have one rack with all circuits and another with all vents.

The computation of a rack is the sum of all the components' individual computation. For example, two APU (Tier 3) and two Cooling Cores have 240 + 240 + 0 + 0 = 480 base computation per second. However, computation changes significantly depending on the values for overclock and overvolt:

Computation = Base * (1+overclock^2) / (1+(overclock-overvolt)^2)

The heat of a rack is a value between 0 and 10,000 and is reported in the interface of the QC or by using a Portable Scanner on the rack. Every component has a certain heat limit which if exceeded will void that component. Breaking or wrenching a rack while it is hot (>2000) will similarly void the components inside. The QC will explode if the heat exceeds 10,000 but no component has a heat limit greater than that, so don't worry too much about ruining your base.

Heat α HeatConstant * overclock * overvolt^2

The power consumption of a rack is 1A ZPM regardless of the components inside. This is in addition to the 1A ZPM of the QC itself. However, these EU/t values are directly proportional to overclock and overvolt which should increase as you unlock better circuits. Be sure to turn on the QC before the research station and only when you need it.

EU/t = 131,072 * overclock * overvolt * (racks + 1)

To get you started, craft 4x APU (Tier 3) and 4x Cooling Cores. Place two of each component in the two racks and the QC will safely produce 1,920 computation/s for just 393,215 EU/t (0.75A UV) which is more than enough for researching the Wetware Mainframe. If you would like to further increase the computation/s at the cost of power, adjust the overclock and overvolt values to 1.44 and 1.03, respectively. This will generate 2,526 computation/s at a cost of 583,217 EU/t (1.11A UV).

If the APUs are too bothersome to craft, try Crystal Mainframes instead but you will need different overclock and overvolt values to get the most out of them. That goes for every unique combination of circuits and vents.

title: Tier 8 - UV > Space Elevator
text:
Quest: Space Elevator
Quest line: Tier 8 - UV

The Space Elevator is a modular structure. It can be equipped with Space Elevator modules, which then can take on different tasks.

Initially, your Space Elevator has 6 module slots that can be used. You can later upgrade that to up to 12 with Mk-II and Mk-III motors. The motor tier also determines the module tier that you can use. The I/O is not shared between modules, each module only sees their own I/O slots. Energy is only provided to the central structure of the Space Elevator and then automatically distributed to all modules.

After a module has been inserted and supplied with the right I/O, it can be configured further using parameters.

You can see in NEI which fluids are pumpable with the Space Pumping Module. It consumes 1A UHV to work. The Gas Type and Planet Type are parameters.

NEI also has an overview of all the ores you can obtain with a Space Mining Module. It needs to be supplied with a drone, which will act as catalyst, a set of input items, computation and either Helium, Bismuth or Radon plasma. The plasma will boost both the recipe time and the amount of bonus stacks you get out of a recipe. With its parameters you can adjust parallels, overdrive, and distance. When multiple recipes have the same input and you have the distance set to a value that they share, the module will pick a random one, taking the recipes weights into consideration.

The space elevator also lets you travel to other planets, but it doesn't get you back though so better keep that in mind!

The mining module also got a cycle mode. In static mode it will hold its distance while in cycle mode it will change its distance after each recipe check (and you can configure the range and step size of that).

Teleportation can be accessed though the controller.

title: Tier 9 - UHV > A Blast to the Past
text:
Quest: A Blast to the Past
Quest line: Tier 9 - UHV

Now that you have the bioware mainframe, you have unlocked the first of the stargate trophies!
Yes, there's multiple of them, one for each major iteration of the stargate recipe.
These trophies are just that, trophies, and you can try to craft them if you want to compare the costs to today's stargate standards.
To complete these quests you have to submit two stargates' worth of materials.

Now, let me bestow upon you a short history lesson about this point in GT:NHs past.

The year is 2020. The bio mainframe was pretty much the end of GTNH progression at the time, not much above UHV existed or was craftable. This was also the point in the pack where you'd start scaling for stargate, as that too was tiered at UHV. Technically UEV parts were craftable, but their only uses were singleblocks for PAs (which only held up to 16 UEV machines) and the Deep Dark Portal. UEV-UMV energy hatches were craftable, but their recipes were simple hull + wire crafting table recipes
...and that was about it for UHV+ content.
With the recent addition of void miners, the previously thought to be impossible started to seem actually attainable, a set of stargates. Specifically, to craft a set of them, not just find them like others have before.

One group in particular, known as the Gigaplex, gave it their all and actually managed to do it, to prove that crafting stargates is possible with enough determination.

Thus, on the 16th of February, 2021, the first set of crafted stargates had been born.

P.S.: If you want to be as faithful to the challenge as possible, try completing this quest without using any of the modern functionality that didn't exist back then.
Here's a non-exhaustive list of major things that didn't exist (in no particular order):
-PCB Factory, Space Elevator, Component Assemblyline, AAL, PrAss, EEC, EIG, Compact Fusions, MCR, MABS
-Any bee related GT machines
-Any UEV or above multis
-XL Turbines, Naq fuel, LEG
-Sub 1-tick OC, Batch Mode, inbuilt Void Protection on multis
-Level Maintainer, AE Fluid Crafting, Stocking Buses/Hatches, Crafting Input Buses, ME Output Buses/Hatches, non-recursive AE component recipes
-Shift-clicking recipes into AE patterns (pain)
-Early-Midgame QoL such as ghost circuits, visual prospecting, reprogramming circuits with a screwdriver, seeing Assline recipes in NEI before having crafted them, and more

P.P.S: This quest is missing the chaotic capacitors on purpose, because the chaotic core recipe requires spacetime now, but the chaotic capacitor recipe did not change at all since then. All in all the cost for these banks was completely negligible back then and still is today, they only serve as a magic gate for SG.

title: Tier 9 - UHV > Soldering's Not Working Anymore
text:
Quest: Soldering's Not Working Anymore
Quest line: Tier 9 - UHV

After all these advancements, it looks like some things just aren't meant to be. Every machine that your Assembly Line has crafted works, but the most advanced ones so far seem to be... a bit rough around the edges. Further inspection revealed that Indalloy just isn't good enough. It seems that Infinity's neverending vibrations destabilize the joints where the soldering happens, your living circuits have been offering resistance to this crude soldering alloy, however that happens...

It's likely that new materials will completely break Indalloy's ability to get pieces soldered together. Because of that, it's about time for a new development in this technology, and the previous rejection by your living circuits has given you an excellent idea. Any new material can have some new behavior that will ruin assembling for you, but what if the solder itself learns about these complications and learns how to adjust to them, mutating for them?

That's right: Mutated Living Solder.

This sort of chemistry is only possible in a full-scale Chemical Plant, equipped with the most advanced casing: Botmium. On top of that, the catalyst you need to use has been consumed so thoroughly that you were forced to use Infinity for it, on top of the mutating Naquadria. Your Infinity will be lost to the crafting, still, unless you manage to put Tungstensteel Pipe Casings and Awakened Draconium Coils in your Chemical Plant, which prevent the catalyst from losing durability. Any better coils also have the same effect.

The new solder itself is a different story. Wetware technology is too primitive for this, and your Bio Cells have refused to bond with any fluid that would serve as its carrier for soldering. When you tried a mixture of hot Tin and Bismuth, it finally worked, but the soldering didn't actually work. It looked like the Bio Cells hadn't learned how to fulfill their new job, which could be fixed by adding an example material as a test subject, something simpler like Infinity Catalyst... but it seemed impossible to bond the cells to the dust. You need more energy... not just loads of EU, something concentrated, hot, fizzling with energy!

Yes, everything alive died instantly when you decided to add plasmas instead of hot fluids. No surprise there. However, Bio Cells did survive inside hot fluids, so we just need some temperature control here, and some separation between cell and plasma... yes, Gravi Stars can be used for this. We still need to cool down the plasmas, so that the enhanced cells can mix with them in liquid form, and EU alone would be too expensive. Gelid Cryotheum has proven to be surprisingly efficient, perhaps due to its origins, as a component of a living being, the Blizz.

There we go! The Mutated Living Solder is now complete. The highly intelligent Bio Cells are energized by the concentrated heat of the plasmas, while keeping a distance from them due to the Gravi Stars' influence, and they analyze the Infinity Catalyst Dust to learn about material instability. This is a very slow process, but it happens at the same time as the plasmas are slowly cooled, using Cryotheum and EU, until the learning process is complete and the Bio Cells fall into the Tin and Bismuth, now in the liquid form that was shown to work before. Finally, armed with their new knowledge, the cells flow through the Naquadria-based, Infinity-reinforced catalyst so that they can mutate in real-time after researching the material they're soldering.

This should work for any future soldering need, regardless of material. Let's hope so, at least...

title: Tips and Tricks > Automating Power On/Off
text:
Quest: Automating Power On/Off
Quest line: Tips and Tricks

Once you have a GT boiler or Large Combustion Engine with a long startup time, you may wish to automate turning it on/off to save fuel, since extra power or Steam will just be voided. Additionally, the bigger your Steam/EU buffer is, the less time your generators will spend heating up, which makes them more efficient.

Use a Machine Controller Cover on the controller for that. You can put it on top, bottom, or sides next to a casing - casings will transmit the redstone signal. You can use a Soldering Iron and Fine Soldering Alloy Wire to set the Redstone Output of a controller block to strong. When set to Strong it can go through a casing, but not hatches, buses, or other blocks. Use it with an activity detector if you want to receive a signal from the controller rather than turning it on/off with one.

With a Machine Controller Cover, you can use redstone to turn the machine on and off. This is handy if you don't want to use a Soft Hammer to disable a machine yourself constantly.

The best way to do that is with an RS latch. One input will turn the machine on, and one input will turn the machine off. Use a comparator attached to a valve to measure the steam level in your multiblock Iron or Steel Tank. Invert the signal to turn on your boiler when the steam level is low. When the steam level signal is high, turn your boiler off. Use a trail of redstone to lower the signal strength. Because of boiler/turbine warmup, try to set the ON strength to 30 percent of capacity and OFF strength to about 90 percent.

Red alloy wire will hold a redstone signal for a longer distance than normal redstone, while redstone conduits will go indefinitely. You can also use amplified redcrystal to improve the strength of the signal for a long distance, repeating as necessary.

You can use an Energy Detector Cover in Normal Electrical Storage (including batteries) mode to monitor the power in a battery buffer and use it to enable/disable generators in a similar way. Change mode using a screwdriver. If you use a dense redcrystal, it will only allow signal through at a certain level, perfect for automating this kind of thing.

For a video version, check out this video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jPfnifJEO64

Applying it is easy: use a vanilla anvil, just like any other enchantment.

PS: Put soulbound on your backpack itself - the backpack and everything inside it stays with you on death.

title: Tips and Tricks > Covering Up
text:
Quest: Covering Up
Quest line: Tips and Tricks

This quest goes over all of the covers, just in case you forgot or they weren't mentioned. If they have their own quest, look at it for more info. You can put them on basically any GT block, pipe, machine, tank, etc. Though that doesn't consider whether it will work right or be useful. Shift-right-click will open a GUI for many of them. For covers that you can adjust the amount of, clicking the left side with a screwdriver goes down, and right goes up. All covers block rain on the side they're attached to. Generally you can adjust covers with a screwdriver, whether they have a GUI or not. You can remove them with a crowbar if you forgot.

Fluid-Related Covers:
Pump: Transfers fluids at the speed specified on the tooltip.

Fluid Regulator: Regulates the rate that fluid can go through it, as well as pumping it. Can work x/s or x/t.

Steam Valve: Moves more, but is only for steam. Only goes to IV. Does not work on SH steam.

Overflow: Voids anything over the specified amount in the tank.

Fluid Detector: Will emit a redstone signal (RS) based on fluid fill rate of the tank it's on. By default, empty=15, full=0. Use inverted mode to swap. Useful on tanks and hatches.

Ender Fluid Link: Cover version of ender tanks to TP fluid around. Doesn't connect to ender tanks though.

Drain Module: Protects from rain on that side, and will fill the tank with water from rain if it can. Useless.

Fluid Filter: Filters fluid going through it. Click with a cell to set it.

Shutter: Blocks items/fluids when active. Use it with a machine controller and RS. Does not visually disconnect/block. You place it between the pipes, and put the MC on the same pipe.

Item-Related Covers:
Conveyor: Sends items. Use an item pipe in import mode or on a GT block/machine.

Robot Arm: Sends from a specific slot in the machine it's on (internal) to another specific slot in a block next to it (adjacent). Keep going through numbers until you get it right, it seems to change per machine. If the output slot is full, it won't output. There needs to be a valid block with slots to send to, or the settings won't save.

Item Detector: Will emit RS based on item fill rate of the block it's on. By default, empty=0, full=15. Detects by filled slots, so doesn't work right with the super/quantum chests. Probably better for buses.

Filtered Conveyor: Filters up to one type of item (whitelist/blacklist) and acts as a conveyor module. Locked to either export or import.

EU-Related Covers:
Energy Detector: Will emit RS based on EU fill rate of the batbuff/tank it's on. By default, empty=0, full=15. Make sure to set it to include batteries. Can also detect steam for some reason.

Power Pass Upgrade: Read the tooltip, then ask Bart how it works, he didn't bother telling anyone. He'll probably just tell you the code is the best documentation, just like the Tectech guys. May not actually be finished/work, either.

Tesla Coil/Tesla Coil Rich Edition: Use with the Tesla Tower to send EU wirelessly or something.

Other Covers:
Player Detector: Detects players. About 10 block range. Currently owner/other is inverted on non-pipes due to some bug or another.

Activity Detector: Detects either recipe progress or idleness. 0%=0 RS, ~95%=14 by default. In idle mode, idleness is 15, and is 0 when running by default.

Machine Controller: Turns machine on/off based on RS. Disable machine will keep it off regardless of RS state. Safe Mode only works on MBs. If a MB runs out of power, it will normally turn off, but a MC will turn it back on, continuing to void stuff. This will set it to the disable machine state instead. You will also get a notification. Safe mode is currently broken?

Needs Maintenance: Emits RS if it meets the condition specified. Rotor=turbine?

Redstone Transmitter/Receiver (In/Out): OK, these things are confusing, so listen closely. First, set a frequency, either by using the GUI, or using the original way: right-clicking it with an item. Empty hand = 0, other items = their item ID. Be careful not to reset it to 0 by accident. Honestly, just use the GUI. You can set it to private or not, it's the same kind of thing as EnderStorage, so you don't blare RS across the server. Channel state = RS level.

RT(O) sets the channel state based on the redstone level sent from outside to the specific side. You can TP an RS from this to the RR(O).
RT(I) sets the channel state based on redstone level that would be emitted from the machine itself. Always sends 15, so it's useless.
RR(O) outputs redstone level based on channel state. You can TP RS from the RT(O) to here.
RR(I) controls whether a machine can work based on channel state, just like a machine controller cover does. If it has 0 RS, it stays off. At least 1, and it turns on. You send the signal from elsewhere with the RT(O).
RR(I) can also be used in conjunction with other covers whose states talk about conditional.

IC2 Heat vents: Speeds up machines a tiny amount? Also looks neat. TODO: someone please look at the code to see what it actually does.

Crafting Table: Adds a crafting table to the block you can use. Mostly cosmetic.

Planks/Plates/Foils: Blocks I/O on that side. Use a screwdriver to set allowed types of stuff through. Blocks everything by default. Set the output to another side first to avoid changing its settings too. You'll probably 'use' this by accident at least once.

Computer Monitor: Adds a visual look. Cosmetic-only cover.

Lens: Cosmetic-only cover.

You can also use AE2 facades as cosmetic covers.

title: Tips and Tricks > Lootbag Uptiering
text:
Quest: Lootbag Uptiering
Quest line: Tips and Tricks

In GTNH, the lootbags are quite useful tools for boosting your resources. There are a wide variety of lootbag types, and those types all have upgrade paths to get better resources.

There are two paths you can take when it comes to upgrading your lootbags, you can either enchant it with fortune, or you can upgrade the bag itself. Enchanting the lootbag with fortune will increase the chances of more rare drops being given to you on opening, while upgrading the bag itself will change the item pool to that of the upgraded bag. Notably, if you uptier the bag itself, it will cost 3 of the previous bag tier, so make sure it's worthwhile to upgrade before you do so!

If you're looking to maximize your advantage it's recommended you both uptier your lootbag AND apply the fortune upgrade. 

Be sure to use NEI to see all of this information. Use 'U' on your lootbag and you will be able to see the potential drops, the drop chances based on fortune levels, and you will be able to see recipes for uptiering the bag.

title: ...Without Dying > Modular Meddling
text:
Quest: Modular Meddling
Quest line: ...Without Dying

Interested in powerful, customizable armor that you can modify as you advance? Look no further than &z&zMechanical Armor!

In order to begin tinkering, you'll need a workspace for modifying modular equipment along with a set of Mechanical Armor. The armor is essentially useless on its own, but gains additional features through modification. Each piece of armor is composed of three parts:

Augments: Augments add a wide variety of useful features to the armor. Augments are categorized into one of three types: Protection, Movement, and Utility. Augments can only be inserted into slots corresponding to their category.

Frames: The armor's frame determines the protection value of the armor along with how many slots it contains for augments.

Energy Cores: The energy core determines how much energy the armor stores, its charging tier, and which augments can be equipped.

title: Working with Oil > Acetone and Ethenone
text:
Quest: Acetone and Ethenone
Quest line: Working with Oil

Another ingredient in the making of TNM is Ethenone, which can be made directly from Acetone. This one is a little more organic, which is to say it's much easier to automate if you chose Benzene or Biomass. From those routes, you can get it from a Wood Vinegar DT, or reacting Acetic Acid with Calcite Dust from a Fermented Biomass DT (get the calcite from electrolyzing Fertilizer). If you used biomass to get Ammonia, you can do it this way.

If not using plants, though, there are other ways to automate this. Ethenone can be made directly from Acetic Acid and Sulfuric Acid, and this last one should already be automated from cleaning the sulfuric waste from the oil fractions. Acetic Acid, on the other hand, is a mix of Oxygen and Ethylene, a combo that you might have already automated to make Polyethylene. If not, this is a good time to do so.

The amount of Ethenone you need to make a lot of Cetane-Boosted Diesel is small, so it's unlikely that you'll run out of Sulfuric Acid for this. Make sure you automate it all, though.

Tasks:

Rewards: 32 × IC2:itemCellEmpty; Coin "The Chemist 100"
Prerequisites: Boosting the Diesel
Unlocks: Tetranitromethane as Additive

title: Working with Oil > Ammonia Source
text:
Quest: Ammonia Source
Quest line: Working with Oil

One of the components of Tetranitromethane is Nitric Acid, which is made from Nitrogen Dioxide, and this from Nitrogen Oxide, which is ultimately created from Ammonia. You can do a small Chemical Reactor chain to do this line of recipes, but the better option is to make an LCR and use the circuit 24 recipe to turn Ammonia and Oxygen directly into Nitric Acid.

You'll still need to automate Ammonia, though, and there are two main ways of doing this. One of the options is to create it directly from Nitrogen and Hydrogen, but this recipe consumes a lot of EU. The other option is to switch to the biological side of things and get it from the DT recipe of Fermented Biomass, but this requires a whole other setup with sapling automation, a Pyrolyse Oven and some other machines, so don't do it unless you're interested in getting the other outputs of that recipe. It, however, might be a good option if you don't have those yet. Either way, automate your Ammonia.

title: Working with Oil > Basic Cracking
text:
Quest: Basic Cracking
Quest line: Working with Oil

Despite what the Distillery recipe might have led you to believe, there are many more fractions of Oil than the four you could choose from. However, to get the rest of the oil byproducts, you need to split these four into the others, a process known as cracking. To crack the fuels, they must not be sulfuric, and you will need either Hydrogen (hydro-cracking) or Steam (steam-cracking) to successfully crack. Your Hydrogen source for desulfurizing is hopefully good enough to sustain hydro-cracking, and the Steam you were previously using for power can now be useful to get more out of the Oil you're pumping.

Heavy Fuel, Light Fuel, Refinery Gas and Naphtha can each be cracked both ways, and with three different intensities: lightly, moderately or severely cracked. This means that each portion has 6 different cracking options, and the products of distilling them can be cracked once more! There are a lot of options here, but a few of them stand out for their usefulness.

The first one you should try is Refinery Gas. In order to make that, you will need to desulfurize Sulfuric Gas, so make some of that in your Distillery. Currently, you can only crack through the Chemical Reactor, so once you have the Refinery Gas grab some steam and get cracking.

*Hint* You should start by making some Severely-Cracked Refinery Gas

Make x5 as many cells if you don't want to waste anything.

Tasks:
- Retrieve (optional): 10 × Sulfuric Gas Cell
- Retrieve (optional): Basic Chemical Reactor
- Retrieve (optional): 10 × Refinery Gas Cell; 10 × gregtech:gt.metaitem.98
- Retrieve: 8 × gregtech:gt.metaitem.99:15735
Rewards: choose one of: enhancedlootbags:lootbag:4; Conveyor Module (LV); 5 × Coin "The Chemist 10"

title: Working with Oil > Boiler and Super Fuel
text:
Quest: Boiler and Super Fuel
Quest line: Working with Oil

With the advancements in building materials you've made until now, a new kind of generator has been unlocked. The Large Boilers you might have looked at before, and perhaps used, change when you reach Titanium, and if you build one of those, you will get something quite different from the tiers before.

To start, most burnable items don't work here. These advanced boilers need to burn much hotter, and as such they only accept specific fuels. The fuel of interest here is one of two, who are built in a sort of chain, in a similar fashion as to how Diesel and CBD worked. There is Solid Super Fuel, and Magic Solid Super Fuel, and they are both created from some coal-like block, some binder and some liquid fuel. You can use CBD for this, but Heavy Fuel and LPG are also options.

Why go through this route, though? The answer is that this extra processing, although it is difficult to automate, creates fuel that is much more efficient than the fuels that were put into it, and this is because the advanced Large Boilers are slow burners that output Superheated Steam, instead of regular one. This also means that they will need two turbines to convert all the steam into EU, and even more if the amount produced is too much for them. If fuel efficiency is something you're looking for, you can tackle this challenge and further process your CBD into something even more powerful.

Tasks:

Rewards: choose one of: enhancedlootbags:lootbag:7; 6 × gregtech:gt.blockmachines:5152; 20 × Coin "The Technician 100"

Unlocks: Magic Super Fuel

title: Working with Oil > Boosting the Diesel

Quest: Boosting the Diesel

As you might have guessed, extra byproducts are not the only thing that HV does with Oil. On top of that, you can further improve the main fuel that you use for power, and this builds on the previous tier, as Diesel did from Light Fuel. As before, you will need to mix the fuel you have with something else to improve it, but it is not a direct byproduct this time. Instead, it's a chemical that requires a complicated processing chain to produce, at a much higher EU cost, with only a tiny amount needed to create the next fuel, Cetane-Boosted Diesel.

To make this additive, Tetranitromethane (TNM), you will need to source several chemicals you might have not used yet. I hope you have some Distillation Towers handy, because they will be very useful for this.

title: Working with Oil > Desulfurizing
text:
Quest: Desulfurizing
Quest line: Working with Oil

After distillation, the fluid you got still isn't that good. It can be used for power, but it's almost as bad as Oil itself unless you remove the sulfuric content it has. This applies for all the portions that can be distilled from Oil, and as such it's a required step regardless of which one you're working with.

To get clean Light Fuel, the sulfur needs to be drawn out with something that reacts with it, in a Chemical Reactor. What you need is Hydrogen, a relatively common gas that can be electrolyzed from water, or from specific ores (check NEI for all the possible sources). After reacting, you will get Hydrogen Sulfide and the clean Light Fuel, which can be further processed or burned for power at this stage.

title: Working with Oil > Diesel
text:
Quest: Diesel
Quest line: Working with Oil

Finally, the oil of the gods. At least, early gods.

Diesel, as a power source, has widely been known as the optimal choice all the way up to EV, when you unlock the ability to make nukes. It can be further upgraded into Cetane-Boosted Diesel in HV, by adding another chemical chain to it, but a fuel value of 480k EU on a fuel that needs so few machines to be made is quite exceptional. It should be automated as soon as possible, to ensure that you won't run out of power when you need it the most.

At this stage, you can use either LV or MV Combustion Generators. Using the LV ones will mean you need to make more of them, and more pollution, but they have 95% fuel efficiency compared to MV's 90%. It's a difference, but an automated Diesel setup is unlikely to be affected by a 5% change in efficiency.

As you progress, fuel will become more and more power-dense, but also need more steps automated. The next tier is much harder than this one, so get ready!

title: Working with Oil > Distillation Tower
text:
Quest: Distillation Tower
Quest line: Working with Oil

In HV, your oil processing options soar to new levels of complexity, and efficiency. Many of the processing multis that can be used are unlocked in this tier, and one of the most iconic is the Distillation Tower, the direct upgrade of the Distillery.

This tower can do actual fractional distillation, a process used in real life petrochemistry to separate oil into many different parts, based on their boiling points. The tall structure is required for the process, because the condensation of the vapors occurs in different temperatures. And since heating is only applied at the bottom, temperature drops the higher the vapor travels. This means that compounds with higher boiling points will condense sooner and will end up lower in the column, the opposite is also applicable for compounds with low boiling points.

That said, the Distillation Tower replaces Distilleries by allowing you to collect all fractions at once, from the same amount of input. This means that the tower is both more efficient, and also allows automation of all the outputs at the same time, but this comes at a cost: the controller needs EV circuits, which require a built Cleanroom, and the structure blocks are mostly made of Stainless Steel. Not only that, but the tower's height depends on the recipe, since each output needs its own height level to successfully be extracted. A max-height, 12-block tall DT can cost almost a dozen stacks of stainless to build, a very expensive multi for the tier.

Instead of doing that, the first DT you should build is a 5-block tall one, to distill the Oil you're pumping out of reservoirs. Doing this, you can get all the fractions at once, for a reasonably cheap multi, compared to its maximum size.

Prerequisites: Tier 3 (HV); Hello Baron, How's Your Black Gold Today?
Unlocks: Using All the Fractions

text:

You don't always have to crack the base fuels to get useful chemicals out of them. The best example of this is Heavy Fuel, whose recipe only has 3 outputs, but they're all excellent. This is the perfect format for a Distillation Tower automation, so get on it as soon as you can, you won't regret it!

As a sidenote, all of these are power-dense, and can be used for power if you stockpile a lot of them. Benzene is the first one you should use for this purpose, if you wish to do it, because the other two are core chemicals for required progression in HV and EV. However, Benzene can also turn into several useful chemicals, so don't burn it all for power.

title: Working with Oil > Early Ethylene
text:
Quest: Early Ethylene
Quest line: Working with Oil

In LV, cracking fuels is only possible in a Chemical Reactor, which has a lower efficiency than the Oil Cracker multiblock that is available at HV. That said, it is still a great source of some fluids, one of which being Ethylene, the precursor to Polyethylene, the first plastic that can be produced and a required part of progression in the pack. To obtain Ethylene from Oil, the best way to go is to severely steam-crack Refinery Gas.

Simply put the Refinery Gas and the Steam in a Chemical Reactor with the correct circuit (check NEI) and then distill the cracked Refinery Gas. It can give a lot of different outputs, so make sure you choose the right one. After doing this, you'll have successfully processed Oil, both for power and for byproducts. Congratulations!

After you unlock different types of oil from underground fluids at MV the best route to ethylene may change depending on what type of oil you will decide to extract.

title: Working with Oil > Extreme Combustion Engine
text:
Quest: Extreme Combustion Engine
Quest line: Working with Oil

Very similar to the LCE in most aspects, the Extreme Combustion Engine was created to close the gap between the diesels and more advanced forms of powergen, mainly nuclear fusion. However, the main thing they differ on is the fuel that they can run, and in this case you're limited to the powerful fuel from the last tier, High Octane Gasoline.

That's right, only this fuel will work, and in exchange the ECE will output more than 10k EU/t. If you add Liquid Oxygen, which you'll need 4 Vacuum Freezers for (3 at HV and 1 at EV), you can keep it boosted permanently, which will send it up to 4 IV amps of power and 150% fuel efficiency. It's in your best interest to keep this thing going if you want to keep using Oil fuels for power, and the only thing you can rely on is your automated HOG setup, which you might have to, and should improve with the new IV multis as soon as you can, unless you have other sources of power working simultaneously.

As a last note, there is also an IV equivalent of the Vacuum Freezer, if you want to tackle the Liquid Oxygen needs that way. It's more power efficient, look it up on the Mass Processing tab.
